repomix.files: This section contains the contents of the repository's files. 1: # MarkmapEditor Draw.io Report MVP Architecture 2: 3: **Status:** Locked architecture for the first thin Draw.io MVP 4: **Scope:** Thin MVP only 5: **Canonical source:** Reviewed Markdown Report 6: **Output:** One editable, uncompressed `.drawio` XML file generated from one user-selected template 7: 8: Current implementation: 9: 10: - ACT G (Quick Report + Report lifecycle): complete. 11: - H1 (Reviewed Markdown importer): complete (committed at `e738ec3`, registered via `js/app/script-loader.js`, runtime API `globalThis.MME_REPORT_MARKDOWN_IMPORT`, dormant validator passes 39/39 in Node). 12: - H2 (Draw.io reconciler): complete (committed at `f1a82b5`; XML declaration/BOM assessment compatibility added at `3ab7f65`; runtime API `globalThis.MME_DRAWIO_REPORT_RECONCILER`; validator passes 101/101 in Node with honest totals; accepts `<mxfile>`/`<mxGraphModel>` roots optionally preceded by a UTF-8 BOM, leading whitespace, and one standard XML declaration — assessment-view normalization only, original template and declaration-in-output preserved; compressed payloads still rejected as `template-compressed`). 13: - H3 (reconciliation UI): complete (committed at `a1c39dc`, refined through `3ab7f65`; runtime API `globalThis.MME_DRAWIO_REPORT_PANEL`, validator passes 38/38 in Node; runtime qualification, button availability, Report collapse, overlay open/Close, picker cancellation, no-template blocking, mobile open/Close, and session Close are browser-confirmed). Real-template desktop acceptance is pending. 14: - H4 (Draw.io flexible output delivery): complete (committed at `2c03960`; flexible partial generation, unused-field aggregation, and Android `application/octet-stream` picker compatibility at `3ab7f65`; validator-honesty and single-owner delivery logging cleanup at `4541709`; runtime APIs `globalThis.MME_DRAWIO_REPORT_PANEL.generateDrawioOutput` and `validateDrawioOutputDelivery`, output-delivery validator passes 107/107 in Node; browser-only acceptance — real Save As dialog, picker cancellation, download fallback, laptop end-to-end suite, generated-file opening in Draw.io, mobile reachability — is pending). The embedded Draw.io editor remains outside the thin MVP. 15: 16: --- 17: 18: ## 1. Product decision 19: 20: The Draw.io workflow must remain simple, transparent, portable, and manually recoverable. 21: 22: ```text 23: Workspace data 24: → Quick Report Markdown 25: → user reviews and edits Markdown 26: → Report Markdown importer 27: → field dictionary 28: → select one Draw.io template 29: → extract {{field name}} placeholders 30: → reconcile fields 31: → complete missing values in Markdown 32: → generate one .drawio output 33: ``` 34: 35: The reviewed Markdown Report is the source of truth. 36: 37: The Draw.io file is a generated artifact. Draw.io must never become the only location containing report information. 38: 39: If MarkmapEditor is unavailable, the user must still be able to: 40: 41: 1. open the Markdown Report in another editor; 42: 2. find a field such as `{{summary}}`; 43: 3. open the Draw.io template; 44: 4. find the same `{{summary}}` placeholder; 45: 5. copy the value manually. 46: 47: No user-facing translation layer is allowed. 48: 49: --- 50: 51: ## 2. Locked MVP rules 52: 53: 1. Use the exact same visible token syntax everywhere: 54: 55: ```text 56: {{field name}} 57: ``` 58: 59: 2. Field normalization may only: 60: 61: - trim whitespace inside braces; 62: - collapse repeated internal spaces; 63: - lowercase letters. 64: 65: 3. Field normalization must not: 66: 67: - translate languages; 68: - guess synonyms; 69: - convert visible spaces to underscores; 70: - remove unknown fields. 71: 72: 4. One reviewed Markdown Report is reconciled with one Draw.io template. 73: 74: 5. The first MVP accepts **uncompressed Draw.io XML only**. 75: 76: 6. The template remains unchanged. Generation creates a new output string/file. 77: 78: 7. Unknown or unresolved placeholders remain visible and are reported. 79: 80: 8. Missing values are maintained in Markdown under a stable section: 81: 82: ```md 83: ## Template Fields 84: 85: {{customer}}: 86: {{region}}: 87: {{ali summary}}: 88: ``` 89: 90: 9. No customer, owner, Project, Task, or Tag grouping is implemented in this MVP. 91: 92: 10. No embedded Draw.io editor is implemented in this MVP. 93: 94: --- 95: 96: ## 3. Why uncompressed Draw.io XML is required initially 97: 98: The `.drawio` document model is XML-based. Draw.io can expose and accept diagram XML, and uncompressed XML is inspectable and editable outside MarkmapEditor. 99: 100: For the first integration: 101: 102: ```text 103: Template requirement: 104: Uncompressed .drawio XML 105: ``` 106: 107: This keeps the implementation: 108: 109: - browser-native; 110: - dependency-free; 111: - diffable; 112: - manually repairable; 113: - compatible with ordinary text tools. 114: 115: Compressed Draw.io payload support is deferred until after the end-to-end MVP works. 116: 117: --- 118: 119: ## 4. Canonical field syntax 120: 121: ### Standard examples 122: 123: ```text 124: {{title}} 125: {{summary}} 126: {{highlights}} 127: {{risks}} 128: {{next steps}} 129: {{management notes}} 130: ``` 131: 132: ### Manual template-specific examples 133: 134: ```text 135: {{customer}} 136: {{region}} 137: {{ali summary}} 138: {{customer decision}} 139: {{regional risk}} 140: ``` 141: 142: ### Current automatic content 143: 144: Current Report sections such as Completed Tasks, Project Forecast, and Forecast Totals may be imported as section-derived fields. 145: 146: Conceptual keys: 147: 148: ```text 149: {{completed tasks}} 150: {{project forecast}} 151: {{forecast totals}} 152: ``` 153: 154: The first MVP may populate these as complete Markdown/text blocks. It does not split them automatically by customer or owner. 155: 156: --- 157: 158: ## 5. Reviewed Markdown import contract 159: 160: The Report Markdown importer produces a plain serializable projection. 161: 162: ```js 163: { 164: ok, 165: metadata, 166: title, 167: fields, 168: fieldOrder, 169: sections, 170: sourceMarkdown, 171: diagnostics 172: } 173: ``` 174: 175: ### Required import sources 176: 177: - leading Report frontmatter; 178: - first H1 title; 179: - known H2 sections; 180: - token-value lines such as `{{customer}}: Alibaba`; 181: - the `## Template Fields` section; 182: - unknown custom sections, preserved as section content where practical. 183: 184: ### Standard section mapping 185: 186: ```text 187: # Report title 188: → title 189: 190: ## Summary 191: → summary 192: 193: ## Highlights 194: → highlights 195: 196: ## Completed Tasks 197: → completed tasks 198: 199: ## Project Forecast 200: → project forecast 201: 202: ## Forecast Totals 203: → forecast totals 204: 205: ## Risks and Attention Points 206: → risks 207: 208: ## Next Steps 209: → next steps 210: 211: ## Management Notes 212: → management notes 213: ``` 214: 215: The importer must not rescan the Workspace Index or regenerate the Report. 216: 217: Manual edits in the current Markdown are authoritative. 218: 219: --- 220: 221: ## 6. Draw.io template contract 222: 223: A template is a user-selected uncompressed `.drawio` or `.xml` file containing visible placeholders. 224: 225: Example cell label: 226: 227: ```text 228: Executive Summary 229: {{summary}} 230: ``` 231: 232: Example template-specific field: 233: 234: ```text 235: Customer 236: {{customer}} 237: ``` 238: 239: The reconciler scans the XML source for `{{...}}` tokens without interpreting Draw.io layout, shape geometry, style, or relationships. 240: 241: The renderer replaces only known placeholder text. It must not: 242: 243: - move objects; 244: - resize shapes; 245: - modify connectors; 246: - modify styles; 247: - modify page structure; 248: - overwrite the template file. 249: 250: --- 251: 252: ## 7. Reconciliation result 253: 254: The reconciler returns: 255: 256: ```js 257: { 258: ok, 259: placeholders, 260: fields, 261: matched, 262: missingValues, 263: unknownPlaceholders, 264: unusedFields, 265: diagnostics 266: } 267: ``` 268: 269: ### Definitions 270: 271: **Matched** 272: 273: A template placeholder has a nonblank Markdown value. 274: 275: **Missing value** 276: 277: The Markdown contains the field, but its value is blank. 278: 279: **Unknown placeholder** 280: 281: The template contains a field that does not exist in the imported Markdown. 282: 283: **Unused field** 284: 285: The Markdown contains a field with no destination in the selected template. 286: 287: Unknown placeholders and missing values are not deleted. 288: 289: --- 290: 291: ## 8. Missing-field workflow 292: 293: When the selected template contains unresolved placeholders: 294: 295: ```text 296: Template placeholder 297: → unresolved 298: → show in review 299: → add to Markdown under ## Template Fields 300: → user fills value 301: → reconcile again 302: ``` 303: 304: Example insertion: 305: 306: ```md 307: ## Template Fields 308: 309: {{customer}}: 310: {{customer decision}}: 311: {{ali summary}}: 312: ``` 313: 314: The Markdown remains canonical after the user fills the values. 315: 316: The UI must not hold the only copy of manually entered values. 317: 318: --- 319: 320: ## 9. Output generation 321: 322: Generation inputs: 323: 324: ```text 325: validated uncompressed template XML 326: + 327: reconciled Markdown fields 328: ``` 329: 330: Generation output: 331: 332: ```text 333: new uncompressed .drawio XML string 334: ``` 335: 336: Suggested filename: 337: 338: ```text 339: <report-name>-visual.drawio 340: ``` 341: 342: The template file is never overwritten automatically. 343: 344: The output remains editable in Draw.io/diagrams.net. 345: 346: --- 347: 348: ## 10. UI MVP 349: 350: The UI may be a compact overlay or dedicated Report action surface. 351: 352: Required actions: 353: 354: ```text 355: Select Draw.io Template 356: Review Fields 357: Add Missing Fields to Markdown 358: Generate Draw.io 359: Cancel 360: ``` 361: 362: Required review groups: 363: 364: ```text 365: Matched 366: Missing Values 367: Unknown Template Fields 368: Unused Markdown Fields 369: ``` 370: 371: The MVP does not require a live Draw.io preview. 372: 373: --- 374: 375: ## 11. Proposed modules 376: 377: ### 11.1 `js/report/report-markdown-import.js` 378: 379: Pure module. 380: 381: Responsibilities: 382: 383: - recognize Report Markdown from leading frontmatter; 384: - parse frontmatter metadata; 385: - extract title; 386: - extract known sections; 387: - extract all `{{field name}}: value` lines; 388: - parse `## Template Fields`; 389: - preserve custom fields; 390: - return diagnostics; 391: - never mutate source Markdown. 392: 393: Export: 394: 395: ```js 396: globalThis.MME_REPORT_MARKDOWN_IMPORT 397: ``` 398: 399: ### 11.2 `js/report/drawio-report-reconciler.js` 400: 401: Pure module. 402: 403: Responsibilities: 404: 405: - normalize field names; 406: - extract `{{field name}}` placeholders from Draw.io XML; 407: - reconcile placeholders with imported Markdown fields; 408: - build missing `Template Fields` Markdown; 409: - populate an uncompressed Draw.io XML string; 410: - preserve unknown placeholders; 411: - never access DOM or file handles. 412: 413: Export: 414: 415: ```js 416: globalThis.MME_DRAWIO_REPORT_RECONCILER 417: ``` 418: 419: H2 implementation status: complete (committed at `f1a82b5`; XML declaration 420: and BOM assessment compatibility added at `3ab7f65`; registered via 421: `js/app/script-loader.js`; validator passes 101/101 in Node with honest 422: totals; sanitized H1-to-H2 integration passes). 423: 424: Current H2 limitations: 425: 426: - uncompressed XML only (compressed payloads rejected, not decoded); 427: - direct textual token replacement only; 428: - no semantic Draw.io editing; 429: - no compressed payload decoding; 430: - no UI; 431: - no template picker; 432: - no output Save As; 433: - no grouping. 434: 435: ### 11.3 Reconciliation UI owner 436: 437: Implementation file: 438: 439: ```text 440: js/report/drawio-report-panel.js 441: ``` 442: 443: Currently implemented (H3, committed at `a1c39dc`). The reconciled UI owns: 444: 445: - Report-gated entry; 446: - template selection; 447: - template assessment (compressed/invalid blocking); 448: - the four reconciliation categories (Matched, Missing Values, Unknown Template 449: Placeholders, Unused Report Fields); 450: - occurrence display; 451: - Add Missing Fields (insert absent tokens only into `## Template Fields`); 452: - Reconcile Again; 453: - the temporary in-memory session lifecycle; 454: - the single responsive overlay; 455: - light/dark mode support; 456: - the "How it works" guidance box. 457: 458: H3 does not own output delivery. H4 owns output delivery (implemented at 459: `2c03960`; flexible partial generation, aggregation, and picker compatibility 460: at `3ab7f65`; cleanup at `4541709`; APIs on 461: `globalThis.MME_DRAWIO_REPORT_PANEL`: 462: 463: - final current-Markdown reread on every generation attempt; 464: - final H1 import and final H2 reconciliation reruns — deterministic two-pass 465: reconciliation when the template opts in via `{{unused report fields}}` 466: (PASS 1 classifies; a derived field with `source: 'derived'` is added to a 467: non-mutated effective projection; PASS 2 drives the gate and population); 468: - the flexible generation gate: missing values, unknown template placeholders, 469: and unused Report fields never block; blocked only by in-progress generation, 470: non-Report, no session, no/invalid/compressed/no-placeholder templates, or no 471: matched field with a nonblank value (`no-populated-fields`); 472: - intentional partial output: matched nonblank values populated exclusively 473: through H2 `populateTemplate()`; blank matched and unknown placeholders remain 474: visible with intact braces; structural verification replaces the former 475: unresolved-token rejection; 476: - generation modes `partial` (with unresolved count) and `complete`; 477: - the `<report>-visual.drawio` output filename contract (supported Markdown/ 478: text extensions stripped, invalid characters sanitized, duplicate `-visual` 479: prevented, safe `report` fallback base; no path appends `.xml`); 480: - Save As picker delivery with a writable handle deliberately NOT retained as 481: `currentSaveHandle`, plus an XML Blob download fallback with revoked object 482: URL; 483: - template picker compatibility: `application/octet-stream` mapped to `.drawio` 484: and `application/xml` to `.xml` (no duplicate-extension declarations), All 485: files retained, files read as text, `file.type` never trusted, H2 content 486: assessment authoritative; 487: - single-owner delivery logging: the main.js adapter emits the final 488: saved/delivered/cancelled/failed logs; the panel owns begin/blocked logs, 489: visible status, and toasts; 490: - a concurrency guard blocking duplicate generation and resetting after every 491: result; 492: - cancellation and failure handling: picker cancellation (AbortError) is 493: normal and retryable, write/permission failures are structured failures — 494: neither produces a false success, and both preserve the H3 session and 495: Report; 496: - state preservation: generated delivery never contaminates the Report 497: Markdown, dirty state, `currentSaveHandle`, `currentFileName`, Report 498: identity, the H3 template session, Navigation History, 499: `WORKSPACE_STATE.activeFile`, Hot Reload ownership, or Report Notes 500: configuration; after successful generation another attempt remains allowed; 501: - aggregation guarantees: no new mxCell elements, no geometry changes, the 502: reserved placeholder never enters Markdown via Add Missing Fields, and the 503: template controls the aggregate element's location, size, and style. 504: 505: Browser-only acceptance for this flow (real picker, cancellation, download 506: fallback, laptop end-to-end suite, generated-file opening in Draw.io, mobile 507: reachability) is pending. 508: 509: Real-template desktop acceptance for H3 is pending. 510: 511: --- 512: 513: ## 12. Implementation sequence 514: 515: ### ACT H1: Reviewed Markdown import 516: 517: Deliver: 518: 519: - `report-markdown-import.js`; 520: - deterministic fixtures; 521: - Report recognition; 522: - section extraction; 523: - field extraction; 524: - source preservation. 525: 526: No Draw.io UI. 527: 528: ### ACT H2: Draw.io reconciler foundation 529: 530: Deliver: 531: 532: - `drawio-report-reconciler.js`; 533: - placeholder extraction; 534: - reconciliation result; 535: - missing Template Fields builder; 536: - uncompressed XML population; 537: - deterministic fixtures. 538: 539: No file picker and no UI. 540: 541: ### ACT H3: Reconciliation UI 542: 543: Deliver: 544: 545: - select one template; 546: - import current saved/reviewed Report Markdown; 547: - display reconciliation groups; 548: - add missing fields to Markdown; 549: - generate output after reconciliation. 550: 551: No embedded Draw.io editor. 552: 553: ### ACT H4: Output delivery 554: 555: Deliver: 556: 557: - Save As `.drawio`; 558: - suggested filename; 559: - template remains unchanged; 560: - fresh-session runtime validation; 561: - PWA registration only after workflow stability. 562: 563: --- 564: 565: ## 13. Report Notes template persistence 566: 567: The current repository snapshot describes Report Notes as module-local temporary state and explicitly labels it as never persisted. 568: 569: This is not a Draw.io blocker. 570: 571: After the Draw.io MVP, a small preference feature may add: 572: 573: ```text 574: Save Notes Template 575: Reset Notes Template 576: ``` 577: 578: Storage: 579: 580: ```text 581: localStorage 582: ``` 583: 584: Rules: 585: 586: - one saved template only; 587: - no versions; 588: - no template manager; 589: - workspace-independent user preference; 590: - Reset restores application defaults. 591: 592: --- 593: 594: ## 14. Deferred intelligence 595: 596: The following are explicitly deferred: 597: 598: - group completed Tasks by customer; 599: - group Projects by customer; 600: - group Risks by owner; 601: - group content by Tag; 602: - customer or person dimensions; 603: - automatic account-specific placeholder creation; 604: - automatic Project splitting; 605: - automatic Task splitting. 606: 607: Manual template-specific fields are acceptable in the first MVP. 608: 609: Example: 610: 611: ```text 612: {{alibaba completed tasks}}: 613: {{alibaba projects}}: 614: {{alibaba risks}}: 615: ``` 616: 617: Real Report usage will determine the later grouping architecture. 618: 619: --- 620: 621: ## 15. Out of scope for first MVP 622: 623: - embedded Draw.io editor; 624: - live template viewer; 625: - live output viewer; 626: - compressed Draw.io payloads; 627: - multiple templates in one generation; 628: - template library; 629: - template versioning; 630: - template inheritance; 631: - automatic grouping; 632: - visual field mapping; 633: - AI-generated diagrams; 634: - changing Draw.io geometry or styles; 635: - treating Draw.io as canonical data. 636: 637: --- 638: 639: ## 16. Acceptance criteria 640: 641: The MVP is complete when: 642: 643: 1. A reviewed saved Report Markdown is recognized. 644: 2. Manual Markdown edits are imported. 645: 3. One uncompressed Draw.io template can be selected. 646: 4. All `{{field name}}` placeholders are extracted. 647: 5. Matched fields are identified. 648: 6. Blank fields are identified. 649: 7. Unknown template placeholders are identified. 650: 8. Unused Markdown fields are identified. 651: 9. Missing placeholders can be inserted into `## Template Fields`. 652: 10. The user can fill those values in Markdown. 653: 11. Reconciliation can run again. 654: 12. One new editable `.drawio` output is generated. 655: 13. The template remains unchanged. 656: 14. Unknown placeholders remain preserved. 657: 15. The entire workflow can be understood and reproduced manually. 658: 659: --- 660: 661: ## 17. Architecture lock 662: 663: During ACT H implementation, do not add grouping, an embedded editor, template management, or compressed XML support. 664: 665: If a limitation is discovered: 666: 667: ```text 668: finish the thin workflow 669: → document the limitation 670: → checkpoint the working implementation 671: → improve it in a later ACT 672: ``` 673: 674: Do not redesign the workflow in the middle of implementation unless the locked end-to-end path is technically impossible. 1: # MarkmapEditor Projects Discovery MVP 2: 3: ## Architecture and Implementation Handoff 4: 5: **Purpose:** Add a minimal Markdown-native Projects workflow that follows the existing MarkmapEditor architecture used by Tasks, Tags, Relationships, the Journal sidebar, and the Full Workspace Index. 6: 7: **Primary product rule:** A Project is valid when it has a name. Every other field is optional. 8: 9: **Primary user outcome:** Write one simple Project declaration in any indexed Journal or Concept file, then automatically receive: 10: 11: - a Project entry in the shared Workspace Index; 12: - a compact sidebar Projects panel grouped by expected-order quarter; 13: - an expanded, presentable Projects Register; 14: - totals by currency; 15: - simple value and period filters; 16: - source-file navigation. 17: 18: This MVP does **not** create a full Project Manager, a `projects/` folder, standalone Project files, Tasks integration, Reports integration, Gantt, subtasks, or synchronization. 19: 20: --- 21: 22: # 1. Product philosophy 23: 24: MarkmapEditor should accept simple Markdown once and produce an organized, presentable result with minimal manual work. 25: 26: Projects follows the same pattern as Tasks: 27: 28: ```text 29: Markdown declaration in a normal file 30: ↓ 31: Workspace parser 32: ↓ 33: Shared Workspace Index state 34: ↓ 35: Compact Journal sidebar projection 36: ↓ 37: Expanded read-only Projects Register 38: ``` 39: 40: The source Markdown remains authoritative in this MVP. 41: 42: The application must not require a dedicated Project file, Project folder, separate database, or rich editor. 43: 44: --- 45: 46: # 2. Architectural fit with the current repository 47: 48: The current repository uses these established layers: 49: 50: ```text 51: workspace-parser.js 52: Parses one Markdown document into normalized metadata. 53: 54: workspace-scanner.js 55: Discovers physical Markdown files. It should not contain Project parsing. 56: 57: WORKSPACE_STATE 58: Owns the physical workspace, folder handles, files, and active physical file. 59: 60: WORKSPACE_INDEX_STATE 61: Owns the aggregated read model for files, tags, tasks, links, and future Projects. 62: 63: buildWorkspaceIndex() in main.js 64: Parses indexed files, aggregates normalized data, updates WORKSPACE_INDEX_STATE, 65: refreshes panels, and dispatches mme-workspace-index-ready. 66: 67: Journal sidebar panels in main.js 68: Follow ensure → render → wire patterns, delegated/idempotent behavior, 69: persisted collapse state, and canonical ordering. 70: 71: workspace-index-document.js 72: Generates the deterministic Full Workspace Index HTML projection. 73: It consumes state but must not scan files or mutate index state. 74: 75: workspace-index-workspace.js 76: Owns the virtual read-only Full Index workspace, Return, refresh, 77: activation/deactivation, and physical source opening. 78: 79: workspace-controller.js / openWorkspaceFile() 80: Own physical file opening, dirty-state safety, navigation-history integration, 81: active-file updates, and source navigation. 82: 83: workspace-host.js 84: Owns workspace lifecycle only. Projects Discovery does not add a new Host 85: workspace in this MVP. 86: 87: script-loader.js / sw.js 88: Own module loading and static cache generation. 89: ``` 90: 91: Projects must extend these existing owners rather than duplicate them. 92: 93: --- 94: 95: # 3. MVP boundaries 96: 97: ## Included 98: 99: - Project declarations in indexed Journals and Concepts. 100: - Project name as the only required value. 101: - Inline dictionary pairs. 102: - Multiline dictionary pairs. 103: - Optional Markdown list markers. 104: - Comma and semicolon separators for inline pairs. 105: - Quarter normalization. 106: - Known field aliases. 107: - Unknown field preservation in `extraFields`. 108: - `WORKSPACE_INDEX_STATE.projects`. 109: - Compact sidebar Projects panel. 110: - Sidebar grouping by expected-order quarter. 111: - `Unscheduled` group. 112: - Expanded Projects section/register in the Full Workspace Index. 113: - All / With Value / Without Value filters. 114: - Year and quarter filters. 115: - Totals grouped by currency. 116: - Source-file opening through the existing physical opener. 117: - Responsive presentation consistent with the current Index. 118: 119: ## Explicitly excluded 120: 121: - `projects/` folder. 122: - Standalone Project files. 123: - Project IDs written into Markdown. 124: - Project editing from the sidebar or Full Index. 125: - Project enrichment workflow. 126: - Project Workspace Host registration. 127: - Top-bar Projects workflow. 128: - Project archive workflow. 129: - Tasks inside Projects. 130: - Project/task synchronization. 131: - Subtasks. 132: - Milestones. 133: - Gantt. 134: - Probability calculations. 135: - Currency conversion. 136: - Reports integration. 137: - Groups integration. 138: - Configurable schemas. 139: - Migration of existing documents. 140: 141: --- 142: 143: # 4. Markdown declaration contract 144: 145: ## 4.1 Minimal valid Project 146: 147: ```md 148: Project: ByteDance CCTV 149: ``` 150: 151: Only the Project name is required. 152: 153: These are also valid Projects: 154: 155: ```md 156: Project: Internal workflow improvement 157: ``` 158: 159: ```md 160: Project: Customer opportunity, Status: Lead 161: ``` 162: 163: A declaration with no name is not indexed: 164: 165: ```md 166: Project: 167: ``` 168: 169: No error dialog is required. The parser may expose a non-blocking diagnostic. 170: 171: ## 4.2 Compact inline form 172: 173: ```md 174: Project: ByteDance CCTV, Value: 50000, Currency: USD, Order: 26Q4, Delivery: 27Q1, Billing: 27Q1 175: ``` 176: 177: Semicolons are equivalent separators: 178: 179: ```md 180: Project: ByteDance CCTV; Value: 50000; Currency: USD; Order: 2026-Q4 181: ``` 182: 183: ## 4.3 Multiline form 184: 185: ```md 186: Project: ByteDance CCTV 187: Value: 50000 188: Currency: USD 189: Order: 26Q4 190: Delivery: 27Q1 191: Billing: 27Q1 192: Description: CCTV opportunity for the new facility. 193: ``` 194: 195: ## 4.4 Markdown-list form 196: 197: ```md 198: Project: ByteDance CCTV 199: 200: - Value: 50000 201: - Currency: USD 202: - Order: 2026/Q4 203: - Delivery: 2027-Q1 204: - Billing: 27Q1 205: - Description: CCTV opportunity for the new facility. 206: ``` 207: 208: Bullets are optional. Accepted list prefixes for field lines may include: 209: 210: ```text 211: - 212: * 213: + 214: ``` 215: 216: ## 4.5 Multiple Projects in one file 217: 218: ```md 219: ## Commercial opportunities 220: 221: Project: ByteDance CCTV 222: Value: 50000 223: Currency: USD 224: Order: 26Q4 225: 226: Project: Alibaba Expansion 227: Value: 80000 228: Currency: USD 229: Order: 26Q3 230: 231: ## Meeting notes 232: 233: The customer requested an updated quotation. 234: ``` 235: 236: This produces two Project records. 237: 238: --- 239: 240: # 5. Project block boundaries 241: 242: A Project starts only when a parsed dictionary key normalizes exactly to: 243: 244: ```text 245: project 246: ``` 247: 248: The Project name is the value of that pair. 249: 250: A Project block continues across blank lines. 251: 252: A Project block ends at the first of: 253: 254: 1. another valid `Project:` declaration; 255: 2. a Markdown heading after the Project declaration; 256: 3. end of document. 257: 258: A heading before the Project declaration does not matter. 259: 260: Do not create a Project from `Name:` alone. 261: 262: Do not treat ordinary prose containing the word “project” as a declaration. 263: 264: --- 265: 266: # 6. Pair parsing rules 267: 268: ## 6.1 Core grammar 269: 270: ```text 271: Key: Value 272: ``` 273: 274: Accepted pair separators: 275: 276: - new line; 277: - comma followed by another key and colon; 278: - semicolon followed by another key and colon. 279: 280: Do not use arbitrary whitespace as a pair separator. 281: 282: This must not be parsed as separate fields solely because of spaces: 283: 284: ```md 285: Project: ByteDance CCTV Value: 50000 Currency: USD 286: ``` 287: 288: ## 6.2 Commas inside values 289: 290: Split a comma only when lookahead proves that another dictionary pair begins. 291: 292: Example: 293: 294: ```md 295: Project: ByteDance CCTV, Description: CCTV, access control, and monitoring, Value: 50000 296: ``` 297: 298: Expected result: 299: 300: ```text 301: Project = ByteDance CCTV 302: Description = CCTV, access control, and monitoring 303: Value = 50000 304: ``` 305: 306: Semicolon remains the recommended separator when values contain many commas. 307: 308: ## 6.3 Key normalization 309: 310: Normalize keys before alias resolution: 311: 312: - trim; 313: - lowercase; 314: - replace underscores and hyphens with spaces; 315: - collapse repeated whitespace; 316: - remove optional Markdown list prefix before extraction. 317: 318: Examples that normalize together: 319: 320: ```text 321: Expected Order 322: expected_order 323: expected-order 324: expected order 325: ``` 326: 327: --- 328: 329: # 7. Known vocabulary and aliases 330: 331: Only `Project:` starts a Project. 332: 333: ## Name 334: 335: ```text 336: project 337: project name 338: ``` 339: 340: The value of the starting `Project:` pair is canonical `name`. 341: 342: A later `Name:` pair may update the name only inside an already-started Project block. It must not start a new Project. 343: 344: ## Value 345: 346: ```text 347: value 348: amount 349: quotation value 350: quote value 351: ``` 352: 353: Canonical field: 354: 355: ```text 356: value 357: ``` 358: 359: ## Currency 360: 361: ```text 362: currency 363: curr 364: ``` 365: 366: Canonical field: 367: 368: ```text 369: currency 370: ``` 371: 372: Normalize display/storage value to uppercase when non-empty. 373: 374: ## Expected order 375: 376: ```text 377: order 378: expected order 379: order date 380: expected order date 381: ``` 382: 383: Canonical field: 384: 385: ```text 386: expectedOrder 387: ``` 388: 389: ## Expected delivery 390: 391: ```text 392: delivery 393: expected delivery 394: delivery date 395: expected delivery date 396: ``` 397: 398: Canonical field: 399: 400: ```text 401: expectedDelivery 402: ``` 403: 404: ## Expected billing 405: 406: ```text 407: billing 408: expected billing 409: billing date 410: expected billing date 411: invoice 412: expected invoice 413: ``` 414: 415: Canonical field: 416: 417: ```text 418: expectedBilling 419: ``` 420: 421: ## Status 422: 423: ```text 424: status 425: stage 426: ``` 427: 428: Canonical field: 429: 430: ```text 431: status 432: ``` 433: 434: Do not enforce a fixed status vocabulary in the parser MVP. Preserve normalized display text. 435: 436: ## Description 437: 438: ```text 439: description 440: desc 441: details 442: ``` 443: 444: Canonical field: 445: 446: ```text 447: description 448: ``` 449: 450: ## Unknown fields 451: 452: Preserve unknown dictionary pairs under: 453: 454: ```text 455: extraFields 456: ``` 457: 458: Example: 459: 460: ```md 461: Project: ByteDance CCTV 462: Customer: ByteDance 463: Country: Brazil 464: Probability: 70 465: ``` 466: 467: Expected: 468: 469: ```js 470: extraFields: { 471: customer: "ByteDance", 472: country: "Brazil", 473: probability: "70" 474: } 475: ``` 476: 477: Unknown keys must not break parsing or require parser changes. 478: 479: --- 480: 481: # 8. Quarter normalization 482: 483: ## 8.1 Accepted forms 484: 485: Two-digit year: 486: 487: ```text 488: 26Q1 489: 26/Q1 490: 26-Q1 491: 26q1 492: 26/q1 493: 26-q1 494: ``` 495: 496: Four-digit year: 497: 498: ```text 499: 2026Q1 500: 2026/Q1 501: 2026-Q1 502: 2026q1 503: 2026/q1 504: 2026-q1 505: ``` 506: 507: The same applies to Q2, Q3, and Q4. 508: 509: ## 8.2 Canonical internal representation 510: 511: Normalize all accepted values to: 512: 513: ```text 514: YYYY-QN 515: ``` 516: 517: Examples: 518: 519: ```text 520: 26Q1 → 2026-Q1 521: 26/Q2 → 2026-Q2 522: 26-Q3 → 2026-Q3 523: 2026Q4 → 2026-Q4 524: 2027/Q1 → 2027-Q1 525: ``` 526: 527: ## 8.3 Display representation 528: 529: Default compact display: 530: 531: ```text 532: YYQN 533: ``` 534: 535: Examples: 536: 537: ```text 538: 2026-Q1 → 26Q1 539: 2027-Q4 → 27Q4 540: ``` 541: 542: ## 8.4 Two-digit year expansion 543: 544: For the MVP, use a deterministic fixed rule: 545: 546: ```text 547: 00–99 → 2000–2099 548: ``` 549: 550: Do not use a moving-century window. 551: 552: ## 8.5 Invalid values 553: 554: Invalid values do not invalidate the Project. 555: 556: Examples: 557: 558: ```text 559: 26Q5 560: 2026-Q0 561: Q3 562: 26-3 563: ``` 564: 565: Recommended behavior: 566: 567: - keep the raw value in the relevant field diagnostic/raw metadata if useful; 568: - normalized quarter becomes `null`; 569: - Project appears in `Unscheduled` for expected-order grouping unless another valid order value exists; 570: - no blocking error. 571: 572: ## 8.6 Shared helper contract 573: 574: Add a small reusable parser helper conceptually equivalent to: 575: 576: ```js 577: normalizeProjectQuarter(value) 578: ``` 579: 580: Return shape: 581: 582: ```js 583: { 584: raw: "26/Q1", 585: canonical: "2026-Q1", 586: display: "26Q1", 587: year: 2026, 588: quarter: 1, 589: valid: true 590: } 591: ``` 592: 593: Invalid return: 594: 595: ```js 596: { 597: raw: "26Q5", 598: canonical: null, 599: display: "26Q5", 600: year: null, 601: quarter: null, 602: valid: false 603: } 604: ``` 605: 606: --- 607: 608: # 9. Product Intent 25: 26: MarkmapEditor should reduce repeated copying, formatting, and re-entry across disconnected work systems. 27: 28: The Quick Report MVP must support this flow: 29: 30: ```text 31: Daily Journals + optional Task metadata + discovered Projects 32: ↓ 33: Shared Report Dictionary 34: ↓ 35: Generated Markdown Report 36: ↓ 37: Existing HTML Preview 38: ↓ 39: Save As, discard, or edit manually 40: ↓ 41: Future: Open in Rich Report 42: ↓ 43: Populate Draw.io template and edit in-app 44: ``` 45: 46: The first useful output is the generated Markdown report. Task Syntax and Metadata 258: 259: ## 5.1 Basic Task remains sufficient 260: 261: ```md 262: - [ ] Update customer quotation 263: ``` 264: 265: No metadata is required. 266: 267: ## 5.2 Completed Task with hidden metadata 268: 269: ```md 270: - [x] Update customer quotation <!-- mme-task: completed=2026-08-05 --> 271: ``` 272: 273: ## 5.3 Future optional metadata 274: 275: ```md 276: - [x] Update customer quotation <!-- mme-task: completed=2026-08-05; priority=high; owner=Adelson --> 277: ``` 278: 279: Supported MVP metadata: 280: 281: ```text 282: completed 283: ``` 284: 285: Recognized but optional future-compatible metadata, only if easy to preserve safely: 286: 287: ```text 288: priority 289: owner 290: due 291: ``` 292: 293: Do not require, validate, or expose Priority, Owner, or Due in the first Report UI. 294: 295: ## 5.4 Normalized Task fields 296: 297: ```js 298: { 299: text: "Update customer quotation", 300: completed: true, 301: completedDate: "2026-08-05", 302: priority: null, 303: owner: null, 304: dueDate: null, 305: sourcePath: "...", 306: sourceKind: "...", 307: sourceLine: 12 308: } 309: ``` 310: 311: The exact Task object must preserve all existing fields. 312: 313: ## 5.5 Metadata rules 314: 315: - Checked Task with valid `completed` metadata receives a normalized `completedDate`. 316: - Checked Task without metadata remains completed with `completedDate: null`. 317: - Open Task must not keep a stale completion date after a source-proven open transition. 318: - Invalid completion date must not be treated as a valid period date. 319: - Existing Task text must exclude the hidden metadata comment. 320: - Hidden metadata must remain invisible in rendered Markdown and Markmap output where current renderer behavior allows. 321: 322: --- 323: 324: # 6. Task Completion Date Behavior 325: 326: ## 6.1 Completion from Task Review 327: 328: When Task Review changes: 329: 330: ```md 331: - [ ] Update customer quotation 332: ``` 333: 334: into completed state, write: 335: 336: ```md 337: - [x] Update customer quotation <!-- mme-task: completed=YYYY-MM-DD --> 338: ``` 339: 340: Use the current local date in a stable `YYYY-MM-DD` format. 341: 342: When Task Review reopens the Task: 343: 344: ```md 345: - [ ] Update customer quotation 346: ``` 347: 348: Remove only the `completed` property. 349: 350: If future metadata exists: 351: 352: ```md 353: <!-- mme-task: completed=2026-08-05; priority=high; owner=Adelson --> 354: ``` 355: 356: reopening becomes: 357: 358: ```md 359: <!-- mme-task: priority=high; owner=Adelson --> 360: ``` 361: 362: If the metadata comment becomes empty, remove the comment entirely. 363: 364: ## 6.2 Completion through the editor 365: 366: Do not insert dates while the user types. 367: 368: Do not insert dates during: 369: 370: - editor input; 371: - delayed render; 372: - editor blur render; 373: - local draft autosave; 374: - HTML Preview; 375: - workspace scanning; 376: - file opening; 377: - app boot. 378: 379: Use conservative reconciliation only immediately before a physical Save or Save As. 380: 381: ### Save-time reconciliation 382: 383: 1. Capture a Task baseline when a physical document becomes active or after a successful Save. 384: 2. Before physical Save, parse current editor Tasks. 385: 3. Compare the current Task set with the baseline. 386: 4. Detect unambiguous `open → completed` transitions. 387: 5. Add today’s completion date only when no completion date exists. 388: 6. Detect unambiguous `completed → open` transitions. 389: 7. Remove only the completion field. 390: 8. Apply one controlled editor/text transaction. 391: 9. Save the reconciled text. 392: 10. Refresh the Task baseline after successful Save. 393: 394: ### Conservative matching 395: 396: Prefer stable Task identity if the repository already provides one. 397: 398: Otherwise use a conservative combination such as: 399: 400: ```text 401: normalized Task text 402: + occurrence index among identical Task texts 403: + source path 404: + previous completion state 405: ``` 406: 407: If matching is ambiguous: 408: 409: - do not insert a completion date; 410: - do not remove metadata; 411: - preserve user text; 412: - optionally record a concise diagnostic. 413: 414: Never assign today’s date to every checked Task in the file. 415: 416: Historical checked Tasks without dates remain `completedDate: null`. 417: 418: --- 419: 420: # 7. 233: - existing editor, workspace, HTML, Markmap, and Report workflows remain 234: functional. 1: # MarkmapEditor Task Lifecycle Architecture 2: 3: ## Status 4: - **T1A — core lifecycle:** implemented. 5: - **T1B — physical-Save integration:** implemented. 6: 7: This document describes the Task lifecycle owner and its data contract. It is 8: the lifecycle companion to the existing 9: `docs/architecture/MarkmapEditor_Quick_Report_and_task_Metadata_MVP_PLAN.md`, 10: which remains the authority for the `mme-task` metadata comment grammar and the 11: legacy `completed` date behavior. 12: 13: > **Important:** T1B is now active. Automatic Opened/Started/Closed date writing 14: > happens **only during physical Save** (via `reconcileTasksBeforeSave`), never 15: > during typing or draft Auto-save. The lifecycle owner remains pure — all 16: > I/O, Save, and Workspace Index mutation live in `js/main.js`. Report documents 17: > are excluded from Task reconciliation by identity. 18: 19: --- 20: 21: ## 1. Purpose 22: 23: MarkmapEditor captures work as it happens (Journal and Concept notes, meetings, 24: daily notes) and derives minimal useful structure with as little manual 25: maintenance as possible. Tasks must stay easy to write as ordinary Markdown. 26: 27: The lifecycle model supports four statuses — `backlog`, `todo`, `ongoing`, 28: `done` — with automatic Opened/Started/Closed dates, so that a future simple 29: Task Board and date-based Report sections can consume trustworthy data without 30: requiring the user to maintain lifecycle fields by hand. 31: 32: ## 2. Product simplicity principle 33: 34: - Natural capture: a user types `- [ ] Prepare proposal` and nothing more is 35: required. No ID, Opened Date, status, source path, project, owner, priority, 36: or due date is required. 37: - Automatic structure: derived metadata is attached only where source-compatible 38: and unambiguous. 39: - Reveal only what is needed: lifecycle data exists for future consumers; it is 40: not surfaced everywhere in the Editor, TaskReview, Sidebar, Markmap, or HTML 41: Preview. 42: - Standard Markdown checkboxes remain authoritative. Metadata is hidden 43: HTML-comment data that other Markdown readers ignore. 44: 45: ## 3. Existing metadata grammar authority 46: 47: Task metadata uses the established hidden comment syntax defined in the Quick 48: Report Task metadata document: 49: 50: ```md 51: - [ ] Task text 52: - [x] Task text <!-- mme-task: completed=YYYY-MM-DD --> 53: - [ ] Task text <!-- mme-task: status=ongoing; owner=adelson --> 54: ``` 55: 56: Rules inherited from that authority: 57: 58: - The comment is empty-removed when all fields are gone. 59: - Keys are normalized (lowercase, `-`/space → `_`). 60: - Duplicate keys: last wins, matching the existing parser. 61: - Unknown keys are preserved round-trip. 62: - There is at most one canonical `<!-- mme-task: ... -->` comment per task line. 63: 64: T1A reuses this grammar and does not invent a second metadata format. 65: 66: ## 4. Lifecycle owner 67: 68: The pure lifecycle owner is `js/tasks/task-lifecycle.js`, published as the single 69: application global `globalThis.MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE` (following the established 70: ordered-global-script pattern; no ES imports). 71: 72: It contains only pure Task lifecycle responsibilities: 73: 74: - lifecycle status vocabulary; 75: - normalization; 76: - date-field parsing and validation; 77: - canonical task-local metadata serialization; 78: - complete-line transitions (`applyTransition`); 79: - deterministic validator fixtures. 80: 81: It performs **no I/O**: no DOM access, no Editor access, no file/localStorage/ 82: fetch access, no Save behavior, no Workspace Index mutation. 83: 84: ## 5. Checkbox authority 85: 86: The checkbox is authoritative over any lifecycle status: 87: 88: - `[x]` ⇒ effective `done`, even if a stale `status=ongoing` or `status=backlog` 89: survives in metadata. 90: - `[ ]` ⇒ open; the raw `status` selects among `todo` (default), `ongoing`, and 91: `backlog`. 92: 93: Canonical normalization therefore never lets a stale open status render a 94: checked task as open. 95: 96: ## 6. Status semantics 97: 98: | Effective status | Checkbox | Source representation | 99: | ---------------- | -------- | --------------------- | 100: | `backlog` | unchecked | `status=backlog` | 101: | `todo` | unchecked | no explicit status (default). `status=todo` is redundant and may be removed. | 102: | `ongoing` | unchecked | `status=ongoing` | 103: | `done` | checked | `completed=YYYY-MM-DD` (no `status=done`) | 104: 105: - Unchecked with `status=ongoing` → `ongoing`. 106: - Unchecked with `status=backlog` → `backlog`. 107: - Unchecked with `status=todo` → `todo`. 108: - Unchecked with absent or unknown status → `todo` (backward compatible). 109: - Checked → `done` regardless of stale status. 110: - `status=done` is never serialized. 111: 112: Todo-by-absence is the default open-state interpretation; existing Tasks without 113: ## 7. Lifecycle dates 114: 115: Canonical lifecycle fields (all `YYYY-MM-DD`): 116: 117: - `opened=YYYY-MM-DD` — first date the task became known (Opened Date); recorded 118: once, never silently replaced by a later date. 119: - `started=YYYY-MM-DD` — first date the task entered `ongoing` (Started Date); 120: recorded only on first entry to Ongoing; preserved if the task later returns 121: to Todo/Backlog. 122: - `completed=YYYY-MM-DD` — date the task entered `done` (Closed Date); recorded 123: when the checkbox becomes checked; removed on reopen. 124: 125: Normalized output on a task record: 126: 127: - `openedDate`; 128: - `startedDate`; 129: - `completedDate`; 130: - `closedDate` — an alias of the validated `completedDate`. 131: 132: Invalid calendar dates normalize to `null` for date consumers but are preserved 133: in the underlying raw metadata (never silently deleted). 134: 135: ## 8. Date supplied by the caller 136: 137: The pure lifecycle module **never reads the clock**. It does not call `new Date`, 138: `Date.now`, UTC conversion, or locale date formatting. 139: 140: The current local date is supplied by callers explicitly: 141: 142: ```js 143: applyTransition(line, { target: 'ongoing', today: '2026-09-01' }) 144: ``` 145: 146: The single application date-reading owner is `getLocalIsoDate()` in 147: `js/main.js`. When a transition semantically requires a date and the supplied 148: `today` is missing or invalid, the transition returns a validation failure and 149: writes nothing — it never invents a date. 150: 151: ## 9. Canonical serialization 152: 153: Only lifecycle-owned keys (`status`, `opened`, `started`, `completed`) may be 154: added, updated, or removed by lifecycle serialization. Unrelated metadata 155: (`owner`, `priority`, `due`, `project`, custom/unknown keys) survives round-trip 156: unchanged in meaning. 157: 158: Order behavior: 159: 160: - Existing entries keep their order. 161: - Existing lifecycle keys are updated in place. 162: - Newly introduced lifecycle keys are appended deterministically. 163: - Non-lifecycle entries and malformed segments are preserved. 164: 165: Task-line transformation preserves the bullet marker, indentation, visible task 166: text, unrelated trailing content, and newline ownership outside the single line. 167: Only the checkbox marker and lifecycle metadata may change. 168: 169: ## 10. applyTransition responsibility 170: 171: `applyTransition(line, { target, today })` is the future Task Board transition 172: API. It owns the complete task line: it may change the checkbox and task-local 173: metadata together. 174: 175: - `done` ⇒ checkbox checked; `completed` date; no `status=done`; stale open 176: status removed. 177: - `todo` / `backlog` / `ongoing` ⇒ checkbox unchecked; canonical open-status 178: representation; `completed` removed. 179: - Existing `opened`, `started`, `completed` values are not overwritten unless 180: the transition semantically requires it (e.g. Started Date on first entry to 181: Ongoing). 182: - A transition that produces a byte-identical line reports `changed: false` 183: (idempotence under repeated application) while still allowing canonical 184: cleanup on the first application, e.g. removing a redundant `status=todo`. 185: 186: This function does not access the Editor, write a file, reload the Workspace 187: Index, trigger Save, call the clock, or update a baseline. 188: ## 11. Save reconciliation responsibility (T1B, implemented) 189: 190: Automatic lifecycle reconciliation during physical Save is implemented in T1B 191: (`js/main.js` `reconcileTasksBeforeSave`). It observes the checkbox state already 192: present in the Editor Markdown — it never decides that the user intended to 193: check/uncheck a task. It: 194: 195: - aligns current Tasks to the pre-Save baseline via `matchTasksForSave` 196: (reorder-safe, text-identity matching); 197: - records/removes Closed Date (`completed`) on checkbox completion/reopening via 198: `applySaveLifecycle` (checkbox-authoritative; one consolidated Editor 199: transaction); 200: - refreshes the baseline only after a successful physical Save. 201: 202: Report documents are excluded from reconciliation by identity. Sequence matching, 203: occurrence indexing, ambiguity classification, and line-edit assembly live in the 204: pure lifecycle owner; the glue lives in `js/main.js`. 205: 206: ## 12. Date-validator consolidation (resolved) 207: 208: The temporary T1A/T1B date-validator duplication is resolved. After T1B, 209: `js/main.js` no longer declares `isValidIsoDate()` / `isLeapYear()` — the only 210: active lifecycle date validation is the pure arithmetic-only 211: `MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE.isValidIsoDate()`. The single application-local date reader 212: remains `main.js getLocalIsoDate()`, which always supplies `today` to the 213: lifecycle APIs. 214: 215: ## 13. Legacy behavior and no backfill 216: 217: Existing Tasks may lack Opened/Started/status/stable identity. Policy: 218: 219: - A legacy unchecked Task with no status defaults to `todo`. 220: - A legacy checked Task defaults to `done`; missing historical Opened Date 221: remains unknown; an existing `completed` (Closed Date) remains respected. 222: - No mass backfill. The current physical-Save date is assigned only to Tasks 223: detected as newly inserted at Save time (a T1B responsibility). 224: - A mass historical backfill, if ever desired, is a separate user-triggered 225: maintenance command and is out of scope. 226: 227: ## 14. No stable ID in T1A 228: 229: T1A introduces no stable Task ID and no UUID. The lifecycle owner operates on 230: task lines and metadata without identity. Stable identity (if required) is 231: deferred to the future Task Board / Save-integration work and is source-proven 232: only. 233: 234: ## 15. Future Board handoff 235: 236: The Board (out of scope here) will consume the pure data contract: 237: `normalizeTask`, `applyTransition`, and canonical serialization. Tasks created 238: or moved through the Board may update immediately at the board boundary, but 239: the Board UI, drag-and-drop, columns, Done-period filter, and controls are 240: explicitly excluded. 241: 242: ## 16. Future Report handoff 243: 244: Future Report sections will need Tasks Opened / Started / Closed during a 245: period, and counts of currently Ongoing / Backlog / Todo. Those consumers read 246: `effectiveStatus`, `openedDate`, `startedDate`, `closedDate` from the indexed 247: Task records. No Report section, Dictionary change, or Quick Report output 248: change is made by the lifecycle work. 249: 250: ## 17. Document-frontmatter separation 251: 252: Lifecycle metadata is task-local and lives only in the task-line `mme-task` 253: comment. Nothing is placed in document YAML frontmatter. A Journal or Concept 254: may contain many Tasks with different states and dates; each Task's lifecycle 255: metadata remains associated with its own record. Document frontmatter and 256: Metadata Template visibility architecture remain separate and unmodified. 257: 258: --- 259: 260: ## Scope 261: 262: **Included (T1B, in addition to T1A):** parser lifecycle enrichment 263: (`parseMarkdownTasks` adopts `MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE.normalizeTask`, adding 264: `status`, `effectiveStatus`, `openedDate`, `startedDate`, `closedDate` while 265: retaining every source-compatible field); physical-Save lifecycle reconciliation 266: in `js/main.js` (`reconcileTasksBeforeSave`); deterministic occurrence-aware 267: sequence matcher (`matchTasksForSave`); pure save-lifecycle metadata writer 268: (`applySaveLifecycle`) used by the reconcile pass; one consolidated CodeMirror 269: transaction; concise aggregate TaskReconcile metrics log; baseline lifecycle 270: (capture after document open; refresh only after successful physical Save; never 271: on draft Auto-save or failed Save; excluded for virtual Report documents); date-validator 272: consolidation (legacy `main.js` `isValidIsoDate`/`isLeapYear` removed in favor of 273: the pure lifecycle owner, `getLocalIsoDate` retained as the single date reader); 274: release cache identity bump in `sw.js`. 275: 276: **Explicitly excluded:** Board UI, drag-and-drop, Done-period filter, TaskReview 277: redesign, Report sections, Projects, document frontmatter, stable-ID migration, 278: transition history, Reopened Date, mass historical migration. 279: 280: --- 281: 282: ## 18. T1B implementation (physical-Save integration) 283: 284: T1B wires the pure lifecycle owner (`js/tasks/task-lifecycle.js`, global 285: `MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE`) into the existing parser and physical-Save reconciliation 286: in `js/main.js`. It adds no new UI and changes no Report output. 287: 288: ### 18.1 Parser enrichment 289: 290: `parseMarkdownTasks()` retains every existing field and, when the lifecycle owner 291: is available, folds the normalized record back via `Object.assign(task, 292: lifecycle.normalizeTask(task))`. This adds `status`, `effectiveStatus`, 293: `openedDate`, `startedDate`, `closedDate` (where `closedDate` equals the validated 294: `completedDate`). A checked Task is always effectively `done`; an unchecked 295: Task is `backlog` / `ongoing` / `todo` by its status, defaulting to `todo` for 296: absent or unknown status. Unknown raw status and unknown metadata remain 297: preserved. Parsing never writes metadata; it is a pure read of source. A legacy 298: fallback (`task.done && isValidIsoDate(meta.completed)`) remains only for the 299: case where the lifecycle owner is unexpectedly absent. 300: 301: ### 18.2 Validator consolidation 302: 303: The legacy `js/main.js` `isValidIsoDate()` / `isLeapYear()` helpers are removed: 304: after enrichment the only active lifecycle date validation is 305: `MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE.isValidIsoDate()` (arithmetic-only, no `Date` calls). The 306: single application-local date reader remains `main.js getLocalIsoDate()`, which 307: always supplies `today` to the pure lifecycle APIs — the lifecycle owner never 308: reads the clock. 309: 310: ### 18.3 Sequence matcher (`matchTasksForSave`) 311: 312: `MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE.matchTasksForSave(baseline, current)` is a small, deterministic, 313: occurrence-aware matcher built on canonical clean text and an ordered LCS 314: alignment. Its job is to PROVE only the insertion of uniquely identifiable Tasks 315: (same visible text that did not exist in the baseline); everything else is 316: classified ambiguous and never auto-tagged. 317: 318: The matcher classifies regions between matched anchors: 319: 320: - pure insertion region (unmatched current, no baseline deletions) whose visible 321: text does not already exist in the baseline, and whose text does not already 322: appear in the baseline, is a **source-proven new** candidate; 323: - pure insertion of a duplicated label (identical text already present in the 324: baseline) is **ambiguous** because, without a stable Task ID, positional proof 325: is impossible; 326: - deletion-only, edit/replace, or mixed counts are **ambiguous**, and no lifecycle 327: rewrite is applied; 328: - an inserted count above the per-gap / whole-document cap flips `skippedRewrite`, 329: so automatic new-tagging is skipped while safely matched completion/reopening 330: still applies. 331: 332: A moved existing Task is intentionally ambiguous for *new-tagging* (it must not 333: receive a spurious Opened Date). For checkbox-change detection it is handled by 334: the aligned matched pairs (text identity, not line number). The `newIndices` 335: array is intentionally unused by the Save-reconcile pass (which only processes 336: matched pairs); it exists for future Board/consumer use. The safety cap values 337: are narrow by design (per-gap 8, total-insert 20, total-new 16). 338: 339: ### 18.4 Save-lifecycle writer (`applySaveLifecycle`) 340: 341: `applySaveLifecycle(rawLine, { today, isNew, checked, explicitStatus })` edits 342: ONLY the task-local `mme-task` comment during physical-Save reconciliation. It 343: never rewrites the checkbox marker and preserves every non-lifecycle key and 344: unknown raw status. Date fields follow "add only if absent", so valid hand-written 345: dates and invalid raw values are never silently overwritten or deleted; invalid 346: raw values normalize to `null` on the derived date fields. Returns 347: `{ ok, changed, line, added, removed }`. 348: 349: ### 18.5 Physical-Save reconcile (`reconcileTasksBeforeSave`) 350: 351: The existing `js/main.js` `reconcileTasksBeforeSave()` is extended to delegate to 352: the lifecycle owner. Required ordering (one local lines array, one join, one 353: `__cmSetText`): 354: 355: 1. read current Markdown; 356: 2. parse current Tasks; 357: 3. align current Tasks against the baseline (`matchTasksForSave`); 358: 4. for each matched pair where the current checkbox disagrees with the baseline, 359: apply `applySaveLifecycle` (checkbox-authoritative); 360: 5. return one reconciled text; 361: 6. `__cmSetText` once if changed (inside `__programmaticTextChange`); 362: 7. continue through the existing physical Save; 363: 8. refresh the baseline only after a successful write. 364: 365: Report documents are excluded (`skippedReason: 'report-document'`); a missing 366: baseline or no Tasks also short-circuits with a `skippedReason` (no metadata is 367: reported as persisted). A `skippedReason` does not block the Save itself. 368: 369: ### 18.6 New-Task contract (physical Save) 370: 371: A source-proven new Task receives Opened Date during physical Save (via the 372: reconcile pass), never during typing or draft Auto-save: 373: 374: - new Todo: `opened=today`; no status; no started; no completed; 375: - new Backlog: `opened=today`; `status=backlog` preserved; no started unless 376: already valid; 377: - new Ongoing: `opened=today`; `status=ongoing` preserved; `started=today` if 378: absent; 379: - new Done: `opened=today`; `completed=today` if absent; never `status=done`; 380: stale recognized open status removed during canonical editing. 381: 382: ### 18.7 Completion and reopening 383: 384: - Open to Done: add `completed=today` if missing; preserve existing `opened` / 385: started; remove a recognized stale open status (`backlog`/`ongoing`/`todo`) 386: only when canonically editing; never write `status=done`. 387: - Done to Open: remove `completed`; preserve `opened` / `started`; keep an explicit 388: `status=backlog` or `status=ongoing`; reopen to Ongoing with missing started 389: adds `started=today`; absent/unknown status is effectively `todo`. 390: - No Reopened Date; no transition-history log. 391: 392: ### 18.8 Legacy / no-backfill policy 393: 394: Existing Tasks without `opened` stay without `opened` unless a source-proven 395: transition requires another edit. Completing a legacy Task adds `completed=today` 396: but does NOT invent `opened`. Existing checked Tasks without `completed` remain 397: `done` with unknown close date unless they newly transition in the active 398: session. Existing invalid dates normalize to `null`; raw metadata is preserved. 399: No Workspace scan or mass file update. 400: 401: ### 18.9 Duplicate-task limitation (honest) 402: 403: Visible-text identity with no stable ID cannot prove which occurrence of an 404: identical label is new after insertion, movement, or edit. The matcher therefore 405: treats ambiguous duplicate regions conservatively: it preserves source, increments 406: `ambiguous`, and never rewrites the region by occurrence number. Stable Task 407: identity remains deferred to the future Board package. The architecture does NOT 408: claim that ambiguous identical duplicates receive an Opened Date. 409: 410: ### 18.10 Baseline lifecycle 411: 412: - **Physical-open capture:** baseline captured after document content becomes 413: authoritative (post open, post draft-restore) for every normal open path 414: (`openTextDocument`, `openFromRecent`, `openSmart`, `newDocument`). 415: - **Virtual Report:** baseline is never created or used (`__taskBaseline = null`). 416: - **Draft Auto-save:** baseline is not refreshed. 417: - **Failed Save:** baseline is NOT refreshed (the next Save retries safely and 418: idempotently). 419: - **Successful Save:** baseline refreshed via `captureTaskBaseline()`. 420: - **Persistence:** in-memory only; never persisted to `localStorage`. 421: 422: ### 18.11 Transition terminology 423: 424: The lifecycle vocabulary uses 12 directional transitions across the 4 statuses 425: (backlog, todo, ongoing, done) with same-state idempotence, serialized 426: canonically by `buildTaskMetadataComment`. 427: 428: ### 18.12 Consumers 429: 430: - **Workspace Index:** enriched fields flow through the existing object spreads 431: (`...task`); `open`/`done` counts unchanged (`!done` / `done`); Backlog/Todo/Ongoing 432: all remain open. No index rendering change. 433: - **TaskReview:** current open/done view unchanged; `done` filter unchanged. 434: - **Report:** completed-task output remains based on `done`/`completedDate`; 435: byte-compatible for identical source data; no new lifecycle sections. 436: - **Journals / Concepts:** lifecycle metadata is task-local only. 437: - **Standalone Editor:** without a valid physical-document baseline, reconcile 438: short-circuits (`no-baseline`); no guessing. 439: 440: --- 441: 442: ## 19. Task Board Quick View (consumer) 443: 444: This section documents the first visual Task management experience — the **Simple 445: Task Board Quick View** — as a consumer of the lifecycle owner. It adds no 446: lifecycle logic and does not begin Reports, Projects, Groups, or a full Task mode. 447: 448: ### 19.1 Three-level Task architecture 449: 450: - **Level 1 — Workspace Index:** the normalized read model. Discovers Tasks, 451: normalizes lifecycle fields (`status`, `effectiveStatus`, `openedDate`, 452: `startedDate`, `completedDate`, `closedDate`) and preserves source path, file 453: kind, file name, and line. Stays close to raw Workspace data. 454: - **Level 2 — TaskReview Sidebar:** the compact Sidebar view (`js/workspace/task-review.js`). 455: Owns the Sidebar Tasks panel, quick search/filters, open/done experience, source 456: navigation, and the single **Board** entry action. 457: - **Level 3 — Task Board Quick View:** the focused wide overlay 458: (`js/tasks/task-board.js`, global `MME_TASK_BOARD`). Renders four lifecycle 459: columns, supports status changes and Done-period filtering, and navigates to 460: source. A future optional full Task Manager mode is a possible later layer, not 461: part of this package. 462: 463: ### 19.2 Board entry ownership 464: 465: TaskReview owns the Sidebar entry. A single visible-text **`Board`** button 466: (`aria-label="Open Task Board"`, `id="workspaceTaskBoardBtn"`) sits beside the 467: Tasks panel collapse control as a sibling (no nested buttons; the collapse control 468: is wrapped in `.workspaceTasksHeaderCollapse`). It appears only when TaskReview is 469: available (a Workspace and Index are ready gate the Tasks panel). It opens the 470: single Board owner and never creates duplicate overlays. It is not added to the 471: global toolbar and does not create a separate Tasks application context. 472: 473: ### 19.3 Quick View ownership (the overlay) 474: 475: The Board is one stable in-application overlay (`#mmeTaskBoard`, `role="dialog"`, 476: `aria-modal="true"`) created once by `ensureBoard()`. Lifecycle: `ensure → wire 477: once → render from current Index → show/hide`. Reopening never re-creates the 478: overlay and never duplicates wiring (idempotent guards). Opening preserves the 479: active application context, pane layout, Workspace, and Editor instance; closing 480: hides the overlay, restores focus to the invoking Board button where practical, 481: and does not navigate or reset lifecycle state. Escape closes the Board when it is 482: the visible top dialog, following the existing overlay-precedence grammar; no new 483: modal manager is introduced. A single `mme-workspace-index-ready` listener (guarded) 484: re-renders only while the Board is open. 485: 486: ### 19.4 Four fixed columns 487: 488: The Board contains exactly the four lifecycle columns in order: 489: 490: `Backlog → Todo → Ongoing → Done` 491: 492: Grouping uses the lifecycle `effectiveStatus` (via the lifecycle owner's 493: `effectiveStatusOf` when present), with the documented fallback: checked → Done; 494: `status=backlog` → Backlog; `status=ongoing` → Ongoing; other unchecked → Todo. 495: Unknown status values fall to Todo. Columns are not configurable; no Waiting, 496: Blocked, Canceled, Archived, status customizations, or swimlanes. 497: 498: ### 19.5 Workspace Index as read model; Markdown as source of truth 499: 500: The Board renders **only** from `WORKSPACE_INDEX_STATE`. There is no parallel Task 501: store and no Task array is persisted to `localStorage`. Markdown remains the source 502: of truth: the Board never writes checkbox markers, `status`, `opened`, `started`, 503: or `completed` itself, and never patches the Workspace Index directly. 504: 505: ### 19.6 applyTransition as the lifecycle mutation owner 506: 507: Every status change calls 508: `globalThis.MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE.applyTransition(currentLine, { target, today })`. 509: The Board supplies the **current physical line**, the **target status**, and the 510: **canonical local today** — it does not reimplement lifecycle rules. The pure 511: lifecycle owner decides checkbox state, status metadata, started/completed dates, 512: and canonical serialization. The Board does not write `status=done` (the module 513: never writes `status=` at all) and does not require explicit `status=todo`. 514: 515: ### 19.7 Canonical local date owner 516: 517: `main.js` publishes `getLocalIsoDate` narrowly as 518: `globalThis.getLocalIsoDate = getLocalIsoDate` (main.js is the single reader of 519: the system clock). The Board calls only this public owner and passes `today` 520: explicitly to the lifecycle module. The Board never calls `new Date()`, 521: `Date.now()`, UTC conversion, or locale date formatting. 522: 523: ### 19.8 Source-first mutation and persistence flow 524: 525: The status-change persistence flow (reusing existing owners — no alternate Save 526: pipeline): 527: 528: 1. the user chooses a new status; 529: 2. the Board retrieves the current source path/line from the indexed Task record; 530: 3. navigation is requested through the existing `openWorkspaceFile` owner, and the 531: Board awaits a definitive result; 532: 4. after the source opens, the Board revalidates the current physical line via the 533: existing TaskReview source resolver (`MME_TASK_REVIEW.findActualTaskLine`) using 534: source path, indexed line, canonical clean text, and the *current* Editor 535: content — never stale `raw`/indexed metadata or an assumed line number; 536: 5. `applyTransition(currentLine, { target, today })` returns the canonical line; 537: 6. the existing `__cmReplaceLine` bridge replaces exactly that resolved physical line; 538: 7. `saveSmart()` persists the change through the existing owner; 539: 8. the existing `scheduleWorkspaceIndexRebuild()` rebuilds the Workspace Index; 540: 9. the Board re-renders from the rebuilt Index (index-ready listener) and TaskReview 541: refreshes through its own existing index-ready path. 542: 543: The Board uses an in-progress guard and disables only the active card control while 544: a mutation is pending; it does not block the whole application. 545: 546: ### 19.9 Dirty-file and navigation protection 547: 548: A Task may belong to the active document or to another Journal/Concept. Because a 549: modal Board overlay could obscure navigation/dirty-state prompts, the Board 550: **temporarily hides itself** before requesting source navigation, then restores 551: afterward. It distinguishes the three `openWorkspaceFile` outcomes: 552: opened successfully (proceeds), cancelled (`null` / `ok:false,cancelled` — leaves 553: all sources unchanged and restores the Board with the touched control reset), or 554: failed/blocked (leaves source unchanged, refreshes the Board from the current 555: Index, shows a concise message). File permissions are never bypassed and no 556: cross-file writer is created. Stale indexed text is never overwritten. 557: 558: After a successful open, the Board revalidates the resolved line using the current 559: Editor content. A no-match, ambiguous match, out-of-range, or text-inconsistent 560: result aborts the mutation (preferring no change over editing the wrong occurrence 561: of a duplicate label), resets the Move control, and refreshes from source. There is 562: **no stable task ID** in this package; line drift after lifecycle metadata updates 563: is handled by the existing source resolver's near-line fallback. 564: 565: ### 19.10 Status movement interaction 566: 567: Status movement does **not** depend on drag-and-drop. Each card exposes one native 568: **Move to…** select (Backlog/Todo/Ongoing/Done) — keyboard, touch, and mouse 569: accessible, with the current status disabled. Drag-and-drop is not implemented in 570: this package. 571: 572: ### 19.11 Done-period filter 573: 574: - Default: **30** days. Options: **7 / 30 / 90 / All**. Custom period is deferred. 575: - Persisted only under `markmap:taskBoard:doneWindow`; invalid stored values fall 576: back to `30`. Card positions, copied data, complete Board state, filtered arrays, 577: and open file content are never persisted. 578: - **Recent-Done rule:** a Done Task is recent iff its `closedDate` is valid and 579: falls on one of the N calendar dates ending at the canonical local today — today 580: plus the previous **N−1** dates. The boundary is **inclusive**, date-only, with 581: no UTC shift. 582: - **Undated Done** (no valid `closedDate`): excluded from 7/30/90 recent views; 583: included under **All**; counted (optionally shown) as *undated*; never assigned a 584: fabricated date. 585: - The filter changes **visibility only**. It never archives, deletes, or modifies 586: Markdown, completed metadata, Reports, or Workspace Index counts. 587: 588: ### 19.12 Source navigation (title click) 589: 590: Clicking a card title identifies the Workspace-relative source path, closes the 591: Board, calls the existing TaskReview `openTaskSource` owner (no second navigation 592: implementation), opens the source file, navigates to the best available Task line, 593: and focuses the Editor where supported. This path performs no lifecycle mutation. 594: 595: ### 19.13 Card content and empty/legacy states 596: 597: Cards show only task text, concise source context (kind • file name), an optional 598: relevant lifecycle date (Started for Ongoing; Closed for Done when present), and 599: the Move control. Raw metadata, full paths, internal identity, owner/priority/due/ 600: project/tags are not shown. Missing dates never block rendering; legacy Tasks stay 601: visible. Concise empty states are used per column (e.g., "No tasks in progress."). 602: No Workspace / no Index states prevent opening an empty four-column shell. 603: 604: ### 19.14 Touch, keyboard, and responsive behavior 605: 606: Four columns are visible where width permits; at narrow widths the columns area 607: scrolls horizontally with stable readable column widths, and the Board overlay 608: honors safe-area insets. Touch scrolling is not blocked by card movement (native 609: select, no drag). Restrained semantic accents (Backlog gray, Todo blue/neutral, 610: Ongoing amber, Done green/subdued) never rely on color alone — column names and 611: counts remain visible — and light/dark modes reuse existing CSS variables. 612: Coarse-pointer targets follow existing application conventions. No separate mobile 613: Board architecture and no mandatory primary-column state. 614: 615: ### 19.15 Integrated T1B acceptance 616: 617: The Board is the main browser-acceptance surface for the T1B physical-Save 618: reconciliation. Cases include: a new unchecked Task typed normally gains no 619: metadata during typing or draft Auto-save and receives `opened=today` once on 620: physical Save; middle insertion tags only the new unique Task; Todo→Ongoing adds 621: `started`; Todo/Ongoing→Done checks the checkbox and adds `completed`; Done→Todo 622: unchecks and removes `completed` while preserving `opened`/`started`; Todo→Backlog 623: writes `status=backlog`; ambiguous duplicate labels do not swap metadata; TaskReview 624: stays synchronized after rebuild and Index counts remain correct; Report output and 625: Journals/Concepts remain correct; source navigation/Editor behavior stays sane with 626: no duplicate render or log flood. Lifecycle defects found during that validation are 627: fixed in their true owner (`task-lifecycle.js`, `main.js` Save reconciliation, 628: Workspace Index refresh, or TaskReview compatibility) — never patched inside Board 629: rendering. Any unexecuted browser case is reported honestly, never marked PASS. 630: 631: ### 19.16 Future scope (deferred) 632: 633: - A full Task Manager mode is a possible future layer; this package only adds the 634: three-level architecture and the Quick View, and does not build architecture for 635: a full mode. 636: - **Groups** integration is not part of this package. 637: - **Project filters** are not part of this package. The Board header reserves space 638: such that a small future filter area (Group / Project / Search) can be added 639: without redesigning the entire Board; no disabled placeholders are rendered. 1: # MarmapEditorX3 — Workspace Host Foundation 2: 3: ## Repository-Specific Whole-Implementation Plan 4: 5: **Status:** PLAN / REVIEW 6: **Implementation:** NOT AUTHORIZED UNTIL PHASE 1 HANDOFF IS REVIEWED 7: **Repository baseline:** latest supplied Repomix snapshot (`repomix-output-depaulo-MarkmapEditor (3).xml`) 8: **Target:** Introduce a Workspace Host while preserving the current Journal experience 9: **Candidate runtime module:** `js/workspaces/workspace-host.js` 10: 11: --- 12: 13: ## 1. Core Architectural Principles 103: 104: ### 3.1 Host owns workspace lifecycle only 105: 106: The Workspace Host owns: 107: 108: - workspace registry; 109: - active workspace ID; 110: - activation/deactivation transition; Target Interfaces 185: 186: ### 4.1 Workspace descriptor 187: 188: Recommended minimum shape: 189: 190: ```javascript 191: { 192: id: 'journal', 193: title: 'Journal', 194: 195: async activate(context) {}, 196: async deactivate(context) {}, 197: async refresh(context) {}, 198: async detach(context) {}, 199: 200: getState() {}, 201: async restoreState(state, context) {} 202: } 203: ``` 204: 205: ### 4.2 Workspace Host public API 206: 207: Recommended candidate API: 208: 209: ```javascript 210: MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.register(workspace) 211: MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.unregister(id) 212: MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.has(id) 213: MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.get(id) 214: MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.list() 215: MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.getActive() 216: MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.getActiveId() 217: MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.getSession(id) 218: MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.subscribe(listener) 219: 220: await MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.activate(id, context) 221: await MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.switchTo(id, context) 222: await MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.deactivate(context) 223: await MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.refresh(context) 224: await MME_WORKSPACE_HOST.detach(context) 225: ``` 226: 227: Exact names may change after Phase 1 review, but lifecycle ownership must remain centralized. 228: 229: --- 230: 231: ## 5. Transactional Switching Contract 232: 233: Workspace switching must be transactional. 234: 235: Unsafe flow: 236: 237: ```text 238: deactivate current 239: → set active ID to next 240: → next activation fails 241: → no valid active workspace 242: ``` 243: 244: Required conceptual flow: 245: 246: ```text 247: 1. validate target registration; 248: 2. reject/serialize concurrent switches; 249: 3. capture current workspace state; 250: 4. ask current workspace to deactivate; 251: 5. ask target workspace to restore prior target state if available; 252: 6. ask target workspace to activate; 253: 7. only after activation succeeds, commit active workspace ID; 254: 8. notify subscribers; 255: 9. if target activation fails, attempt to reactivate previous workspace; 256: 10. report structured failure without silently corrupting host state. 257: ``` 258: 259: The skeleton must be reviewed against actual Journal lifecycle behavior before relying on rollback. 260: 261: --- 262: 263: ## 6.
