Purpose 15: 16: Implement the first safe version of application-level document navigation history: 17: 18: - **Back** returns to the previously opened physical workspace document. 19: - **Forward** returns to the next document after a Back operation. 20: - History represents user navigation order, not filesystem order. 21: 22: Example: 23: 24: ```text 25: Journal A 26: → Concept B 27: → Journal C 28: → Back = Concept B 29: → Back = Journal A 30: → Forward = Concept B 31: ``` 32: 33: This V1 deliberately establishes and validates the navigation foundation before the virtual Workspace Index document is introduced. 34: 35: --- 36: 37: ## 2. V1 Scope 38: 39: V1 includes: 40: 41: 1. One centralized navigation-history state owner. 42: 2. Transactional Back / Forward behavior. 43: 3. A canonical physical workspace location identity. 44: 4. Duplicate-current-location prevention. 45: 5. Dirty-document cancellation safety. 46: 6. Forward-stack invalidation after successful normal navigation. 47: 7. History clearing when a workspace is opened. 48: 8. Startup-restored physical file seeding without a Back entry. 49: 9. Visible Back / Forward controls in the Journal workspace sidebar. 50: 10. Navigation inherited through the central physical workspace-open flow. 51: 11. Browser and regression validation. 52: 53: V1 does **not** include: 54: 55: - virtual Workspace Index document; 56: - virtual locations; 57: - browser History API; 58: - persistent history across reloads; 59: - filesystem Previous / Next; 60: - keyboard shortcuts; 61: - cursor restoration; 62: - scroll restoration; 63: - graph or Mermaid views; 64: - Report Mode; 65: - changes to workspace scanning, parsing, tags, tasks or backlinks. 66: 67: The later virtual Workspace Index package must reuse this V1 history system rather than create another one. 68: 69: --- 70: 71: ## 3. Repository Reality 72: 73: The current repository has a predominant physical workspace-open function: 74: 75: ```text 76: openWorkspaceFile(file, kind, reason) 77: ``` 78: 79: Its current responsibilities include: 80: 81: 1. validating the physical file and handle; 82: 2. reading the file; 83: 3. applying existing dirty-document confirmation; 84: 4. opening the text through the current document lifecycle; 85: 5. assigning `WORKSPACE_STATE.activeFile`; 86: 6. persisting the active physical path; 87: 7. updating sidebar highlight; 88: 8. refreshing Active, Related and Tasks panels; 89: 9. scheduling workspace-index rebuild; 90: 10. returning the opened file or `null` when navigation is cancelled. 91: 92: This is the preferred physical navigation integration boundary. 93: 94: The repository also contains paths that must be classified during PLAN: 95: 96: - `openWorkspaceSearchResultFile()` fallback; 97: - `reopenLastActiveWorkspaceFileIfPossible()`; 98: - `openToday()`; 99: - New Concept behavior; 100: - physical opens initiated by Wiki Links; 101: - Related items; 102: - Task Review; 103: - Tags; 104: - Search results; 105: - sidebar journal/concept lists. 106: 107: Do not independently add history code to every UI surface if those surfaces already reach the same physical open path. 108: 109: --- 110: 111: ## 4. Architectural Principles 112: 113: ### 4.1 One history owner 114: 115: Recommended new module: 116: 117: ```text 118: js/navigation/navigation-history.js 119: ``` 120: 121: It owns: 122: 123: - current physical navigation location; 124: - back stack; 125: - forward stack; 126: - location normalization and equality; 127: - Back / Forward transaction semantics; 128: - navigation-in-progress protection; 129: - subscriptions for UI state; 130: - `canBack` / `canForward` derivation. 131: 132: It must not: 133: 134: - read files; 135: - parse Markdown; 136: - access File System handles directly; 137: - rebuild the workspace index; 138: - render workspace panels; 139: - implement Wiki-Link-specific history; 140: - own Save or Save As. 141: 142: ### 4.2 One physical opener 143: 144: Physical navigation must continue through the existing workspace-opening behavior. 145: 146: Do not replace `openWorkspaceFile()`. 147: 148: Do not create a second complete physical file loader. 149: 150: ### 4.3 Transactional history 151: 152: History must commit only after successful navigation. 153: 154: Unsafe: 155: 156: ```text 157: mutate stacks 158: → attempt open 159: → user cancels 160: → stacks are corrupted 161: ``` 162: 163: Required: 164: 165: ```text 166: peek target 167: → attempt open 168: → await result 169: → commit stack movement only when opened 170: ``` 171: 172: ### 4.4 No source-specific histories 173: 174: Wiki Links, Related, Tasks, Tags, Search, Today and sidebar clicks must not maintain independent stacks. 175: 176: They should inherit history through the central coordinator / successful physical-open boundary. 177: 178: --- 179: 180: ## 5. Physical Navigation Location Contract 181: 182: V1 supports only physical workspace files. 183: 184: Recommended conceptual structure: 185: 186: ```javascript 187: { 188: type: 'workspace-file', 189: path: 'concepts/alibaba.md', 190: kind: 'concepts', 191: name: 'alibaba.md', 192: source: 'wiki-link' 193: } 194: ``` 195: 196: Required identity fields: 197: 198: - `type` 199: - canonical `path` 200: 201: Useful metadata: 202: 203: - `kind` 204: - `name` 205: - `source` 206: 207: V1 must not store a `FileSystemHandle` as the location identity. 208: 209: The opener may resolve the current physical file record from the canonical path when restoring history. 210: 211: Location equality: 212: 213: ```text 214: type + normalized canonical path 215: ``` 216: 217: Normalize paths consistently with current workspace path behavior. 218: 219: Opening the current location again must return a no-op and must not: 220: 221: - add history; 222: - clear Forward; 223: - prompt dirty discard; 224: - cause a duplicate file open. 225: 226: --- 227: 228: ## 6. Navigation Modes 229: 230: V1 must distinguish these modes: 231: 232: ### `normal` 233: 234: Used for ordinary user navigation. 235: 236: After successful open: 237: 238: - previous current moves to Back; 239: - target becomes current; 240: - Forward clears. 241: 242: If unsuccessful or cancelled: 243: 244: - all history remains unchanged; 245: - Forward remains unchanged. 246: 247: ### `restore` 248: 249: Used by Back and Forward. 250: 251: - target opens through the physical opener; 252: - no normal history entry is generated; 253: - stack movement commits only after successful open. 254: 255: ### `seed` 256: 257: Used after startup last-active-file restoration. 258: 259: - establishes current location; 260: - creates no Back entry; 261: - leaves Forward empty. 262: 263: A later package may add `refresh` for virtual documents. V1 may reserve the mode name but must not implement virtual refresh behavior. 264: 265: --- 266: 267: ## 7. Structured Navigation Result 268: 269: Physical navigation integration must distinguish: 270: 271: ```javascript 272: { 273: status: 'opened' | 'cancelled' | 'failed' | 'noop', 274: location, 275: error 276: } 277: ``` 278: 279: Semantics: 280: 281: - `opened`: target successfully became the current physical workspace document. 282: - `cancelled`: existing dirty confirmation was cancelled. 283: - `failed`: file resolution, handle access or open lifecycle failed. 284: - `noop`: target equals the current location. 285: 286: Do not report a cancelled navigation as failure. 287: 288: Do not commit history for `cancelled`, `failed`, or `noop`. 289: 290: --- 291: 292: ## 8. Recommended Public API 293: 294: Exact names may be reconciled, but semantics must remain centralized. 295: 296: ```javascript 297: MME_NAVIGATION.back() 298: MME_NAVIGATION.forward() 299: MME_NAVIGATION.canBack() 300: MME_NAVIGATION.canForward() 301: MME_NAVIGATION.getCurrent() 302: MME_NAVIGATION.seed(location) 303: MME_NAVIGATION.clear() 304: MME_NAVIGATION.subscribe(listener) 305: MME_NAVIGATION.setOpener(openLocation) 306: MME_NAVIGATION.recordSuccessfulNavigation(location, options) 307: ``` 308: 309: Avoid a public API that encourages callers to push a destination before it has opened successfully. 310: 311: The module should expose read-only snapshots rather than direct mutable stack references. 312: 313: --- 314: 315: ## 9. Back Transaction 316: 317: Required conceptual sequence: 318: 319: ```text 320: 1. If navigation is in progress, do nothing. 321: 2. If Back is empty, return noop. 322: 3. Peek the Back target without removing it. 323: 4. Capture the current location. 324: 5. Attempt target open with mode=restore. 325: 6. If opened: 326: - remove target from Back; 327: - push prior current into Forward; 328: - set target as current; 329: - notify subscribers. 330: 7. If cancelled or failed: 331: - preserve Back; 332: - preserve Forward; 333: - preserve current; 334: - notify only if UI in-progress state changed. 335: 8. Clear in-progress state in finally. 336: ``` 337: 338: Forward performs the inverse. 339: 340: --- 341: 342: ## 10. Concurrency Contract 343: 344: While Back or Forward is opening a target: 345: 346: - Back and Forward controls are disabled; 347: - a second navigation-history request must not start another transition; 348: - stack state must not partially commit; 349: - the in-progress guard must clear in `finally`. 350: 351: V1 may ignore repeated requests while one history transition is active. 352: 353: It does not need to implement a queue. 354: 355: --- 356: 357: ## 11. Dirty Document Contract 358: 359: The current dirty-confirmation behavior remains authoritative. 360: 361: Back / Forward must not introduce another independent confirmation prompt. 362: 363: Required behavior: 364: 365: ```text 366: dirty physical document 367: → press Back 368: → existing confirmation appears 369: → Cancel 370: → document unchanged 371: → Back unchanged 372: → Forward unchanged 373: → current location unchanged 374: ``` 375: 376: Normal navigation after a Back must clear Forward only after the new target opens successfully. 377: 378: If the open is cancelled, Forward must remain available. 379: 380: --- 381: 382: ## 12. Workspace Lifecycle 383: 384: ### Successful workspace open 385: 386: On successful workspace open: 387: 388: ```text 389: MME_NAVIGATION.clear() 390: ``` 391: 392: This prevents stale paths or handles from a prior workspace from being restored. 393: 394: ### Last-active-file restoration 395: 396: If the repository restores a last active physical file: 397: 398: ```text 399: successful restoration 400: → MME_NAVIGATION.seed(restoredLocation) 401: ``` 402: 403: No Back entry is created. 404: 405: ### No restored file 406: 407: History remains empty until the first successful normal physical navigation. 408: 409: Do not derive cross-workspace identity only from workspace display name. 410: 411: --- 412: 413: ## 13. Purpose 4: 5: This document defines the stable product principles that guide the design and development of MarkmapEditor. 6: 7: It explains why the product is structured as it is and provides decision criteria for future features, architecture plans, implementation packages, and user-interface changes. 8: 9: This document does not replace subsystem architecture files. 10: 11: Use the following authority model: 12: 13: PRODUCT_PRINCIPLES.md 14: -> stable product philosophy and decision criteria 15: 16: AI_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md 17: -> required PLAN, review, ACT, validation, and checkpoint process 18: 19: AI_DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md 20: -> execution environment and tooling constraints 21: 22: docs/architecture/ 23: -> subsystem ownership, contracts, information flows, and boundaries 24: 25: Feature PLAN handoffs 26: -> source-grounded scope for the current implementation package 27: 28: ACT completion reports 29: -> implementation evidence, validation results, and checkpoint status 30: 31: When multiple technically valid solutions exist, prefer the one that follows these principles while preserving the current source-proven architecture. 32: 33: --- 34: 35: ## 1. Simplicity First 36: 37: MarkmapEditor should remain as straightforward as possible. 38: 39: Use the smallest complete workflow that provides real user value. 40: 41: Do not introduce complexity only because it could become useful in the future. 42: 43: Architectural space may be reserved for future evolution, but reserving space does not authorize implementing the future subsystem now. 44: 45: Prefer: 46: 47: - direct workflows; 48: - understandable controls; 49: - minimal required fields; 50: - existing application patterns; 51: - explicit actions; 52: - progressive enhancement; 53: - small, complete implementation packages. 54: 55: Avoid: 56: 57: - speculative configuration; 58: - duplicate systems; 59: - unnecessary management screens; 60: - premature abstraction; 61: - hidden automation; 62: - features that create ongoing maintenance work for the user; 63: - large frameworks for problems that can be solved locally and clearly. 64: 65: Complexity must be justified by a real workflow, current technical requirement, or repeated usage need. 66: 67: --- 68: 69: ## 2. Markdown Is the Canonical Source 70: 71: Markdown remains the primary portable and understandable source of information. 72: 73: Visual interfaces should consume, enrich, or interact with Markdown-backed information without silently replacing it with a competing source of truth. 74: 75: The preferred information path is: 76: 77: Physical Markdown 78: -> parsing and normalization 79: -> shared application model 80: -> focused views and outputs 81: -> explicit source mutation 82: -> physical Save 83: -> shared model refresh 84: 85: Examples include: 86: 87: Tasks: 88: Markdown Task 89: -> Task lifecycle normalization 90: -> Workspace Index 91: -> TaskReview or Task Board 92: -> source mutation 93: -> physical Save 94: -> Workspace Index rebuild 95: 96: Projects: 97: Markdown Project declaration 98: -> Workspace Index 99: -> Sidebar Projects view 100: -> Project Quick View 101: -> richer Project workflow only if justified 102: 103: Reports: 104: Workspace Index 105: -> generated Markdown report 106: -> user review 107: -> Report Dictionary 108: -> Draw.io reconciliation 109: -> visual output 110: 111: Knowledge: 112: Markdown Journals and Concepts 113: -> Workspace Index 114: -> links, tags, timelines, and explorers 115: -> future graph-based views if justified 116: 117: Markmap, HTML Preview, Task Board, Draw.io, Mermaid, and future Graph Views are representations or interaction surfaces over shared information. 118: 119: They do not automatically become canonical data stores. 120: 121: Any change to the canonical-data model requires an explicit architecture decision. 122: 123: --- 124: 125: ## 3. Information Flow Must Be Clear 126: 127: The movement of information through the application should be explainable. 128: 129: For every feature, the architecture should be able to answer: 130: 131: What is the canonical source? 132: Who parses it? 133: Who normalizes it? 134: Who displays it? 135: Who may mutate it? 136: Who persists it? 137: What event or operation refreshes its consumers? 138: 139: If these answers are unclear, duplicated, or contradictory, the work package must return to PLAN or architecture review. 140: 141: Implementation convenience is not sufficient justification for an unclear information flow. 142: 143: A user or future developer should be able to understand how information moves from source to interface and back to source without reconstructing the behavior from unrelated modules. 144: 145: --- 146: 147: ## 4. One Clear Owner per Responsibility 148: 149: Each important responsibility should have one authoritative owner. 150: 151: Examples of responsibilities include: 152: 153: - parsing; 154: - normalization; 155: - lifecycle transitions; 156: - source mutation; 157: - physical persistence; 158: - view rendering; 159: - navigation; 160: - refresh coordination; 161: - global preferences; 162: - workspace state. 163: 164: Consumers should call or observe the appropriate owner rather than reproduce its logic. 165: 166: Avoid: 167: 168: - duplicated lifecycle rules; 169: - multiple competing indexes; 170: - separate local copies of global preference state; 171: - repeated file scanning; 172: - polling when an existing refresh event is sufficient; 173: - visual components writing metadata directly when a domain owner exists; 174: - multiple modules believing they own the same control or transaction. 175: 176: A new owner should be introduced only when an existing owner cannot reasonably or safely hold the responsibility. 177: 178: --- 179: 180: ## 5. Reuse Shared State Before Creating Parallel State 181: 182: Before adding state, determine whether the required information already exists in: 183: 184: - the current physical document; 185: - the Workspace Index; 186: - an established domain owner; 187: - a current workspace session; 188: - an existing global preference; 189: - an existing event or refresh lifecycle. 190: 191: Prefer derived read models over redundant persisted state. 192: 193: Do not create a second source of truth merely to simplify one user interface. 194: 195: Patterns to avoid include: 196: 197: - a second Workspace Index; 198: - a separate Project scanner; 199: - a Board-only copy of Task lifecycle state; 200: - a local theme system for one overlay; 201: - a duplicated document metadata store; 202: - a persisted value that can be safely and cheaply derived; 203: - polling for changes already announced by application events. 204: 205: Parallel state is acceptable only when its purpose, synchronization contract, failure behavior, and owner are explicitly defined. 206: 207: --- 208: 209: ## 6. Use Progressive Interaction Levels 210: 211: MarkmapEditor should introduce interaction depth progressively. 212: 213: The product-wide model is: 214: 215: Source or normalized Workspace data 216: -> closest representation of the underlying information 217: 218: Sidebar 219: -> quick information and lightweight actions 220: 221: Quick View 222: -> richer focused interaction 223: 224: Full Mode 225: -> only when sustained usage justifies it 226: 227: Examples: 228: 229: Tasks 230: -> TaskReview Sidebar 231: -> Task Board Quick View 232: -> possible future Task Manager 233: 234: Projects 235: -> Projects Sidebar 236: -> Project Quick View 237: -> possible future Projects Mode 238: 239: Reports 240: -> Report Sidebar setup 241: -> focused Report generation and reconciliation 242: -> possible future Report Designer 243: 244: Knowledge 245: -> compact Sidebar panels 246: -> focused explorers 247: -> possible future Graph or Knowledge Mode 248: 249: A Full Mode should not be created merely because another feature has one. 250: 251: Visual symmetry is not sufficient justification for architectural symmetry. 252: 253: --- 254: 255: ## 7. Standalone First, Integration by Opt-In 256: 257: Useful workflows should provide value without requiring the user to configure the entire MarkmapEditor workspace model. 258: 259: Where technically reasonable: 260: 261: - standalone document workflows should work immediately; 262: - Journal and Knowledge integration should be optional; 263: - Workspace aggregation should add value without becoming mandatory; 264: - Groups should remain optional; 265: - advanced metadata should remain optional; 266: - users should be able to capture information before organizing it deeply. 267: 268: Integration should be progressive: 269: 270: Standalone use 271: -> optional Workspace discovery 272: -> optional Knowledge or Journal aggregation 273: -> optional Groups and richer filtering 274: 275: The application should not require advanced organization before basic work can begin. 276: 277: --- 278: 279: ## 8. Fast Capture Remains a First-Class Workflow 280: 281: MarkmapEditor must preserve fast Markdown capture even as richer visual workflows are added. 282: 283: A user should be able to create useful information with minimal syntax and minimal interruption. 284: 285: Examples: 286: 287: - a basic Markdown checkbox remains a valid Task; 288: - a Project is valid when it has a name; 289: - optional metadata enriches behavior but does not invalidate simple input; 290: - Reports begin as understandable Markdown; 291: - Mermaid begins as Markdown-native diagram syntax; 292: - specialized templates remain optional. 293: 294: Rich interfaces must share the same underlying information model. 295: 296: They should not force users to abandon direct Markdown editing. 297: 298: --- 299: 300: ## 9. Metadata Must Be Progressive 301: 302: Metadata should be introduced only when it enables a useful workflow. 303: 304: Basic content must remain valid without every optional field. 305: 306: Prefer: 307: 308: - minimal required fields; 309: - optional structured enrichment; 310: - conservative normalization; 311: - visible user-authored tags; 312: - metadata that can be ignored safely; 313: - archive instead of destructive deletion where appropriate. 314: 315: Avoid: 316: 317: - fields users normally delete immediately; 318: - mandatory empty properties; 319: - speculative metadata; 320: - automatic historical backfill; 321: - mass rewriting of existing files; 322: - metadata that exists only to satisfy a future hypothetical feature. 323: 324: Default Journal and Concept starters should remain minimal. 325: 326: Additional fields should be introduced through specialized templates or later workflows rather than placed in every new document. 327: 328: --- 329: 330: ## 10. Automate Only at Stable Boundaries 331: 332: Automation should happen at deliberate and understandable transaction points. 333: 334: Preferred automation boundaries include: 335: 336: - physical Save; 337: - explicit Generate; 338: - explicit Reconcile; 339: - explicit Archive; 340: - explicit status transition; 341: - explicit workspace refresh; 342: - explicit import or export. 343: 344: Avoid surprising structural mutation during ordinary typing. 345: 346: Draft auto-save should not silently perform operations intended for physical document persistence. 347: 348: When automation changes source information, its owner, trigger, result, and failure behavior must be clear. 349: 350: --- 351: 352: ## 11. Preserve Ambiguity Instead of Inventing Certainty 353: 354: MarkmapEditor should not guess when identity, ownership, mapping, or source location cannot be established safely. 355: 356: When information is ambiguous: 357: 358: - preserve the original source; 359: - avoid destructive mutation; 360: - avoid silently selecting one possible interpretation; 361: - expose the limitation when useful; 362: - request architecture review when the ambiguity affects a contract; 363: - defer richer identity systems until usage justifies them. 364: 365: Conservative behavior is preferred over apparently intelligent but unreliable automation. 366: 367: An honest limitation is better than incorrect certainty. 368: 369: --- 370: 371: ## 12. Visual Outputs Remain Reproducible 372: 373: Whenever practical, visual outputs should remain explainable and reproducible from their canonical information. 374: 375: Examples: 376: 377: - Markmap is rendered from Markdown; 378: - HTML Preview is rendered from Markdown; 379: - Task Board consumes normalized Tasks; 380: - Reports are generated as Markdown; 381: - Draw.io reconciliation consumes the Report Dictionary and a selected template; 382: - Mermaid diagrams remain embedded in Markdown; 383: - future Graph Views should consume established relationships rather than create an unrelated graph database by default. 384: 385: A visual representation may maintain temporary interaction state, but that state must not silently replace the canonical content. 386: 387: --- 388: 389: ## 13. Complete Thin Workflows Before Expanding Them 390: 391: Prefer an end-to-end thin workflow over an incomplete rich system. 392: 393: Use this sequence: 394: 395: finish the smallest useful workflow 396: -> validate it with real usage 397: -> document limitations 398: -> create a stable checkpoint 399: -> improve it in a later PLAN and ACT package 400: 401: Do not redesign a locked workflow in the middle of implementation unless the approved path is technically impossible or would violate an established architecture contract. 402: 403: Potential improvements should be recorded without automatically expanding the current ACT scope. 404: 405: --- 406: 407: ## 14. Real Usage Decides Future Complexity 408: 409: Future possibilities may be documented or reserved, but they are not current requirements. 410: 411: Examples of intentionally conditional directions include: 412: 413: - Full Task Manager; 414: - Full Projects Mode; 415: - Gantt views; 416: - Graph View; 417: - advanced Groups behavior; 418: - global filtering systems; 419: - automated intelligent grouping; 420: - template libraries and template versioning; 421: - Mermaid visual editing; 422: - advanced Project hierarchies; 423: - multiple reporting data stores; 424: - extensive presentation-template systems. 425: 426: These should be implemented only when real usage demonstrates that the simpler workflow is insufficient. 427: 428: Future compatibility should normally be preserved through clean ownership and data contracts, not through premature feature implementation. 429: 430: --- 431: 432: ## 15. Groups Are Optional Scope, Not a Replacement Structure 433: 434: Groups should remain an optional organizational layer. 435: 436: Groups are not automatically: 437: 438: - tags; 439: - folders; 440: - workspaces; 441: - document types; 442: - mandatory classifications. 443: 444: Their primary purpose is to provide optional scope, filtering, and aggregation. 445: 446: Initial Group integration should favor focused views such as: 447: 448: - Task Board; 449: - Project Quick View; 450: - Report setup; 451: - Search; 452: - future knowledge exploration. 453: 454: Groups should not introduce hidden global filtering that makes application state difficult to understand. 455: 456: Group behavior must follow the established metadata architecture before broad integration begins. 457: 458: --- 459: 460: ## 16. Projects Should Grow Progressively 461: 462: Projects should begin with fast Markdown discovery. 463: 464: The minimum valid Project is a Project name. 465: 466: Additional fields may remain optional, including: 467: 468: - period; 469: - value; 470: - currency; 471: - status; 472: - delivery information; 473: - billing information; 474: - Group; 475: - parent or subproject relationships. 476: 477: The preferred progression is: 478: 479: Markdown Project capture 480: -> Workspace Index discovery 481: -> lightweight Sidebar view 482: -> Project Quick View 483: -> richer Projects Mode only if justified 484: 485: Archive should normally be preferred over deletion. 486: 487: Parent Projects should remain the primary objects in the Sidebar, Journal aggregation, and default Workspace Index. 488: 489: Subprojects should remain compact and subordinate unless a focused view requires them. 490: 491: --- 492: 493: ## 17. Tasks Should Remain Easy to Create 494: 495: A normal Markdown checkbox is sufficient to create a basic Task. 496: 497: Task metadata may enrich lifecycle behavior, but it must not make ordinary Task capture difficult. 498: 499: The Task information model should remain: 500: 501: Markdown Task 502: -> Task lifecycle owner 503: -> Workspace Index 504: -> TaskReview 505: -> Task Board 506: -> explicit source mutation 507: -> physical Save 508: -> index refresh 509: 510: The Task Board is a consumer of Task lifecycle rules. 511: 512: It must not create a competing lifecycle implementation. 513: 514: Completion metadata, dates, and future enriched fields should remain conservative and compatible with simple checkbox completion. 515: 516: A future Full Task Manager remains optional and must be justified by usage. 517: 518: --- 519: 520: ## 18. Reports Remain Markdown First 521: 522: The automatic Markdown report is the core reporting output. 523: 524: The preferred reporting flow is: 525: 526: Workspace information 527: -> Report setup 528: -> generated unsaved Markdown 529: -> user review and editing 530: -> optional Save 531: -> Report Dictionary 532: -> optional Draw.io reconciliation 533: -> rich visual output 534: 535: HTML and Draw.io provide richer presentation and finishing experiences. 536: 537: They should consume the same underlying report information rather than create a separate reporting truth. 538: 539: Partial reconciliation is acceptable. 540: 541: Unknown placeholders, unmatched fields, and missing values should remain visible and recoverable rather than being silently discarded. 542: 543: --- 544: 545: ## 19. Mermaid Should Begin as a Markdown-Native Capability 546: 547: Mermaid should initially be implemented as a Markdown-native feature. 548: 549: Initial goals may include: 550: 551: - fenced Mermaid syntax; 552: - HTML Preview rendering; 553: - Markmap integration where technically appropriate; 554: - report diagrams; 555: - Project flows; 556: - future local relationship visualization. 557: 558: Do not initially create: 559: 560: - a complex dedicated Mermaid module; 561: - a separate diagram data store; 562: - an elaborate visual Mermaid editor; 563: - extensive configuration systems. 564: 565: Mermaid may later support Graph View or knowledge exploration, but this future possibility does not require an early graph subsystem. 566: 567: --- 568: 569: ## 20. UI Consistency Should Not Create Unnecessary Features 570: 571: Reuse established interaction and visual patterns when doing so improves understanding. 572: 573: Do not add a control, mode, toolbar, preference, or local state merely because another experience has one. 574: 575: Prefer: 576: 577: - existing application controls; 578: - shared global preferences; 579: - established overlay behavior; 580: - consistent icon treatment; 581: - familiar navigation; 582: - responsive behavior based on capability and available space. 583: 584: A shared global control should remain globally owned. 585: 586: A focused view should consume global Theme, Compact, and other application states rather than duplicate them locally unless a separate local setting has a proven purpose. 587: 588: --- 589: 590: ## 21. Desktop and DeX Are Primary, Without Blocking Other Devices 591: 592: Desktop and desktop-like DeX usage are primary interaction targets. 593: 594: Responsive behavior should use available width, height, pointer capability, and other reliable browser characteristics rather than fragile device detection. 595: 596: Touch targets should remain usable where coarse pointers are present. 597: 598: Narrow and short viewports should retain access to essential actions and content. 599: 600: Mobile support should remain practical and progressive without forcing a large separate mobile architecture unless real usage requires it. 601: 602: --- 603: 604: ## 22. Explicit Exclusions Protect Simplicity 605: 606: Architecture and PLAN documents should state what is out of scope. 607: 608: An exclusion is not a product failure. 609: 610: It protects the current workflow from uncontrolled expansion and helps future contributors understand whether an absence is deliberate. 611: 612: Typical exclusions may include: 613: 614: - unrelated feature redesign; 615: - new persistence layers; 616: - broad metadata migration; 617: - historical backfill; 618: - new Full Modes; 619: - new template-management systems; 620: - global filtering; 621: - duplicate scanning; 622: - speculative integrations. 623: 624: Deferred ideas should be recorded in the roadmap rather than inserted into the current ACT. 625: 626: --- 627: 628: ## 23. Development Must Follow PLAN and ACT Separation 629: 630: Product simplicity depends on disciplined implementation. 631: 632: Every implementation package must follow the process defined in: 633: 634: `docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md` 635: 636: The expected lifecycle is: 637: 638: PLAN 639: -> plan review 640: -> explicit ACT authorization 641: -> implementation 642: -> static validation 643: -> browser validation 644: -> final report 645: -> stable checkpoint 646: 647: PLAN must inspect the actual current repository. 648: 649: It must not assume that an earlier prompt, handoff, roadmap, or repository snapshot still represents the current source. 650: 651: ACT must remain inside the approved boundaries. 652: 653: A direct ACT is allowed only when the user explicitly overrides the normal workflow. 654: 655: --- 656: 657: ## 24. Development Agents Must Inspect Before Assuming 658: 659: Before proposing or implementing a change, the development agent should inspect: 660: 661: - current branch; 662: - current repository status; 663: - uncommitted and untracked files; 664: - workflow documents; 665: - environment instructions; 666: - relevant architecture documents; 667: - actual source owners; 668: - loading order; 669: - persistence boundaries; 670: - current runtime evidence; 671: - applicable validators and acceptance requirements. 672: 673: Repository source and verified runtime evidence take priority over assumptions from earlier conversations. 674: 675: If the source, runtime evidence, and architecture disagree, the agent must reconcile them during PLAN. 676: 677: --- 678: 679: ## 25. Every PLAN Must Pass the Product Decision Filter 680: 681: Before a package is ready for ACT, its PLAN should answer: 682: 683: 1. What user problem is being solved? 684: 2. What is the smallest complete solution? 685: 3. What is the canonical source of the information? 686: 4. Which existing owner should handle each responsibility? 687: 5. What existing shared state, event, or workflow can be reused? 688: 6. Does the proposal create another source of truth? 689: 7. Can the information flow be explained clearly? 690: 8. Is any complexity being added only for hypothetical future use? 691: 9. Which behavior is explicitly out of scope? 692: 10. What current files and hunks must be protected? 693: 11. How will static and browser behavior be validated? 694: 12. What stable checkpoint closes the package? 695: 696: If the proposed solution cannot answer these questions clearly, it is not ready for ACT. 697: 698: --- 699: 700: ## 26. Architecture Review Triggers 701: 702: A package should return to architecture review when it would: 703: 704: - change the canonical source of information; 705: - create a new persistent state owner; 706: - duplicate an existing domain owner; 707: - change a public module contract; 708: - alter physical Save boundaries; 709: - alter Workspace Index ownership; 710: - introduce automatic source mutation at a new boundary; 711: - add broad metadata migration or backfill; 712: - establish a new Full Mode; 713: - create a new global filtering layer; 714: - make an optional workflow mandatory; 715: - introduce synchronization between competing sources of truth; 716: - make the information flow difficult to explain. 717: 718: Small CSS, presentation, or local interaction changes do not automatically require architecture review when existing ownership and state contracts remain unchanged. 719: 720: They still require the normal PLAN and ACT workflow unless explicitly overridden. 721: 722: --- 723: 724: ## 27. Documentation Should Remain Layered and Maintainable 725: 726: Do not copy every product principle into every architecture document. 727: 728: Use concise cross-references. 729: 730: The intended documentation hierarchy is: 731: 732: Product principles 733: -> stable decision framework 734: 735: Development workflow 736: -> implementation process 737: 738: Development environment 739: -> execution constraints 740: 741: Architecture documents 742: -> subsystem-specific authority 743: 744: Roadmap 745: -> current and future package order 746: 747: PLAN handoffs 748: -> current source-grounded implementation proposal 749: 750: Completion reports 751: -> evidence and checkpoint status 752: 753: Architecture documents should remain authoritative for their specific subsystems. 754: 755: Historical handoffs should normally remain unchanged as records of the decision state at that time. 756: 757: The roadmap may evolve frequently. 758: 759: Product principles should change only when the long-term product philosophy changes. 760: 761: --- 762: 763: ## 28. Definition of a Good MarkmapEditor Change 764: 765: A good change: 766: 767: - solves a real user problem; 768: - is understandable; 769: - fits the existing information flow; 770: - has clear ownership; Templates beginning with a standard XML declaration (`<?xml version="1.0" ... ?>`) and optional UTF-8 BOM are accepted; compressed Draw.io payloads are detected and rejected. 28: 29: **Generate Draw.io** supports intentional partial generation: matched values are populated, and any unresolved placeholders (missing values, unknown template placeholders) remain visible in the output for later completion — as long as at least one matched field has a value. Identity and classification contract 61: 62: | Concept | Meaning | Physical effect | 63: | --- | --- | --- | 64: | Note | `.md` document in `notes/`; no metadata = normal Note | File in `notes/` | 65: | Today | Shortcut that opens or creates the single daily Note | Initial filename `YYYY-MM-DD.md` | 66: | Named Note | Shortcut creating a Note with a chosen name | Filename defined at creation | 67: | Knowledge | Optional reversible classification | Metadata update only; no move | 68: | Pinned | Quick-access highlight, independent of Knowledge | Metadata update only; no move | 69: | Archived | Outside active views; reachable in Archive | Metadata only; no move | 70: | Rename File | Explicit filename/path change | Separate, higher-risk flow | 71: 72: - Physical identity: handle plus proven relative path. H1 is presentation only, never a navigation key. Duplicate H1 values remain distinct. Navigation uses path/handle. 73: - Indexed H1 title changes are reflected only after Save and Index rebuild; no per-keystroke Workspace indexing. 74: - Classification keys: `date`, `knowledge`, `pinned`, `archived` (exact serialization fixed in the metadata ACT PLAN). 75: 76: --- 77: 78: ## 4. Metadata contract (YAML frontmatter) 79: 80: **Managed keys:** `date`, `knowledge`, `pinned`, `archived`. 81: 82: | Key | Supported values | Absence semantics | 83: | --- | --- | --- | 84: | `date` | ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` | Missing date = Undated (never substitute filesystem mtime silently) | 85: | `knowledge` | `true` when set | Absent = not Knowledge | 86: | `pinned` | `true` when set | Absent = not pinned | 87: | `archived` | `true` when set | Absent = active | 88: 89: Rules: 90: - False classification flags are represented by removing the managed key (a user action never writes `knowledge: false`). A manually typed `false` is read as absent and may be removed on the next managed write. 91: - Unknown frontmatter keys are always preserved verbatim; user formatting and body content are preserved where technically possible. 92: - No frontmatter present: a managed write may prepend a minimal `---` block. 93: - Malformed or unclosed frontmatter: mutators abort safely with a toast; no partial write ever remains. 94: - Insertion/update owner and physical Save owner are fixed in the metadata ACT PLAN. A dedicated frontmatter-mutator module is a RECOMMENDATION to be proven in that PLAN, not an approved file. 95: - Dirty-document policy: a metadata action on the ACTIVE note patches the editor buffer and marks the document dirty. It does NOT auto-save; user-controlled physical Save remains authoritative. 96: - Inactive-note actions are evaluated separately during the metadata ACT and are not assumed earlier. 97: - Virtual Reports are excluded from metadata actions. 98: - Actions are idempotent; permission or write failure rolls back with no partial state. 99: 100: --- 101: 102: ## 5. Creation contract 103: 104: ```text 105: [ + New Note ▾ ] 106: Today -> opens or creates the daily Note; no modal 107: Named Note... -> compact modal 108: ``` 109: 110: **Today** 111: - Local date source: local `Date` components, zero-padded (`YYYY-MM-DD`). 112: - Target: `notes/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. If it exists, open the same file; never create a duplicate and never overwrite. 113: - A new file receives starter Markdown with `date: YYYY-MM-DD` frontmatter. No `journal` type and no `journals/` folder. 114: - Respects dirty guard, Report guard, ModeSession, writable handles and navigation history. 115: - If the daily Note was physically renamed, Today creates a new file for that date (documented consequence; the Rename workflow is a separate future package). 116: 117: **Named Note modal** 118: - Fields: name; note date (defaults to local today, editable, may be cleared → Undated); Knowledge checkbox (unchecked by default); Cancel; Create Note. 119: - Filename normalization strips `[\/:*?"<>|]`, collapses whitespace and appends `.md`. 120: - Guards run BEFORE any file creation: empty name, invalid characters, filename collision (including a name resolving to `YYYY-MM-DD.md`, which collides with Today), and Cancel. 121: - Pin does NOT appear in the modal; Pin is a later, independent action. 122: - Partial-create failure rolls back (no orphan empty file, no index entry). 123: - Outside a Workspace, the simple Editor New/Open File flows keep working; the Workspace menu must never force `notes/` creation for standalone files. 124: 125: --- 126: 127: ## 6. Sidebar and view contract 128: 129: ```text 130: Workspace 131: + New Note 132: Search 133: Notes every active Note (Knowledge included) 134: Pinned top subsection; never duplicated below 135: By date Today and Named Notes grouped by note date 136: Undated no resolved date 137: Knowledge filtered view (knowledge = true) 138: Archive filtered view (archived = true) 139: Tasks / Projects / Reports / Index (existing panels, preserved) 140: ``` 141: 142: - Notes contains every active Note; Knowledge is a filtered view; Pinned is independent; archived Notes never appear in active Notes or Knowledge. 143: - Restore preserves date, Knowledge and Pin. 144: - Duplicate H1 values remain distinct; navigation uses path/handle, never H1. 145: - Journal chronology is not reproduced as a separate physical kind. 146: - **Library decision:** do NOT create a separate Library list alongside Notes. The Sidebar area is the navigation host; `Notes` is the single all-active list. Avoid redundant lists showing the same content without a clear purpose. 147: 148: --- 149: 150: ## 7. Corrected execution sequence (each ACT is a review boundary) 151: 152: ```text 153: ACT 0 Documentation adoption & working-tree reconciliation [AUTHORIZED - executed] 154: ACT 1A Workspace format detection ONLY (strict read-only) [AUTHORIZED NEXT - not started] 155: ACT 1B folders.notes / files.notes + explicit init + notes/ scanner 156: ACT 1C Single Workspace Index over notes/ 157: ACT 2A Consumer preservation: Search, Related, Tags, Wiki Links 158: ACT 2B Consumer preservation: Task Review, Task Board, current Projects discovery 159: ACT 2C Consumer preservation: Reports, Draw.io, Navigation History, 160: Hot Reload, Save, Save As 161: -------- STRUCTURAL CHECKPOINT (browser accepted) -------- 162: -------- MANUAL MIGRATION CHECKPOINT (owner reorganizes) -------- 163: ACT 3A Unified creation flow (+ New Note: Today / Named Note modal) 164: ACT 3B Sidebar views: Notes / Pinned / date groups / Undated / Knowledge / Archive 165: ACT 4 Metadata actions on the active Note (buffer patch + dirty; no auto-save) 166: ACT 5 Timeline grouping + optional Workspace experience; Journal parity decision 167: 6A-6E Independent packages: Tasks; Projects parser; Project metadata; 168: Projects Expanded View; Quick Report + Draw.io alignment; 169: final 1.0 closure and version selection 170: ``` 171: 172: ### ACT 1A — strict read-only format detection (nothing else) 173: - Detects exactly: empty folder; valid `notes/` Workspace; legacy Workspace (`journals/`/`concepts/` without `notes/`); mixed Workspace (`notes/` plus legacy folders); permission failure. 174: - Legacy and mixed folders are REJECTED as Workspaces. The rejection is blocking, read-only and non-mutating. There is no compatibility mode. Individual Markdown files remain openable through Open File. 175: - MUST NOT create `notes/` and MUST NOT call any filesystem API with `create: true`. 176: - No metadata writers, no views and no creation UI anywhere in ACT 1 or ACT 2. 177: 178: ### ACT 1B — explicit initialization and scanner 179: - Only after ACT 1A returns empty AND the owner explicitly confirms: create `notes/`, initialize `folders.notes` and `files.notes`, then execute the notes/ scanner. 180: - Never initializes from a legacy or mixed detection result. 181: 182: ### ACT 1C — single Workspace Index over notes/ 183: - The existing `buildWorkspaceIndex()` aggregates `files.notes` only. One Index; no second Workspace Index, parser or document store. 184: 185: ### ACT 2A–2C — consumer preservation only 186: - Preserve behavior of Search, Related, Tags, Wiki Links, Task Review, Task Board, current Projects discovery, Reports, Draw.io, Navigation History, Hot Reload, Save and Save As against the `notes/` sources. 187: - NO feature improvements in these phases — behavior preservation only. 188: 189: --- 190: 191: ## 8. STRUCTURAL CHECKPOINT (after ACT 2C; browser accepted) 192: 193: Passage criteria: 194: 1. The scanner discovers every Markdown file inside `notes/`. 195: 2. One `WORKSPACE_INDEX_STATE` indexes notes, tasks, tags, projects and links. 196: 3. All preserved consumers behave identically — no regression; every existing validator suite stays green plus new fixtures. 197: 4. Browser acceptance on desktop and mobile/DeX with a test `notes/` Workspace. 198: 199: No creation UI, Sidebar redesign or metadata writer starts before this checkpoint passes. 200: 201: ## 9. MANUAL MIGRATION CHECKPOINT (after structural acceptance) 202: 203: Owner process (the application performs no migration): 204: 1. Keep the old Workspace — with `journals/`, `concepts/` and `archive/` untouched — as the backup. 205: 2. Create a SEPARATE new Workspace folder. 206: 3. Create `notes/` in the new Workspace. 207: 4. Copy reviewed Markdown files into `notes/`. 208: 5. Validate filename collisions and Wiki Link targets after the copy. 209: 6. Open the new Workspace in MarkmapEditor and validate navigation, Tags, Tasks and Reports. 210: 211: Constraint: `journals/` and `concepts/` CANNOT remain inside the selected new Workspace root — the legacy structure stays only in the separate old folder. 212: 213: ## 10. Functional improvements deferred 214: 215: Search H1 matching, Sidebar redesign, creation UX, metadata actions, Timeline grouping, Journal-mode removal or rename, Project metadata, standalone Reports and the Expanded Projects View are deferred until after structural acceptance, each in its own authorized package. The ACT 2A–2C consumer-preservation phases must not improve features. 216: 217: ## 11. Projects future direction (preserved decision) 218: 219: The future Project declaration is: 220: 221: ```text 222: ## Project: Project Name 223: <ordinary Markdown content> 224: ``` 225: 226: - Do not introduce project frontmatter as an alternative primary declaration. 227: - Do not change Projects syntax during structural migration. 228: - The current `Project:` parser behavior stays untouched until the dedicated Projects parser package decides the reconciliation. 229: 230: ## 12. Version boundary 231: 232: No version, cache identity or Service Worker change occurs in ACT 0–5. The post-migration release is NOT assumed to be `1.0.0`; final version selection happens only after product acceptance, with one version/cache bump per accepted release package. 233: 234: ## 13. Acceptance and regression criteria (carry-over) 235: 236: - Today creates/opens `notes/YYYY-MM-DD.md` without duplicating or overwriting. 237: - The Knowledge checkbox classifies the same Note; unpinned/undated states are key removals. 238: - A promoted Note remains in Notes; a pinned Note never duplicates within a view; Archive exits active views; Restore preserves classification. 239: - Filename and H1 may differ; clicks use path/handle; duplicate H1s never merge records. 240: - A legacy or mixed Workspace is never modified silently; a standalone file never joins the Workspace by equal filename. 241: - Creation, metadata and Save/Save As respect dirty state, cancellation, permissions, failure, virtual Report and rollback; no action implicitly rewrites Wiki Links. 242: - Existing validators stay green; `node --check` on touched JS/CJS; `git diff --check`; desktop/mobile/dark/offline browser checkpoints. 243: 244: ## 14. The root is the folder that 14: contains `notes/`. Do not select `notes/` itself. 15: 16: Every Markdown file inside `notes/` is a **Note**. There are no separate 17: `journals/`, `concepts/` or `archive/` folders in this format. 18: 19: ## Canonical unit 20: 21: ``` 22: Markdown file -> canonical unit 23: ``` 24: 25: Notes, Knowledge, Pinned and Archive are **projections** over those same 26: physical files. They are visual reuse of one record, not file duplication. 27: 28: ## Classifications 29: 30: Classifications live in the file's YAML frontmatter. 31: 32: | Frontmatter | Effect | 33: | --- | --- | 34: | `knowledge: true` | Note also appears in Knowledge. | 35: | `pinned: true` | Note appears in Pinned. | 36: | `archived: true` | Note leaves Notes, Pinned and Knowledge, and appears in Archive. | 37: 38: ### Projection contract 39: 40: - **Notes** contains every active Note. 41: - **Knowledge** is a filtered projection over active Notes. A Knowledge Note 42: remains visible in Notes. 43: - **Pinned** is an independent classification. A Pinned Note is not repeated in 44: the dated or Undated subsection. 45: - **Archive** holds archived Notes only. Archived Notes appear in Archive and 46: not in active Notes, Pinned or Knowledge. 47: 48: ### Archive is not deletion 49: 50: An archived Note remains a physical file in `notes/`. Archive never moves, 51: renames, copies or deletes anything. Restore removes the `archived` key and the 52: Note returns to the active views. 53: 54: ## Title and physical identity 55: 56: - The **H1 heading** is the primary saved visual title. 57: - The **filename and folder path** remain the physical identity. 58: - Duplicate H1 values are supported. Two Notes with the same H1 remain separate 59: Notes, distinguished by their paths. 60: - Navigation always uses the exact path, never the title. 61: 62: ## Data scopes 63: 64: ``` 65: Current Document -> live single-document scope 66: Workspace -> optional saved aggregation 67: ``` 68: 69: Current Document reflects the live editor buffer. Workspace projections reflect 70: saved files. An unsaved change to a title or classification may not appear in 71: the Workspace views until you Save. Save rebuilds the Workspace Index. 72: 73: ## Migration from a legacy Workspace 74: 75: **There is no automatic migration.** A Workspace that still uses `journals/` or 76: `concepts/` is rejected rather than converted, and the application never 77: creates `notes/` inside such a Workspace without an explicit selection and 78: confirmation. 79: 80: ### Procedure 81: 82: 1. **Keep an untouched backup** of the original Workspace. Do not modify it. 83: 2. **Migrate a copy first.** Run the conversion against the copy, confirm the 84: result, and only then repeat it on the original. 85: 3. For each `concepts/*.md` file, add `knowledge: true` to its frontmatter. 86: 4. For each `journals/*.md` file, no frontmatter is required: a journal becomes 87: an ordinary Note. 88: 5. For items that should be archived, add `archived: true`. 89: 6. Place **all active files physically inside `notes/`** in the new Workspace. 90: 7. Open the **Workspace root**, not `notes/`. 91: 92: The conversion is frontmatter-only. It does not rewrite Markdown body content, 93: rename files, or rewrite Wiki Links. 94: 95: ## Intentional boundaries 96: 97: These are accepted design boundaries, not missing work: 98: 99: - No automatic legacy migration. 100: - No filename rename workflow. 101: - No automatic Wiki Link rewriting. 102: - No non-Markdown asset browser. 103: - No monthly calendar. 104: - No Reminders. 105: - No shared `@` attribute layer and no autocomplete. 106: - No Mermaid/Graph completion. 107: - No Reveal.js completion. 108: - No Journal-mode removal (the application context mode is still internally 109: named `journal`). 1: // @ts-nocheck 2: // ================================ 3: // PWA diagnostics + service worker registration 4: // Uses existing log() panel through pwaDebugLog() 5: // ================================ 6: 7: async function pwaFetchCheck(url, label) { 8: try { 9: const res = await fetch(url, { cache: 'no-store' }); 10: const contentType = res.headers.get('content-type') || ''; 11: 12: if (res.ok) { 13: pwaDebugLog(`✅ ${label} reachable`, { 14: url, 15: status: res.status, 16: contentType, 17: }); 18: } else { 19: pwaDebugLog(`❌ ${label} failed`, { 20: url, 21: status: res.status, 22: statusText: res.statusText, 23: contentType, 24: }); 25: } 26: 27: return res; 28: } catch (err) { 29: pwaDebugLog(`❌ ${label} fetch error`, { 30: url, 31: error: String(err), 32: }); 33: return null; 34: } 35: } 36: 37: function pwaImageCheck(url, label) { 38: return new Promise((resolve) => { 39: const img = new Image(); 40: 41: img.onload = () => { 42: pwaDebugLog(`✅ ${label} image loaded`, { 43: url, 44: width: img.naturalWidth, 45: height: img.naturalHeight, 46: }); 47: resolve(true); 48: }; 49: 50: img.onerror = () => { 51: pwaDebugLog(`❌ ${label} image failed to load`, { url }); 52: resolve(false); 53: }; 54: 55: img.src = url + (url.includes('?') ? Product objective 15: 16: Make MarkmapEditor easier for new users to understand without turning it into a 17: generic note-taking, block-editing or database application. 18: 19: Preserve the product direction: 20: 21: - Markdown is the source. 22: - Markmap is the structure. 23: - Current Document is the focus. 24: - File Knowledge explains the active document. 25: - Workspace Knowledge connects the Workspace. 26: - Derived views make source files actionable. 27: 28: --- 29: 30: ## 2. Sidebar behavioral model 31: 32: Formalize three layers. 33: 34: ### CURRENT DOCUMENT 35: 36: Owns: 37: 38: - active document identity; 39: - title; 40: - Workspace-relative path where relevant; 41: - Edit/Read representation control; 42: - source access; 43: - Quick Actions; 44: - compact/expanded state. 45: 46: The essential identity and Edit/Read control should not disappear completely. 47: 48: Current Document may later support a focused single-file experience when 49: expanded, without reviving a separate Standalone architecture. 50: 51: ### FILE KNOWLEDGE 52: 53: Contains document-scoped cards: 54: 55: - Open Tasks; 56: - Done Tasks; 57: - Links In; 58: - Links Out; 59: - Projects; 60: - future Reminders; 61: - future Highlights. 62: 63: File Knowledge is not a general search surface. 64: 65: Selecting a card exposes a source-scoped list. 66: Selecting an item navigates to the exact source location when available. 67: 68: Only one contextual list should need to expand at a time. 69: 70: ### WORKSPACE KNOWLEDGE 71: 72: Contains: 73: 74: - Workspace Search; 75: - Notes; 76: - Knowledge; 77: - Archive; 78: - Tasks; 79: - Projects; 80: - Tags; 81: - Workspace Index; 82: - future Reminders; 83: - future Highlights. 84: 85: Workspace Search remains exclusively Workspace-scoped. 86: 87: Do not place Workspace Search inside File Knowledge. 88: 89: --- 90: 91: ## 3. Search ownership 92: 93: Document: 94: 95: - CodeMirror Find searches active Markdown source; 96: - Markmap search handles headings/structure; 97: - Workspace Search searches indexed Workspace content; 98: - Read/HTML search remains an open design question. 99: 100: Do not assume the first Edit/Read implementation requires a dedicated Read 101: search. 102: 103: --- 104: 105: ## 4. Document Surface 106: 107: Formalize: 108: 109: Document Surface 110: - Edit; 111: - Read. 112: 113: Edit uses the existing CodeMirror owner. 114: 115: Read uses the existing synchronized HTML renderer. 116: 117: Edit and Read are representations of the same active source. 118: 119: Switching must not: 120: 121: - Save; 122: - reopen the source; 123: - rebuild the Workspace Index; 124: - change active source; 125: - discard drafts; 126: - clear undo/redo. 127: 128: Preserve independently: 129: 130: - Editor cursor; 131: - Editor selection; 132: - Editor scroll; 133: - Read scroll; 134: - dirty state; 135: - writable handle; 136: - Sidebar context; 137: - Markmap zoom/pan. 138: 139: --- 140: 141: ## 5. Structure Surface 142: 143: Markmap remains first-class. 144: 145: Markmap must not become a hidden secondary plugin-like feature. 146: 147: Reassess: 148: 149: - Document + Markmap; 150: - Full Editor; 151: - Full Read; 152: - Full Markmap; 153: - advanced multi-panel desktop layouts. 154: 155: The current four-panel possibility may remain available, but it should not 156: automatically define the primary user experience. 157: 158: --- 159: 160: ## 6.
