11: - repository investigation; 12: - continuation inside the same AI conversation; 13: - incremental instructions; 14: - conditions for starting a new conversation; 15: - source-editing boundaries; 16: - command lifecycle; 17: - validation; 18: - browser evidence; 19: - handoff and completion reports; 20: - mandatory session entry and authority precedence; 21: - model/context-compaction handoff and AI-state lifecycle; 22: - validation tiers, owner-based test selection and mutation-control 23: isolation. 24: 25: Environment-specific instructions are defined separately in: 26: 27: docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md 28: 29: AI coding agents must read that document before using shell tooling. 30: 31: This workflow does not authorize a particular feature implementation. 32: Each work package must still define its own approved scope and file boundaries. 33: 34: --- 35: 36: ## 1. Core Workflow 37: 38: Every implementation package must follow this sequence: 39: 40: PLAN 41: → plan review 42: → explicit ACT authorization 43: → implementation 44: → static validation 45: → browser validation 46: → final report 47: → stable checkpoint 48: 49: Do not skip PLAN because a correction appears simple. 50: 51: Small corrections can still affect: 52: 53: - files with existing uncommitted work; 54: - shared lifecycle code; 55: - event listeners; 56: - render scheduling; 57: - persistence; 58: - workspace indexing; 59: - CodeMirror extensions; 60: - service-worker behavior; 61: - unrelated features in the same file. 62: 63: A direct ACT is allowed only when the user explicitly overrides this workflow. 64: 65: Absent an explicit override, PLAN is mandatory. 66: 67: --- 68: 69: ## 2. PLAN Mode 70: 71: PLAN is an investigation and design phase. 72: 73: During PLAN, the agent must: 74: 75: 1. Inspect the current repository state. 76: 2. Identify existing uncommitted changes. 77: 3. Determine ownership of each changed file and hunk. 78: 4. Inspect the actual current source. 79: 5. Compare runtime evidence with source behavior. 80: 6. Identify the root cause or the evidence still missing. 81: 7. Define the narrowest safe implementation. 82: 8. Define allowed and protected files. 83: 9. Define static and browser validation. 84: 10. Produce a structured PLAN handoff. 85: 11. Stop without editing production source. 86: 87: PLAN must not: 88: 89: - edit production source; 90: - reconstruct files; 91: - run broad replacements; 92: - run automatic formatting; 93: - install packages; 94: - update documentation unless documentation is the task; 95: - commit; 96: - push; 97: - switch itself to ACT. 98: 99: The agent must not treat an apparent one-line fix as authorization to edit. 100: 101: --- 102: 103: ## 3. PLAN Handoff 104: 105: Every PLAN must produce a repository-specific handoff containing, as applicable: 106: 107: - branch; 108: - working-tree state; 109: - changed files; 110: - ownership of existing changes; 111: - protected files; 112: - runtime evidence; 113: - confirmed root cause; 114: - unresolved questions; 115: - architecture ownership; 116: - exact functions and selectors involved; 117: - selected implementation scope; 118: - files allowed in ACT; 119: - files excluded from ACT; 120: - commands allowed in ACT; 121: - prohibited commands; 122: - static validation; 123: - browser validation; 124: - regression checks; 125: - risks and mitigations; 126: - deferred work; 127: - ordered ACT sequence; 128: - explicit PLAN status. 129: 130: The PLAN status must clearly indicate one of these conditions: 131: 132: - ready for review; 133: - partial because evidence is still missing; 134: - blocked because source or ownership cannot be safely verified. 135: 136: The agent must stop after the PLAN handoff. 137: 138: --- 139: 140: ## 4. Plan Review 141: 142: The PLAN handoff is reviewed before implementation. 143: 144: The reviewer may: 145: 146: - approve it; 147: - correct technical assumptions; 148: - narrow the file scope; 149: - request additional evidence; 150: - change validation requirements; 151: - reject speculative changes; 152: - preserve or defer parts of the proposal. 153: 154: Reviewer corrections become part of the existing PLAN context. 155: 156: The agent must not begin ACT until the user explicitly changes the mode. 157: 158: --- 159: 160: ## 5. ACT Authorization 161: 162: ACT begins only with an explicit instruction such as: 163: 164: CURRENT MODE: ACT 165: 166: Implement the approved PLAN handoff already present in this conversation. 167: 168: When ACT begins, the agent must: 169: 170: 1. Recheck repository status. 171: 2. Confirm that relevant source has not materially changed since PLAN. 172: 3. Use the approved handoff already present in context. 173: 4. Apply reviewer corrections. 174: 5. Implement only approved changes. 175: 6. Preserve existing uncommitted work. 176: 7. Validate every changed file. 177: 8. Inspect the complete final diff. 178: 9. Perform available browser tests. 179: 10. Report anything not tested as pending. 180: 181: The agent must not repeat the entire PLAN unless: 182: 183: - the repository materially changed; 184: - the relevant source changed after PLAN; 185: - the user started a new conversation; 186: - the active work package changed; 187: - the previous handoff is no longer reliable. 188: 189: --- 190: 191: ## 6. Same-Conversation Continuity 192: 193: When work continues in the same Cline or Roo Code conversation, the agent should 194: retain and reuse the existing context. 195: 196: Previously established information remains active unless explicitly changed, 197: including: 198: 199: - repository safety rules; 200: - environment constraints; 201: - approved PLAN; 202: - file ownership; 203: - allowed files; 204: - protected files; 205: - tool lifecycle; 206: - permitted commands; 207: - prohibited commands; 208: - runtime evidence; 209: - validation requirements; 210: - deferred work; 211: - final-status vocabulary. 212: 213: Incremental instructions should not unnecessarily repeat the entire original 214: prompt. 215: 216: A continuation instruction may use a compact form such as: 217: 218: CURRENT MODE: PLAN 219: 220: Add the new runtime evidence to the existing investigation. 221: 222: Retain all previously established: 223: 224: - repository-safety rules; 225: - file boundaries; 226: - Termux environment requirements; 227: - tool-lifecycle safeguards; 228: - validation requirements; 229: - deferred scope; 230: - PLAN → review → ACT workflow. 231: 232: Do not repeat completed investigation. 233: Update only the affected sections of the existing PLAN handoff. 234: 235: Similarly, an ACT transition may use: 236: 237: CURRENT MODE: ACT 238: 239: Implement the approved PLAN handoff already present in this conversation. 240: 241: Apply the reviewer corrections below. 242: 243: Retain all previously established: 244: 245: - environment rules; 246: - repository-safety rules; 247: - file boundaries; 248: - tool-lifecycle safeguards; 249: - validation requirements; 250: - deferred scope. 251: 252: Do not repeat the complete audit. 253: Do not broaden the implementation. 254: 255: --- 256: 257: ## 7. When Commands Must Be Repeated 258: 259: Commands already executed in the same conversation do not need to be repeated 260: without a reason. 261: 262: A command should be rerun when: 263: 264: - source files changed after its previous execution; 265: - the working tree changed; 266: - its previous result is no longer current; 267: - a new ACT phase begins; 268: - fresh validation is required; 269: - the previous command failed; 270: - the previous output was incomplete; 271: - the command validates the final implementation; 272: - the agent cannot prove that the earlier result still applies. 273: 274: Examples that normally require fresh execution before or after edits: 275: 276: git status --short 277: git diff --check 278: git diff --stat 279: git diff -- APPROVED_FILE 280: node --check CHANGED_FILE 281: 282: A repository search or source inspection does not need to be repeated merely to 283: restate a finding that remains valid. 284: 285: --- 286: 287: ## 8. When to Start a New AI Conversation 288: 289: Continue in the existing conversation while: 290: 291: - the same work package is active; 292: - the existing PLAN remains relevant; 293: - file ownership remains stable; 294: - the repository has not reached a clean package boundary; 295: - the conversation remains internally consistent; 296: - the agent remembers and obeys the established constraints. 297: 298: Start a new conversation when one or more of these conditions apply: 299: 300: 1. The current work package is complete and validated. 301: 2. The next task belongs to a substantially different feature or architecture. 302: 3. The repository reached a stable committed checkpoint. 303: 4. The existing conversation contains too many superseded plans. 304: 5. Conflicting instructions are causing agent confusion. 305: 6. The agent repeatedly forgets file boundaries or safety rules. 306: 7. The agent attempts to repeat completed implementation. 307: 8. Tool failures or partial edits have polluted the working context. 308: 9. A new Repomix bundle materially replaces the previous repository picture. 309: 10. The next task requires a new full architecture audit. 310: 11. The current conversation is too large for reliable context retention. 311: 12. The user, reviewer, or coding agent explicitly requests a clean context. 312: 313: The reviewer should explicitly tell the user when a new conversation is 314: recommended. 315: 316: --- 317: 318: ## 9. New-Conversation Bootstrap 319: 320: A new AI conversation must receive a complete standalone prompt. 321: 322: Do not assume the new conversation remembers anything from an earlier session. 323: 324: The bootstrap must include: 325: 326: - project name and purpose; 327: - development environment; 328: - instruction to read docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md; 329: - instruction to read this workflow document; 330: - current branch; 331: - expected working-tree state; 332: - last stable checkpoint; 333: - completed features; 334: - current feature package; 335: - confirmed runtime evidence; 336: - known defects; 337: - current repository architecture; 338: - file ownership; 339: - protected files; 340: - PLAN requirements; 341: - safe commands; 342: - prohibited commands; 343: - tool-failure lifecycle; 344: - validation requirements; 345: - deferred work; 346: - required PLAN handoff; 347: - future ACT contract; 348: - allowed final statuses. 349: 350: A new conversation begins in PLAN unless explicitly stated otherwise. 351: 352: --- 353: 354: ## 10. Repository Safety 355: 356: Before editing, the agent must inspect: 357: 358: git branch --show-current 359: git status --short 360: git diff --stat 361: git diff --check 362: git diff --name-only 363: 364: The agent must distinguish among: 365: 366: - changes belonging to the current work package; 367: - changes belonging to another active package; 368: - previous completed but uncommitted changes; 369: - investigation-only logs; 370: - unrelated user changes; 371: - unknown changes. 372: 373: Unknown changes must be preserved. 374: 375: The agent must not use the following without explicit authorization: 376: 377: git reset 378: git restore 379: git checkout -- FILE 380: git clean 381: git stash 382: git rebase 383: rm on repository source 384: automatic formatting 385: automatic lint fixes 386: complete-file reconstruction 387: broad source replacement 388: 389: The agent must not discard or overwrite user work to simplify implementation. 390: 391: --- 392: 393: ## 11. File and Hunk Ownership 394: 395: Every work package must identify: 396: 397: - primary files; 398: - supporting files; 399: - protected files; 400: - exact functions, selectors, or source regions; 401: - allowed runtime behavior changes; 402: - behavior that must remain unchanged. 403: 404: Authorization to edit one function is not authorization to refactor the entire 405: file. 406: 407: Authorization to edit one file is not authorization to modify adjacent modules. 408: 409: If implementation requires an unapproved file, the agent must stop and report: 410: 411: BOUNDARY BLOCKED — CURRENT FIX REQUIRES OUT-OF-SCOPE FILE 412: 413: The agent must not silently broaden scope. 414: 415: --- 416: 417: ## 12. Editing Method 418: 419: Edits must be: 420: 421: - focused; 422: - incremental; 423: - based on inspected current source; 424: - limited to approved hunks; 425: - easy to audit through Git diff; 426: - compatible with existing architecture. 427: 428: Preferred sequence: 429: 430: 1. Locate the exact symbol with rg. 431: 2. Inspect the surrounding code with sed. 432: 3. Confirm ownership and current diff. 433: 4. Make the smallest justified edit. 434: 5. Inspect git diff for that file. 435: 6. Run syntax validation. 436: 7. Continue only if the result is correct. 437: 438: Do not rewrite complete files. 439: 440: Do not reconstruct a file from remembered or previously supplied content. 441: 442: Do not use an old Repomix snapshot as replacement source. 443: 444: The checked-out repository is the source of truth. 445: 446: --- 447: 448: ## 13. Guarded Automated Edits 449: 450: A small script may be used for an exact replacement during ACT only when: 451: 452: - the approved old block is copied from the current checkout; 453: - the script requires exactly one match; 454: - zero matches stop without writing; 455: - multiple matches stop without writing; 456: - the replacement affects only the approved hunk; 457: - the final Git diff is inspected. 458: 459: An automated edit must not: 460: 461: - perform a broad regular-expression rewrite; 462: - reconstruct a complete file; 463: - normalize unrelated whitespace; 464: - format unrelated code; 465: - silently continue after a match-count mismatch. 466: 467: --- 468: 469: ## 14. Termux Command Rules 470: 471: All shell work must follow: 472: 473: docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md 474: 475: In particular: 476: 477: - use commands through PATH; 478: - do not hardcode conventional Linux binary paths; 479: - prefer rg for search; 480: - prefer sed for bounded inspection; 481: - prefer git diff and git status for verification; 482: - check undocumented commands with command -v; 483: - do not install packages without authorization; 484: - classify malformed tool calls as agent/tool errors, not missing commands; 485: - account for native Android Termux and aarch64; 486: - avoid unnecessarily expensive repository operations. 487: 488: --- 489: 490: ## 15. Tool Lifecycle 491: 492: Every tool call must be completed or explicitly classified. 493: 494: The agent must not leave unresolved tool-call identifiers. 495: 496: If a tool invocation fails: 497: 498: 1. Determine whether it was: 499: - malformed tool invocation; 500: - missing command; 501: - command error; 502: - permission/path error; 503: - source validation failure; 504: - provider/quota failure. 505: 2. Retry at most once with a materially corrected or simpler call. 506: 3. Do not repeat the identical failed invocation. 507: 4. Do not modify source because an AI tool call was malformed. 508: 5. Do not install software merely because an invocation was malformed. 509: 6. Stop and report TOOL BLOCKED if the required tool path remains unavailable. 510: 511: No stdout does not automatically mean failure. 512: 513: Commands such as file writes, mkdir, mv, or successful checks may produce no 514: output. 515: 516: Verify results through: 517: 518: git status --short 519: git diff -- FILE 520: sed -n 521: rg 522: ls or find where appropriate 523: 524: Do not claim a command passed without evidence. 525: 526: --- 527: 528: ## 16. Investigation Discipline 529: 530: Investigation should progressively narrow the problem. 531: 532: Preferred pattern: 533: 534: runtime evidence 535: → relevant symbol search 536: → bounded source inspection 537: → call-path inspection 538: → hypothesis 539: → targeted supporting evidence 540: → PLAN decision 541: 542: Avoid: 543: 544: - repeatedly dumping entire large files; 545: - scanning every directory without a reason; 546: - repeating previously completed searches; 547: - presenting speculation as root cause; 548: - making source changes merely to collect broad logs; 549: - leaving permanent high-volume tracing enabled. 550: 551: Temporary diagnostics must be: 552: 553: - narrowly scoped; 554: - recognizable; 555: - removable or flag-controlled; 556: - reviewed after use; 557: - excluded from normal operation when no longer needed. 558: 559: --- 560: 561: ## 17. Runtime Evidence 562: 563: Runtime logs must be interpreted carefully. 564: 565: A log that a refresh was requested does not prove that the refresh executed. 566: 567: A log that a target resolved does not prove that the target opened successfully. 568: 569: A downstream exception must not automatically be classified as failure of every 570: earlier operation. 571: 572: The agent should distinguish: 573: 574: - request; 575: - start; 576: - successful commit point; 577: - completion; 578: - cancellation; 579: - no-op; 580: - failure; 581: - downstream failure. 582: 583: Recommended diagnostic pattern: 584: 585: Feature: operation requested 586: Feature: operation begin 587: Feature: intermediate state 588: Feature: operation committed 589: Feature: operation complete 590: 591: Errors should identify the owning stage. 592: 593: --- 594: 595: ## 18. Static Validation 596: 597: Every ACT package must define validation appropriate to its files. 598: 599: Typical checks include: 600: 601: node --check CHANGED_CLASSIC_JS_FILE 602: npx tsc --noEmit 603: git diff --check 604: git diff --stat 605: git diff -- CHANGED_FILE 606: 607: Do not install packages merely to run an optional validation command. 608: 609: Separate: 610: 611: - validation failures introduced by the current change; 612: - pre-existing validation failures; 613: - environment/tool limitations; 614: - browser-only behavior. 615: 616: The complete final diff must be inspected before reporting completion. 617: 618: --- 619: 620: ## 19. Browser Validation 621: 622: Browser behavior must not be marked as passed based only on source inspection. 623: 624: The agent must distinguish: 625: 626: - source complete; 627: - static validation passed; 628: - browser tests required; 629: - browser test passed; 630: - browser test failed; 631: - browser test blocked. 632: 633: Each work package should define concrete browser tests. 634: 635: Relevant evidence may include: 636: 637: - startup logs; 638: - successful listener wiring; 639: - exact action logs; 640: - state mutation; 641: - persistence; 642: - index changes; 643: - visual behavior; 644: - navigation; 645: - absence of duplicate actions; 646: - absence of uncaught errors; 647: - PWA/cache behavior. 648: 649: A test not performed must be reported as pending. 650: 651: --- 652: 653: ## 20. Performance Work 654: 655: Do not optimize performance based only on perceived delay. 656: 657: Before optimization, collect evidence such as: 658: 659: - operation start; 660: - operation end; 661: - duration; 662: - invocation count; 663: - scheduling reason; 664: - replacement of pending work; 665: - concurrent/in-progress state; 666: - result size. 667: 668: Do not add: 669: 670: - caching; 671: - memoization; 672: - workers; 673: - observers; 674: - incremental indexing; 675: - new scheduling systems 676: 677: until the current architecture and measured bottleneck justify them. 678: 679: First correct functional exceptions that prevent operations from completing. 680: 681: --- 682: 683: ## 21. Documentation 684: 685: Documentation updates should normally occur after implementation and validation. 686: 687: Relevant project documents may include: 688: 689: - README.md 690: - STATUS.md 691: - TODO.md 692: - VERIFY.md 693: - VALIDATION_REPORT.txt 694: - architecture or proposal documents 695: 696: Do not update documentation during a narrow runtime investigation unless the 697: work package explicitly includes documentation. 698: 699: Documentation must describe the verified implementation, not the intended 700: implementation. 701: 702: Deferred behavior must remain clearly marked as deferred. 703: 704: --- 705: 706: ## 22. Commit and Push 707: 708: The coding agent must not commit or push unless explicitly instructed. 709: 710: Before commit: 711: 712: git status --short 713: git diff --check 714: git diff --stat 715: git diff 716: 717: Only validated and approved files should be staged. 718: 719: Before push, confirm: 720: 721: - intended branch; 722: - commit contents; 723: - browser validation status; 724: - service-worker/cache implications; 725: - absence of unrelated staged changes. 726: 727: Promotion from development to main is a separate release action and must not be 728: performed implicitly as part of a feature fix. 729: 730: --- 731: 732: ## 23. Final ACT Report 733: 734: The final report must include: 735: 736: - branch; 737: - initial changed files; 738: - final changed files; 739: - exact files modified by the package; 740: - root cause; 741: - implementation summary; 742: - behavior preserved; 743: - static validation; 744: - browser validation; 745: - tests not performed; 746: - unresolved issues; 747: - deferred work; 748: - final status. 749: 750: The report must not claim repository-wide completion when only a narrow package 751: was completed. 752: 753: Use a status appropriate to the evidence, such as: 754: 755: - implementation complete — browser tests required; 756: - implementation complete — browser validation passed; 757: - implementation partial — source gaps remain; 758: - validation tool blocked; 759: - boundary blocked; 760: - unresolved failures remain. 761: 762: --- 763: 764: ## 24. Stable Checkpoints 765: 766: A stable checkpoint is reached when: 767: 768: - implementation scope is complete; 769: - static checks pass or limitations are documented; 770: - required browser behavior is validated; 771: - unrelated changes remain preserved; 772: - final diff is reviewed; 773: - documentation is consistent where required; 774: - changes are committed when authorized. 775: 776: After a stable checkpoint: 777: 778: 1. Record completed behavior. 779: 2. Record deferred behavior. 780: 3. Decide whether to continue in the same conversation. 781: 4. Start a new conversation if the next package is materially different. 782: 5. Provide a complete new-chat bootstrap when necessary. 783: 784: --- 785: 786: ## 25. Current MarkmapEditor Work-Package Order 787: 788: Unless explicitly changed, use this priority order: 789: 790: 1. Finish and stabilize Task Review. 791: 2. Finish and stabilize Wiki Links. 792: 3. Verify and stabilize Related/backlink behavior. 793: 4. Establish a daily-use release checkpoint. 794: 5. Continue Frontmapper/frontmatter work. 795: 6. Advance Report Mode afterward. 796: 797: Do not mix future work into an active stabilization package merely because the 798: future feature appears easy or isolated. 799: 800: --- 801: 802: ## 26. Release Closure (Mandatory) 803: 804: Every accepted package must close with all of the following documented: 805: 806: - accepted runtime behavior; 807: - static validation; 808: - browser acceptance; 809: - contextual Help review; 810: - validation-backed examples; 811: - Release Notes entry; 812: - semantic version decision; 813: - cache identity update; 814: - LOCAL_APP_SHELL verification; 815: - one-time What's New verification; 816: - permanent history verification; 817: - cache-boundary smoke; 818: - checkpoint commit; 819: - separately authorized push. 820: 821: A package is closed only when each item is verified or an approved exception 822: is recorded. 823: 824: Experiment and non-release rules: 825: 826: - An experiment does not create a release, version change, Help update, or 827: Release Notes entry until its production behavior is accepted. 828: - A rejected feature receives no Release Notes entry. 829: - Browser-pending work does not close a release; it stays pending until 830: browser-proven, then is reconsidered at a later closure. 831: 832: Planned syntax and roadmap behavior must not be documented as implemented. 833: 834: Preservation of historical validation evidence: 835: 836: - Historical validation evidence (records of what previously ran, where, and 837: what it proved) is preserved verbatim. New work never rewrites or re-labels 838: past evidence; updates are recorded as current operational documentation, 839: not as edits to historical proof. 840: 841: Unresolved tool-call guard: 842: 843: - If a validation tool-call fails or returns no result, the package is not 844: closed and no checkpoint is created. Resolve the failure or record an 845: approved exception before declaring closure. 846: 847: --- 848: 849: ## 27. Semantic Version Policy 850: 851: MarkmapEditor uses semantic product versions of the form MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. 852: 853: - An accepted moderate user-facing inclusion increments MINOR. 854: - An accepted correction inside an existing inclusion increments PATCH. 855: - The first completed core releases as 1.0.0. 856: - A major second-generation architecture releases as 2.0.0. 857: - An experiment ships with no version change. 858: - A rejected feature gets no release entry. 859: - Browser-pending work does not close a release. 860: - A package may contain several accepted commits before its release boundary. 861: The product version changes once during final release closure, not once per 862: commit. 863: 864: Four-part numbers (e.g. 0.6001) and channel labels (e.g. v73) are not 865: long-term user-facing product versions. 866: 867: ### First semantic release 868: 869: 0.6.0 is the first semantic MarkmapEditor release. Earlier vNN values were 870: cache identities, not product versions, and are not reconstructed as semantic 871: Release Notes entries. 872: 873: --- 874: 875: ## 28. Pre-1.0 Roadmap 876: 877: - 0.6.x — Help, Permanent Release Notes, semantic versioning, and release closure. 878: - 0.7.x — Projects minimal declaration and managed metadata. 879: - 0.8.x — Projects Expanded View editing and normalized Report integration. 880: - 0.9.x — Basic Reminders and first-generation stabilization. 881: - 0.10.x — Visual hierarchy and interface distinction. 882: - 1.0.0 — First-generation core completion. 883: - 2.0.0 — Second-generation architecture and larger experiences. 884: 885: Roadmap descriptions are planning intent, not release-note text, until reviewed 886: at the gate for each package. 887: 888: ### Version 2 candidates (recorded, not implemented) 889: 890: Version 1 is not blocked by these items. Session Entry and Authority Precedence 915: 916: ### Mandatory session entry 917: 918: Every new coding agent must, before planning, editing, running broad tests or 919: making architecture claims: 920: 921: 1. read `.cline/rules/00-markmapeditor-entrypoint.md`; 922: 2. read `docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md`; 923: 3. read `docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md`; 924: 4. read `project-state.json`; 925: 5. read `docs/work/CURRENT.md`; 926: 6. read `docs/validation/CURRENT_VALIDATION.md`; 927: 7. read the active Package document (`docs/packages/P6-CONSISTENCY.md` for Package 6); 928: 8. read only the architecture and ADR documents referenced by the current work or active Package; 929: 9. inspect Git state: `git branch --show-current`, `git status --short`, 930: `git diff --stat`, `git diff --check`, `git diff --name-only`; 931: 10. inspect relevant live source and executable validators. 932: 933: The concise project entrypoint rule lives in 934: .cline/rules/00-markmapeditor-entrypoint.md and must not be duplicated 935: elsewhere. 936: 937: ### Authority precedence 938: 939: 1. accepted canonical architecture; 940: 2. roadmap and Package mapping; 941: 3. checked-out source and executable validators; 942: 4. `project-state.json` + `docs/work/CURRENT.md` + `docs/validation/CURRENT_VALIDATION.md` + `docs/packages/P6-CONSISTENCY.md`; 943: 5. `docs/ai-state/*` — compatibility pointers only, never operational state; 944: 6. previous reports and conversations; 945: 7. Repomix snapshots. 946: 947: Current source may expose an implementation defect, but accepted architecture 948: remains the authority for intended behavior. Contradictions between source, 949: validators and architecture must be surfaced to the owner, never silently 950: resolved. 951: 952: ### Repository-first inspection and Repomix boundary 953: 954: - Inspect the live repository directly with targeted symbol searches and 955: small source ranges. 956: - Repomix snapshots are secondary; they must not be loaded when the 957: checked-out repository is available. 958: - Do not repeatedly read complete large files when symbol-level inspection 959: is sufficient. 960: 961: --- 962: 963: ## 30. Model Switch and Context-Compaction Handoff 964: 965: - A replacement model must read the canonical state files first, before any 966: planning or editing. 967: - Agents must not reconstruct active state from conversation history when 968: repository state files exist. 969: - `docs/work/CURRENT.md` carries the current authorization: stage, allowed and 970: protected files, stop conditions. 971: - `docs/validation/CURRENT_VALIDATION.md` carries inherited static, browser 972: and device evidence, kept as separate evidence classes. 973: - `project-state.json` carries the current phase, working-tree boundary and 974: the list of architecture documents that are required right now. 975: - A context-compaction handoff is complete only when no tool_call_ids remain 976: unresolved and any partial work is recorded in `docs/work/CURRENT.md`. 977: - One Cline task has one clear goal or one bounded staged ACT; a replacement 978: model continues that ACT rather than starting a new broad one. 979: 980: ### AI-state update responsibilities 981: 982: `docs/ai-state/*` files are compatibility pointers only; they are NOT updated 983: at every ACT. Update the canonical files instead: 984: 985: - Update `project-state.json` at every ACT boundary (HEAD, branch, ACT statuses); 986: - Update `docs/work/CURRENT.md` at every ACT boundary; 987: - Update `docs/validation/CURRENT_VALIDATION.md` with concise evidence 988: (command, exit, summary count, failure-log path) after each accepted 989: validation run; 990: - Update the active Package document at ACT boundary; 991: - Migrate durable decisions into canonical architecture via 992: `docs/decisions/`; clean stale operational detail at Package closure. 993: - Full terminal logs and source dumps never belong in ai-state. 994: 995: --- 996: 997: ## 31. Context-Efficient Execution 998: 999: ### Source inspection 1000: 1001: - Inspect symbols and small ranges; avoid broad reads of large files. 1002: - Search first (`rg`, targeted `sed` ranges), read only what the question 1003: requires. 1004: 1005: ### Terminal output 1006: 1007: - Successful validation output is summarized: one line per suite with 1008: command, exit code and summary count. 1009: - Verbose output is written to an ignored local log (for example 1010: `.validation/<suite>.log`), never returned wholesale to the model. 1011: - Failures are inspected through targeted log ranges, not entire logs. 1012: - Warnings and unexpected stderr are retained in the log and mentioned in the 1013: summary. 1014: 1015: --- 1016: 1017: ## 32. Validation Tiers and Owner-Based Test Selection 1018: 1019: ### Owner-based selection 1020: 1021: - Consult docs/validation/OWNER_TEST_MATRIX.md and 1022: docs/validation/TEST_CATALOG.md before selecting tests. 1023: - Run the smallest meaningful tier for the changed owners; do not run every 1024: script after every edit. 1025: - Inherited accepted evidence is not rerun unless a changed owner can 1026: invalidate it. 1027: - Map `js/main.js` changes by functional owner or source range; a `main.js` 1028: edit does not require every Workspace suite. 1029: 1030: ### Tiers 1031: 1032: - TIER 0 — EDIT HYGIENE: `node --check` on touched JS/CJS, 1033: `git diff --check`, focused anchor/static check. 1034: - TIER 1 — QUICK DOMAIN SMOKE: fast, non-mutating, changed domain only. 1035: - TIER 2 — TARGETED DOMAIN REGRESSION: selected by changed owner; affected 1036: contracts and integrations; no unrelated domains. 1037: - TIER 3 — PACKAGE PRE-ACCEPTANCE: all active Package validators, affected 1038: shared-runtime regressions, anchor audit, syntax/diff, release parity. 1039: - TIER 4 — PACKAGE CLOSURE: final active Package suite, required 1040: cross-domain regressions, documentation checks, Help/Release Notes checks, 1041: release parity, browser/device checklist. 1042: - TIER M — MUTATION-CONTROL GATE: see the next section. 1043: - TIER D — BROWSER/DEVICE: physical evidence, kept separate from static 1044: evidence. 1045: 1046: ### Evidence classes 1047: 1048: Static fixtures never prove: physical scrolling, visual overlap, keyboard 1049: behavior, responsive usability, File System Access prompts, Service Worker 1050: activation, Android/DeX usability. Browser and device claims require 1051: physically observed evidence, labeled as such. 1052: 1053: Aggregate commands (see package.json and scripts/validate-aggregate.cjs): 1054: `validate:quick`, `validate:projects`, `validate:tasks`, 1055: `validate:workspace`, `validate:reports`, `validate:package5`, 1056: `validate:closure`, `validate:mutation:projects`. Direct script execution 1057: remains available. 1058: 1059: --- 1060: 1061: ## 33. Mutation-Control Isolation (Tier M) 1062: 1063: Tier M runs only after contract-sensitive changes, after material validator 1064: changes, or at explicit gates — never routinely. 1065: 1066: Requirements: 1067: 1068: - run in a disposable isolated copy of the repository; 1069: - include the current uncommitted candidate in the copy; 1070: - never mutate browser-served source; 1071: - run no two mutation suites concurrently; 1072: - take exact byte snapshots (sha256) before and after every mutation; 1073: - prove byte-identical restoration and a green baseline rerun; 1074: - account every control as biting, non-biting or structural guard; 1075: - remove the disposable copy and logs afterward. 1076: 1077: Behavior-changing suites that mutate source belong only to Tier M; ordinary 1078: validators must be non-mutating against the served tree. 1079: 1080: --- 1081: 1082: ## 34. ACT Completion, Owner Acceptance and Package Closure 1083: 1084: ### ACT lifecycle 1085: 1086: - `docs/work/CURRENT.md` is updated at every stage change (A/B/C/owner 1087: acceptance/closed) and must reflect the actual state, never intent. 1088: - On ACT completion, `docs/validation/CURRENT_VALIDATION.md` records concise 1089: evidence per suite: command, exit code, summary count, failure-log path — 1090: no pasted output. 1091: - `project-state.json` is updated when the owner accepts a checkpoint and at 1092: Package closure. 1093: 1094: ### Owner acceptance 1095: 1096: - Owner-accepted evidence is summarized compactly in `project-state.json` and 1097: `docs/work/CURRENT.md` and never rewritten or re-labeled later. 1098: - Browser/device acceptance is labeled as such and is not claimed from Node 1099: fixtures. 1100: 1101: ### Package closure cleanup 1102: 1103: - Migrate durable decisions from DECISION_LOG.md into canonical architecture 1104: and leave a short pointer. 1105: - Remove stale operational detail and temporary artifacts. 1106: - Keep release-identity changes, commit and push for the explicit closure 1107: boundary only (see §26 Release Closure). 1108: 1109: --- 1110: 1111: ## 35. General Rule 1112: 1113: Inspect first. 1114: Plan before editing. 1115: Review before ACT. 1116: Edit narrowly. 1117: Validate explicitly. 1118: Preserve existing work. 1119: Reuse valid same-conversation context. 1120: Start fresh when context or work-package ownership changes. 1121: Never claim more than the evidence proves. 1122: 1123: --- 1124: 1125: ## 36. Final Work Report Standard 1126: 1127: Every ACT completion report must follow this standard. The report is the 1128: durable engineering record of what was done, why, and what evidence supports 1129: it. Future agents must be able to reconstruct the ACT from the report without 1130: re-examining Git. 1131: 1132: ### Required sections (in order) 1133: 1134: 1. **Executive Summary** — one paragraph: what changed, why, and the outcome. 1135: 2. **Initial State and Authorized Scope** — starting HEAD, branch, active 1136: Package/ACT status, release activation state, and the exact scope the 1137: owner authorized. 1138: 3. **Source-Proven Findings** — what the inspected source, validators, and 1139: evidence showed before implementation; exact validator counts where 1140: applicable. 1141: 4. **Previous Behavior and Root Cause** — the behavior before the change and 1142: the root cause of the defect or gap being addressed. 1143: 5. **Implementation Detail** — what was changed, in which files, and why those 1144: files; meaningful behavioral explanation, not just file lists. 1145: 6. **Files Changed** — each file with an explanation of its role; no bare file 1146: lists. 1147: 7. **Ownership and Data Flow** — which domain owns each changed file and how 1148: data moves through it after the change. 1149: 8. **User-Visible Result** — what a user can observe differently after the 1150: change. 1151: 9. **Preserved Behavior and Regression Guards** — what intentionally remains 1152: unchanged and what guards prevent regression. 1153: 10. **Validation Evidence** — exact validator counts (e.g. `93/93 PASS`), 1154: separate static/browser/device evidence, exit codes, and log paths. 1155: 11. **Browser and Device Evidence** — physically observed evidence labeled as 1156: such; never claim browser behavior from Node fixtures. 1157: 12. **Documentation Updated** — which documents changed and why each was in 1158: scope. 1159: 13. **Git and Checkpoint** — starting and ending HEAD, branch, dirty state, 1160: commit/push status. 1161: 14. **Deferred and Protected Work** — owner-deferred items and protected scope 1162: that was not touched. 1163: 15. **Known Limitations and Open Questions** — what remains unverified or 1164: unresolved. 1165: 16. **Release State** — releasedVersion, targetVersion, releaseActivation 1166: state, cache/version/service-worker change status. 1167: 17. **Recommended Next Step** — the owner-approved next action, or "none" if 1168: none is authorized. 1169: 1170: ### Requirements 1171: 1172: - Include exact validator counts (e.g. `93/93 PASS`, not "all green"). 1173: - Name relevant owners (e.g. `js/workspace/workspace-parser.js`, `MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE`). 1174: - Provide meaningful behavioral explanation for every changed file. 1175: - Record starting and ending HEAD explicitly. 1176: - Separate static, browser, and device evidence; never mix classes. 1177: - List explicit unperformed tests (tests that were considered but not run). 1178: - Record deferred owner-approved work and protected scope. 1179: - State release activation state (`true`/`false`). 1180: 1181: ### Prohibited 1182: 1183: - Raw successful terminal dumps — summarize passes, inspect failures through 1184: targeted log ranges only. 1185: - Huge copied diffs — explain what changed, do not paste full diffs. 1186: - "All green" without counts — every pass claim must carry a count. 1187: - Unsupported browser claims — browser/device claims require physical 1188: observation, labeled as such. 1189: - File lists without explanation — every listed file needs a role. 1190: - Presenting PLAN targets as implemented — PLAN status is not implementation. 1191: - Claiming closure with a pending browser checkpoint — closure requires all 1192: authorized checkpoints to pass. 1193: - Omitting protected or deferred work — both must be listed explicitly. 1194: 1195: --- 1196: 1197: ## 37. Documentation Update Discipline 1198: 1199: During a normal implementation ACT, agents normally update only: 1200: 1201: - `project-state.json` — machine-readable project state (HEAD, branch, 1202: version, ACT statuses); 1203: - `docs/work/CURRENT.md` — current human-readable work summary; 1204: - `docs/validation/CURRENT_VALIDATION.md` — current validation evidence; 1205: - the active Package document (for Package 6: `docs/packages/P6-CONSISTENCY.md`). 1206: 1207: Other documents change only when their owned information changes: 1208: 1209: - Roadmap — Package sequence or scope change; 1210: - Architecture — durable architecture change; 1211: - ADR — durable cross-Package decision; 1212: - Test catalog/matrix — suite or ownership change; 1213: - Help — accepted user-visible behavior; 1214: - Release Notes — release boundary only; 1215: - version/cache/service worker — accepted activation only. 1216: 1217: Do not update historical or compatibility files at every ACT. Changing only priority never changes a lifecycle date. 175: - If two Tasks share the same text, the exact Task you are editing changes and 176: the other is left alone. 177: 178: ## Wiki Links 179: - [[Note]] links one Note to another. 180: - [[Note|custom text]] shows different text but still opens Note. 181: - A link never spans a line break, and the target cannot contain brackets. 182: - Cross-file resolution uses the SAVED Workspace Index, so Save after renaming 183: or retitling a Note. 184: 185: ### How a link target is resolved 186: - An exact path or filename wins first, then a Note's saved H1 heading. 187: - A filename always takes precedence over a matching H1, so a link never 188: silently picks a different Note than you meant. 189: - A Note may be found by its H1, but opening it always uses its exact file path. 190: - H1 is a visual identity: two Notes may share one H1. 191: 192: ### Link states 193: - Resolved: the target was found and can be opened. 194: - Missing: nothing matched. No file is created and nothing is opened. 195: - Ambiguous: more than one Note matched. Nothing is opened, because choosing for 196: you would be a guess. 197: - Not ready: the saved Workspace Index is not available yet, which is different 198: from the target being missing. 199: 200: ## Links In and Links Out 201: - Links Out are the Wiki Links the current Note declares. While you are editing, 202: they follow your unsaved text. 203: - Links In are the saved Notes whose resolved outgoing links point at the active 204: Note. A Note linked by its H1 is included. 205: - Repeated links from one Note produce a single Links In row. 206: - Links In needs the saved Workspace Index. Before that, the panel says it is 207: unavailable rather than reporting none. 208: - In the Sidebar, the Links In panel shows the count and the source Notes. 209: A confirmed empty result shows 0 and "No Links In."; an unavailable one is 210: shown differently. 211: - Selecting a Links In entry opens that exact source Note. 212: 213: ## Not in this release 214: - Compact Active and Workspace Index relationship cards are planned for a later 215: visual-consistency release. It establishes the cross-feature product contract, package order, dependencies, boundaries, and acceptance model for: 17: 18: - Notes and Workspace; 19: - Standalone Notes; 20: - Tasks; 21: - Wiki Links; 22: - Projects; 23: - Reports; 24: - final visual consistency; 25: - 1.0 release closure. 26: 27: The implementation must remain incremental. Where this document and a subsystem record differ on a 59: cross-feature question, this document governs. 60: 61: Repository facts that constrain this program: 62: 63: - Markdown remains canonical. 64: - The current Workspace format is `workspace-root/notes/*.md`. 65: - Notes, Knowledge, Pinned, and Archive are projections over the same physical Notes. 66: - `WORKSPACE_INDEX_STATE` already aggregates files, Tasks, links, tags, and Projects. 67: - Current Document scope already parses the live editor buffer through the shared Workspace parser. 68: - Task lifecycle is owned by `MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE` and task-local `mme-task` comments. 69: - Task Review and Task Board already consume the shared Workspace read model. 70: - Projects are already discovered by the parser and aggregated into the Workspace Index. 71: - Quick Report, reviewed Markdown import, Draw.io reconciliation, and Report panel foundations already exist. 72: - Version 0.6.2 is published. Notes architecture is frozen except for defects proven by real use. 73: 74: --- 75: 76: ## 3. Product Principles 77: 78: ### 3.1 Markdown-first 79: 80: The Markdown file is the canonical unit. Visual experiences may project, filter, aggregate, and safely edit Markdown, but must not create a competing hidden database. 81: 82: ### 3.2 Progressive opt-in 83: 84: A workflow must work at its simplest level first. Optional Workspace aggregation, metadata enrichment, Reports, and future attribute layers may add value later without making the base workflow mandatory. 85: 86: ### 3.3 Standalone first where useful 87: 88: A standalone Markdown file must remain a first-class experience. Workspace is an optional aggregation layer, not a prerequisite for editing or using document-local features. 89: 90: ### 3.4 One owner per responsibility 91: 92: Do not add: 93: 94: - a second Workspace scanner; 95: - a second Workspace Index; 96: - a second Task lifecycle owner; 97: - a parallel Project database; 98: - a Report source of truth outside Markdown; 99: - duplicate physical open, Save, or navigation paths. 100: 101: ### 3.5 Conservative mutation 102: 103: When identity or reconciliation is ambiguous, do not write automatically. Preserve user content and report the ambiguity. 104: 105: ### 3.6 Small packages, stable checkpoints 106: 107: Every package must end in a browser-tested checkpoint. Version, Service Worker, Help, Release Notes, and documentation are updated once, only after that package is accepted. 108: 109: --- 110: 111: ## 4. Accepted Notes and Workspace Contract 112: 113: ### 4.1 Physical layout 114: 115: ```text 116: workspace-root/ 117: └── notes/ 118: └── *.md 119: ``` 120: 121: ### 4.2 Projections 122: 123: - **Notes:** every active Note. 124: - **Knowledge:** active Notes with `knowledge: true`. Knowledge Notes remain visible in Notes. 125: - **Pinned:** active Notes with `pinned: true`, displayed once in the Pinned area. 126: - **Archive:** Notes with `archived: true`, excluded from active Notes, Knowledge, and Pinned. 127: 128: Archive is reversible metadata. It never moves, copies, renames, or deletes a file. 129: 130: ### 4.3 Identity 131: 132: - H1 is the primary saved visual title. 133: - Filename and exact path remain the physical identity. 134: - Duplicate H1 values are allowed. 135: - Navigation uses path, not title. 136: 137: ### 4.4 Scope 138: 139: ```text 140: Current Document 141: → live editor buffer 142: → one shared parser result 143: → never persisted as a second store 144: 145: Workspace 146: → saved physical Notes 147: → WORKSPACE_INDEX_STATE aggregation 148: ``` 149: 150: Unsaved changes belong to Current Document scope. Workspace projections represent saved content until Save rebuilds the Index. 151: 152: ### 4.5 Freeze rule 153: 154: The accepted Notes architecture must not be redesigned during the 1.0 program. Changes are limited to defects found through real use and narrowly scoped usability improvements assigned to an approved package. 155: 156: ### 4.6 ACT V0 — accepted pre-package visual correction 157: 158: ACT V0 was a source-proven visual correction performed before Package 2. It is part 159: of the **accepted 1.0 baseline**, not a pending change: 160: 161: - the global Workspace action area is exactly **Open Workspace · Today · New Note**; 162: - **Archive and Restore belong to the Active panel action row**, using the existing 163: single metadata writer (`applyActiveNoteMetadata`). The former global 164: "Archive Active" control, its physical archive/ copy-and-remove workflow and its 165: second click lifecycle were removed, so Archive/Restore has exactly one owner; 166: - Sidebar panel badges no longer repeat their panel title (`0 related` → `0`, 167: `<n> tags` → `<n>`); compound badges that carry a real state or a second metric 168: (Active `Note`, Report `Config`, Workspace Index `62 files · 195 open`) were kept; 169: - panel title weight is owned by a single rule, and the Archive panel now uses the 170: same generic sibling separator as every other Workspace panel. 171: 172: ACT V0 changed presentation only. It did not change the parser, the metadata writer, 173: YAML format, Archive semantics, Notes storage, navigation, Task parsing, Wiki Links, 174: Projects data, Report behaviour or pane layout, and it did not change the version or 175: cache identity. Its proof suite is `scripts/workspace-sidebar-visual-validators.cjs` 176: (50 fixtures, including five mutation controls). 177: 178: --- 179: 180: ## 4A. Scope Composition Rule 181: 182: Every consumer in the program must be assessed **individually** and classified as one of: 183: 184: - **Current Document** — the live editor buffer; 185: - **Workspace** — saved physical Notes through `WORKSPACE_INDEX_STATE`; 186: - **Both** — meaningful in each scope, potentially with different content; 187: - **Workspace-only** — meaningless or misleading without aggregation. 188: 189: Both scopes must reuse the same parser. A **second parser, second Workspace Index, or 190: second document store is not allowed.** A consumer that is "Both" reuses the same 191: owner in both scopes with different inputs; it does not acquire a second owner. 192: 193: --- 194: 195: ## 5. Application Entry and Standalone Notes 196: 197: Standalone Notes are part of 1.0. 198: 199: ### 5.1 Target entry contract 200: 201: ```text 202: Open Standalone Note 203: → open one Markdown file 204: → document-relevant tools only 205: 206: Open Workspace 207: → open the Notes Workspace 208: → document tools plus Workspace aggregation 209: ``` 210: 211: The implementation must adapt existing owners. It must not create two independent applications or two independently maintained Sidebars. 212: 213: ### 5.2 Candidate Standalone tools 214: 215: The consumer-fit package must evaluate and explicitly classify each feature as `Current Document`, `Workspace`, `Both`, or `Workspace-only`. 216: 217: Likely useful in Standalone scope: 218: 219: - Editor; 220: - Markmap; 221: - HTML Preview; 222: - Outline; 223: - local Tasks; 224: - local Projects; 225: - local tags; 226: - outgoing Wiki Links; 227: - document information and metrics; 228: - virtual local Projects view with Return; 229: - virtual Quick Report with Return, if the data and Save contract remain simple. 230: 231: Likely Workspace-only: 232: 233: - Notes, Knowledge, Pinned, and Archive aggregation; 234: - search across files; 235: - backlinks from other files; 236: - global tags inventory; 237: - All Tasks; 238: - All Projects; 239: - Workspace Report; 240: - Workspace migration and indexing controls. 241: 242: ### 5.3 Virtual-view contract 243: 244: Projects and Reports may open as virtual views without replacing the physical file identity. 245: 246: ```text 247: Physical Markdown document 248: → open virtual view 249: → inspect or configure derived content 250: → Return 251: → restore the previous physical document and layout safely 252: ``` 253: 254: Virtual views must preserve dirty-state protection, writable handle, Current Document identity, Navigation History, and Return behavior. 255: 256: --- 257: 258: ## 5A. Shared Interaction Grammar 259: 260: **Product principle: learn one interaction → recognize and use the equivalent interaction elsewhere.** 261: 262: The following surfaces must converge visually and behaviorally wherever they represent 263: equivalent information: 264: 265: - Active; 266: - Workspace Index; 267: - Tags Sidebar; 268: - future document-local summaries; 269: - future Highlights and Reminders. 270: 271: Sharing a grammar does **not** create another persistent store. Two surfaces may look 272: identical and still read different scopes. 273: 274: ### 5A.1 Shared summary-card contract 275: 276: Target card contract: 277: 278: - compact title; 279: - numeric count; 280: - small disclosure chevron; 281: - `aria-expanded` state; 282: - concise preview list; 283: - clickable navigation entries; 284: - optional **View All** action; 285: - consistent empty state; 286: - mouse, touch and keyboard support; 287: - **no domain editing inside the summary card.** 288: 289: Scope difference: 290: 291: - **Active** → the active Current Document and relationships involving that document; 292: - **Workspace Index** → saved Workspace aggregation. 293: 294: ### 5A.2 Active summary cards 295: 296: Planned Active cards: 297: 298: - **Open**; 299: - **Done**; 300: - **Links In**; 301: - **Links Out**; 302: - **Projects**. 303: 304: Possible future post-1.0 cards: **Highlights**, **Reminders**. 305: 306: Active remains a **compact summary and navigation surface**. It does not replace Task 307: Review, Task Board, Projects Expanded View, the Wiki Links owner, the Tags Sidebar or 308: the Workspace Index. 309: 310: Initial expanded lists should normally show **no more than three to five items**. 311: **View All delegates to the specialized owner** and never duplicates it. 312: 313: > **Status: planned, not implemented.** No expandable Active card exists in the 314: > current source. `renderWorkspaceActivePanel()` in `js/main.js` renders a flat 315: > `workspaceActiveStats` grid only. No ACT has begun this work. 316: 317: ### 5A.3 Workspace Index parity 318: 319: The Workspace Index may use the same disclosure and navigation grammar for Open Tasks, 320: Done Tasks, Links In, Links Out, Projects and Tags. 321: 322: - Workspace Index uses **Workspace** scope. 323: - Active uses **Current Document** scope. 324: 325: Identical list sizes or complete layouts are **not** required. Equivalent interaction 326: semantics are required. 327: 328: > **Status: planned, not implemented.** The current Workspace Index uses static 329: > metric tiles and sections, not disclosure cards. 330: 331: ### 5A.4 Tags 332: 333: Tags must use the same chip appearance and selection behavior in Active, the Tags 334: Sidebar and the Workspace Index. 335: 336: Workspace behavior: 337: 338: - an Active tag delegates to the existing Workspace Tags filtering owner; 339: - a Sidebar tag uses that same filter owner; 340: - a Workspace Index tag uses that same filter owner. 341: 342: Standalone behavior: 343: 344: - an Active tag operates only inside the Current Document; 345: - no cross-file result is implied without a Workspace. 346: 347: > **Status: planned, not implemented.** ACT V0 established count-only Tags badges but 348: > did not add clickable Active tags or cross-surface parity. 349: 350: ### 5A.5 Relationship terminology 351: 352: Adopt the symmetric convention: 353: 354: - **Links In**; 355: - **Links Out**. 356: 357: **Links In** replaces `Related` wherever Related currently means Notes linking *into* 358: the active Note. **Links Out** means Wiki Links *declared by* the current source. 359: 360: **The rename is planned, not implemented.** Package 3 must first prove that the 361: current Related data is truly the backlink / Links In projection before any visible 362: label changes. 363: 364: > **Source-reconciliation note (Gate 1).** Both projections currently derive from the 365: > same `parsed.conceptLinks` array: `findBacklinksForConcept()` 366: > (`js/main.js:2498`) selects *other* Notes whose `conceptLinks` include the active 367: > one, while the Active stat `linksOut` (`js/main.js:3811`) counts the active 368: > document's *own* `conceptLinks`. This is consistent with Links In / Links Out, but 369: > it is a reading, not a proof. Package 3 owns that proof. 370: 371: --- 372: 373: ## 6. Tasks Architecture for 1.0 374: 375: ### 6.1 Existing foundation 376: 377: Tasks already use: 378: 379: - Markdown checkbox state as the completion authority; 380: - task-local `<!-- mme-task: ... -->` metadata; Source does not override an owner decision; 17: ACT 5A implements the decision and the noted transition. 18: 19: --- 20: 21: ## 1. Product purpose 22: 23: Projects follow the successful architectural philosophy of Tasks: 24: 25: - simple visible Markdown declaration; 26: - important readable attributes remain visible; 27: - independent managed metadata comment; 28: - conservative Save reconciliation; 29: - one mutation owner; 30: - aggregated visual management surface. 31: 32: Tasks and Projects remain **separate feature types**. 33: 34: Projects do **not** share with Tasks: 35: 36: - parser; 37: - writer; 38: - lifecycle; 39: - metadata comment (`<!-- mme-project: ... -->` is independent of `<!-- mme-task: ... -->`); 40: - mutation owner. 41: 42: Task priority remains `#p1`, `#p2`, `#p3`. Package 5 does **not** propose `[p1]`. 43: 44: **Source note.** The Task side of this is real and proven: `PRIORITY_TOKEN_RE = 45: /#p[123]\b/gi` (`js/tasks/task-lifecycle.js:294`), with `#project` proven to be an 46: *unrelated* tag that must not be read as priority 47: (`js/tasks/task-lifecycle.js:1803-1804`). Projects must not disturb either. 48: 49: --- 50: 51: ## 2. Visible Project declaration 52: 53: ### 2.1 Accepted forms 54: 55: Canonical (write this form): 56: 57: ```md 58: Project: Alibaba 59: 60: Project: Alibaba [800000 BRL] 61: 62: Project: Alibaba [27Q3] 63: 64: Project: Alibaba [800000 BRL] [27Q3] 65: ``` 66: 67: Compatible (parsed identically; never written by the serializer): 68: 69: ```md 70: - Project: Alibaba [800000 BRL] [27Q3] 71: 72: * Project: Alibaba [27Q3] 73: 74: + Project: Alibaba 75: ``` 76: 77: ### 2.2 What the visible declaration owns 78: 79: - Project title; 80: - value; 81: - currency; 82: - Expected Order quarter. 83: 84: These values remain visible in: 85: 86: - Editor; 87: - Markmap; 88: - HTML Preview; 89: - Sidebar; 90: - Expanded Projects View; 91: - Reports. 92: 93: ### 2.3 Grammar shape 94: 95: ```text 96: Project: <title> [ <value> <currency> ] [ <quarter> ] 97: ``` 98: 99: Both bracket groups are optional. When both are present the value group precedes 100: the quarter group. The title is required. 101: 102: **Project titles may contain brackets.** The parser consumes **only** valid 103: recognized trailing Project tokens, working from the end of the declaration. 104: Arbitrary bracketed title text remains part of the title, and unsupported tokens 105: are never removed. 106: 107: Examples: 108: 109: ```md 110: Project: Migration [Phase 1] 111: 112: Project: Migration [Phase 1] [800000 BRL] [27Q3] 113: 114: Project: Review [[Alibaba]] [27Q3] 115: ``` 116: 117: In the second example the title is `Migration [Phase 1]` and both tokens are 118: consumed. In the third example the `[[Alibaba]]` Wiki Link remains intact inside 119: the title while `[27Q3]` is consumed as Expected Order. Project parsing never 120: consumes Task lines, so `- [ ] Ship Alibaba [800000 BRL]` remains a Task whose 121: text carries a Project-shaped token (§15.3). 122: 123: ### 2.4 Declaration grammar — canonical vs compatible prefixes 124: 125: The ONE declaration grammar is defined by the canonical parser 126: (`workspace-parser.js`): a line is a Project declaration when, after trimming, 127: it starts with `Project:`. 128: 129: | Form | Status | Example | 130: | --- | --- | --- | 131: | `Project: <title> …` | **CANONICAL** — the only form the serializer writes | `Project: Alibaba [27Q3]` | 132: | `- Project: …` / `* Project: …` / `+ Project: …` | **COMPATIBLE** — read, never written | `- Project: Alibaba [27Q3]` | 133: 134: Rules: 135: 136: - **Bullet prefix is transparent.** Before declaration recognition the parser 137: applies `stripListPrefix()` — `/^[-*+]\s+/` removed, then trimmed. The prefix 138: therefore changes nothing about the record: the title, value, currency and 139: quarter tokens are identical in both forms, and the visible-line edit path 140: (`splitDeclaration()`) preserves the original indentation and prefix so a 141: re-serialization never rewrites the author's list. 142: - **Only the three ASCII bullet markers are stripped.** `stripListPrefix()` is 143: exactly `/^[-*+]\s+/`; ordered-list markers (`1. Project:`) and quote markers 144: (`> Project:`) are NOT stripped and therefore are not declarations. 145: - **A Task line is never a Project.** `isTaskCheckboxLine()` runs before 146: declaration recognition, so `- [ ] Ship Alibaba [27Q3]` stays a Task (§15.3). 147: - **Fenced code is invisible.** Declaration scanning (both the parser and the 148: managed-metadata locator) skips fenced spans (` ``` ` / `~~~`), so a 149: `Project:` line inside a fence is text, never a Project. 150: - **Locators use the same grammar.** The managed-comment locator 151: (`project-metadata-mutation.js → locateProject()`) recognizes exactly this 152: grammar — including the compatible bullet prefixes and the fenced set — when 153: it decides which declaration owns a following managed comment. A neighboring 154: Project (in either form) terminates the search instead of donating its 155: comment, which is what keeps `id`-keyed mutation address correct. 156: 157: --- 158: 159: ## 3. Value and currency contract 160: 161: ### 3.1 Canonical form 162: 163: ```text 164: [<numeric-value> <currency-code>] 165: ``` 166: 167: Examples: 168: 169: ```md 170: [800000 BRL] 171: [1200000 USD] 172: [1250000.50 USD] 173: ``` 174: 175: ### 3.2 Rules 176: 177: - value before currency; 178: - whitespace between value and currency; 179: - period for decimal fraction; 180: - no thousands separators; 181: - uppercase currency normalization; 182: - zero is distinct from missing — `[0 BRL]` is a **present** value of `0`; 183: - negative value is **not** canonical in ACT 5A; 184: - a malformed candidate remains readable Markdown and never throws; 185: - a recognized-but-malformed candidate produces a bounded diagnostic; 186: - no hashtag-based money syntax. 187: 188: ### 3.3 Explicitly rejected as canonical 189: 190: ```md 191: #800000BRL 192: [800000BRL] 193: [1.200.000 BRL] 194: [1,200,000 USD] 195: [-50000 BRL] 196: ``` 197: 198: Rejected input must still **render as ordinary readable Markdown**. It is not 199: deleted, rewritten, or treated as a parse error that aborts the document. 200: 201: **Source note.** "Zero is distinct from missing" already holds today: the legacy 202: parser yields `value: null` for missing and `value: 0` for an explicit zero, and 203: Report filtering uses `Number.isFinite(p.value)` so a zero-valued Project is 204: counted as *with-value* (`js/report/report-dictionary.js:509-511`, fixture 205: `Beta` = 0). This contract preserves that behavior. 206: 207: --- 208: 209: ## 4. Quarter contract 210: 211: ### 4.1 Accepted inputs 212: 213: ```text 214: 27Q1 215: 2027Q1 216: 2027-Q1 217: 2027 Q1 218: ``` 219: 220: Aliases are case-insensitive. Two-digit years always mean 2000–2099; year 221: 2100 is only reachable through the full four-digit form, so no alias is 222: ambiguous. `29Q3`, `2029Q3`, `2029-Q3` and `2029 Q3` normalize identically. 223: 224: ### 4.2 Normalized internal form 225: 226: ```text 227: 2027-Q1 228: ``` 229: 230: ### 4.3 Compact visible form 231: 232: ```text 233: 27Q1 234: ``` 235: 236: Year 2100 keeps the full representation in display too (`2100Q4`, never the 237: ambiguous `00Q4`). 238: 239: ### 4.4 Valid quarters 240: 241: ```text 242: Q1 243: Q2 244: Q3 245: Q4 246: ``` 247: 248: Years are fixed product range **2020–2100 inclusive** (a fixed floor, never 249: derived from the current year). New structured values below 2020 or above 250: 2100 are rejected; existing out-of-range values stay visible as 251: legacy/custom — never silently rewritten, never erased. 252: 253: ### 4.5 Scope 254: 255: Expected Order, Expected Delivery and Expected Billing share ONE structured 256: control contract: label on the first line, compact Year + Quarter side by 257: side on the second line. The empty option `—` is the ONLY Clear affordance — 258: there is no separate Clear button; selecting `—` explicitly clears the 259: complete field. Partial drafts (Year without Quarter, or Quarter without 260: Year) stay visible but are NOT persistable and block Apply; Cancel restores 261: persisted values. 262: 263: The visible line contains **only** Expected Order. 264: 265: Expected Delivery and Expected Billing belong to managed metadata (§5). 266: 267: Package 5 does **not** introduce an exact target date. 268: 269: **Source note.** This contract is satisfied by the shared owner 270: `normalizeProjectQuarter()` (`js/workspace/workspace-parser.js:244+`), which 271: accepts `^(\d{2}|\d{4})[-/ ]?[qQ]([1-4])$` (case-insensitive), emits 272: `canonical: "2027-Q1"` and `display: "27Q1"` (full `2100Q4` for year 2100), 273: enforces the fixed 2020–2100 range, and produces `{ valid: false }` rather 274: than throwing on malformed input. Parser recognition, Projects View 275: recognition, draft validation, mutation validation and persisted output ALL 276: read this one function; no second quarter normalizer exists. 277: 278: ### 4.6 ID-adjacent note (ACT 5D-FU) 279: 280: The quarter range floor moved from 2025 to 2020 by owner decision. Existing 281: 2020–2024 legacy/custom values are NOT mass-rewritten; they become 282: replaceable through the structured controls. 283: 284: --- 285: 286: ## 5. Managed metadata 287: 288: ### 5.1 The comment 289: 290: Projects use an independent managed comment: 291: 292: ```md 293: <!-- mme-project: ... --> 294: ``` 295: 296: Conceptual example: 297: 298: ```md 299: Project: Alibaba [800000 BRL] [27Q3] 300: <!-- mme-project: id=prj_<opaque-id>; created=2026-10-03; stage=quotation; delivery=27Q4; billing=28Q1 --> 301: ``` 302: 303: ### 5.2 What the comment owns 304: 305: - `id`; 306: - `created`; 307: - `stage`; 308: - `delivery` (Expected Delivery); 309: - `billing` (Expected Billing); 310: - `closed`; 311: - `archived`. 312: 313: ### 5.3 What the comment does NOT own 314: 315: - Project title; 316: - value; 317: - currency; 318: - Expected Order; 319: - source path; 320: - source line. 321: 322: Do **not** duplicate visible-line fields inside `mme-project`. Duplication would 323: create two authorities for one value and re-introduce precedence ambiguity. 324: 325: **Source precedent.** `mme-task` uses `key=value` segments joined by `; ` inside 326: one comment, written by `buildTaskMetadataComment()` 327: (`js/tasks/task-lifecycle.js:150-169`). `mme-project` follows the same 328: serialization convention independently; it must not import or extend 329: `MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE` key ownership. Lifecycle keys are owned and appended 330: deterministically while non-lifecycle entries survive round-trip 331: (`js/tasks/task-lifecycle.js:41-46`) — the same discipline applies to `mme-project` 332: keys, with a separate key set. 333: 334: ### 5.4 Comment placement (ACCEPTED) 335: 336: The writer always uses **canonical immediate adjacency**: `mme-project` is the 337: **immediate next line** after the Project declaration. 338: 339: The reader is narrowly tolerant and must define behavior for: 340: 341: | Situation | Behavior | 342: | --- | --- | 343: | immediate valid comment | managed; reconcile nothing | 344: | one blank line between | tolerated as the Project's comment | 345: | ordinary HTML comment between | the Project stays unmanaged; reconciliation inserts **immediately adjacent** | 346: | comment **before** the declaration | **not** associated (orphan) | 347: | orphan metadata comment | diagnosed; left unchanged | 348: | malformed adjacent comment | diagnosed; **no competing comment inserted**; left unchanged | 349: | duplicate adjacent comments | diagnosed; **not** auto-repaired; left unchanged | 350: | another Project declaration before the comment | **not** associated across Projects | 351: | Markdown heading before the comment | **not** associated across a heading | 352: 353: The reader never searches arbitrarily through the document, never matches by 354: title, and never associates across another Project or a heading. 355: 356: ### 5.5 Deterministic serialization (ACCEPTED) 357: 358: Key order is fixed: 359: 360: 1. `id`; 361: 2. `created`; 362: 3. `stage`; 363: 4. `delivery`; 364: 5. `billing`; 365: 6. `closed`; 366: 7. `archived`; 367: 8. safely preserved unknown fields, after the owned keys. 368: 369: - deterministic separator: `; ` between segments, `key=value`, one space after 370: `mme-project:`; 371: - exactly one comment per Project; no duplicate serialized keys; 372: - the reader is whitespace-tolerant; 373: - a valid comment is **not** reformatted by parsing alone; 374: - unrelated Markdown and unrelated HTML comments are preserved byte-for-byte; 375: - parsing never rewrites; 376: - no arbitrary custom Project fields are introduced — specifically **not** 377: `owner`, `customer`, `probability`, `dependency`, `subproject`, `reminder`. 378: 379: --- 380: 381: ## 6. Authority and precedence 382: 383: Recorded order: 384: 385: 1. **Visible Project declaration** — title, value, currency, Expected Order. 386: 2. **`mme-project`** — identity and managed Project properties. 387: 3. **Temporary legacy fallback** — only while transitioning existing Project 388: declarations. 389: 4. **Ordinary Markdown** — never interpreted as managed metadata unless it 390: matches an accepted Project contract. 391: 392: Rules: 393: 394: - Legacy fallback must **not** override the new authorities. 395: - Legacy never overrides a visible field. 396: - Legacy never overrides valid managed metadata. 397: - No automatic migration. 398: - No deletion of legacy lines. 399: - No rewrite of legacy lines. 400: - No automatic copy of legacy `Status:`/`Stage:` into `mme-project: stage=`. 401: - Legacy lines remain source text. 402: - Records expose `legacyFieldsPresent`. 403: - No write-on-scan. 404: - No write-on-index. 405: - Initial reconciliation inserts **only** `id` and `created`. 406: 407: **Source note.** The legacy fallback is the dictionary-pair grammar 408: (`Project: X` / `Value: N` / `Currency: USD` / `Order: 26Q4`, inline or 409: multiline, optional list markers) implemented by `parseProjects()` / 410: `buildProjectFromBlock()` (`js/workspace/workspace-parser.js:451-504`, `356-449`) 411: and normalized by `resolveProjectKeyAlias()` (`js/workspace/workspace-parser.js:209-242`). 412: That grammar remains valid and remains the transition path. 413: 414: --- 415: 416: ## 7. Persistent identity 417: 418: Project identity is stored in `mme-project`. 419: 420: Three separate concepts: 421: 422: | Concept | Meaning | 423: | --- | --- | 424: | `projectId` | persistent opaque identity | 425: | Project title | visible display text | 426: | `sourcePath` / `sourceLine` | current physical location | 427: 428: ### 7.1 Must NOT be used as persistent identity 429: 430: - title; 431: - slug; 432: - filename; 433: - path; 434: - source line; 435: - ordinal; 436: - path + ordinal. 437: 438: ### 7.2 Identity requirements 439: 440: - exactly one ID per Project; 441: - ID preserved through title rename; 442: - ID preserved through line movement; 443: - ID preserved through Project reorder; 444: - ID preserved through refresh, repeated Save, failed Save and retry (the 445: reconciled buffer is reused — no replacement ID is ever minted); 446: - duplicate-ID diagnostics (including copied/imported IDs across files — 447: never silently renumbered); 448: - malformed-comment behavior defined (malformed or duplicated existing 449: identity is never overwritten as a repair); 450: - conservative creation during Save reconciliation (§8); 451: - short IDs are unique within ONE workspace (see §7.3); uniqueness is NOT 452: claimed across independent workspaces or concurrent independent sessions — 453: conservative duplicate detection covers those cases. 454: 455: ### 7.3 Serialization 456: 457: **Accepted by ACT 5D follow-up (supersedes the ACT 5A UUID decision, kept as 458: history below).** New workspace IDs serialize exactly as: 459: 460: ```text 461: prj_0001 462: prj_0002 463: ... 464: ``` 465: 466: - `prj_` prefix + decimal sequence, **minimum 4 digits**, zero-padded; 467: - the sequence grows without truncation or wraparound (`…9999`, `10000`, …); 468: - allocation is against the COMPLETE workspace inventory: every managed ID 469: in the current workspace inventory (all indexed files, **including 470: archived Notes**), every managed ID in the live current buffer (stale-Index 471: protection), and every ID allocated earlier in the same operation/batch 472: (operation reservations persist across Saves within one batch); 473: - the inventory is obtained through the existing mechanisms 474: (`buildWorkspaceIndex` → `WORKSPACE_INDEX_STATE.projects`, live buffer via 475: the accepted CodeMirror-first owner). If the inventory cannot be proven 476: complete (no workspace open, Index not ready), allocation STOPS with the 477: bounded diagnostic `inventory-incomplete` — it never restarts from the 478: current document alone, and never mints a standalone sequence; 479: - IDs are minted ONLY for genuinely missing managed identity. Malformed or 480: duplicated existing identity is diagnosed, never overwritten; 481: - once minted, an ID is permanent: never regenerated after rename, movement, 482: reorder, refresh, repeated Save, failed Save or retry; 483: - existing `prj_<full-UUID>` IDs remain VALID and unchanged — no migration, 484: no mass rewrite; 485: - copied/imported Projects keep their existing identity; duplicate IDs across 486: the workspace are diagnosed, never silently renumbered; 487: - there is no title/slug/path/line/ordinal fallback of any kind; 488: - no global counter service and no generic identity framework: the 489: orchestrator (`generateManagedProjectId()` in `js/main.js`) is the single 490: allocation owner, the pure helpers (`nextWorkspaceProjectId()` / 491: `collectReservedProjectIds()` in `js/workspace/workspace-parser.js`) take 492: the reservation set as input, and the injected-generator/pure-owner 493: separation is preserved so tests stay deterministic; 494: - a complex general UUID subsystem is **not** introduced. 495: 496: **Superseded history — ACT 5A UUID decision.** ACT 5A accepted 497: `prj_<full-crypto.randomUUID()>` (full UUID retained, never truncated; 498: `crypto.randomUUID()` as the browser primitive; injected generator for 499: deterministic tests). That grammar remains RECOGNIZED (every UUID issued 500: stays valid) but is no longer MINTED for workspace Projects. 501: 502: **Source note — superseded design.** The accepted Package 3 baseline computes a 503: provisional `sourceIdentity = ${sourcePath}::${startLine}::${nameKey}` in 504: `buildProjectFromBlock()` (`js/workspace/workspace-parser.js:440-446`), carrying 505: the comment *"Provisional sourceIdentity — NOT a permanent ID."* It is read by 506: no consumer and is dropped by the Report projection `projectProject()` 507: (`js/report/report-dictionary.js:478-492`). 508: 509: Under this architecture, `sourceIdentity` is **retired** and must not be promoted 510: to identity: it is title-derived and line-derived, so it fails §7.1 on two counts. 511: ACT 5A removes it or marks it as transitional. 512: 513: --- 514: 515: ## 8. Save and reconciliation 516: 517: ### 8.1 Intended flow 518: 519: 1. user writes a Project declaration; 520: 2. user invokes the existing Save flow; 521: 3. Project reconciliation detects an unambiguous declaration without managed 522: identity; 523: 4. reconciliation inserts an `mme-project` comment containing `id` and `created`; 524: 5. the existing Save owner writes the document; 525: 6. the Workspace Index rebuilds after successful Save. 526: 527: ### 8.2 Rules 528: 529: - one reconciliation owner; 530: - no second Save path; 531: - no mutation during scan; 532: - no mutation during Index build; 533: - no mutation merely from opening a Workspace; 534: - ambiguous declarations remain unchanged; 535: - malformed comments do **not** receive a competing comment; 536: - a failed or cancelled Save does not claim successful reconciliation; 537: - ordinary Markdown remains preserved. 538: 539: **Physical-write truthfulness (ACCEPTED).** Reconciliation success, physical-write 540: success, physical-write failure and picker cancellation are **distinct** states. 541: No saved baseline and no rebuilt Index may claim success before the physical write 542: succeeds. After a failed or cancelled write: 543: 544: - no Task baseline refresh; 545: - no saved-content baseline refresh; 546: - no Workspace Index rebuild; 547: - no clean/clean-marking; 548: - no persisted-success log; 549: - the reconciled buffer — including generated `id` and `created` — is preserved 550: and stays dirty, so the next Save reuses the same identity instead of minting a 551: replacement. 552: 553: Cancellation is distinguished from failure: a cancelled picker performs no 554: physical write, refreshes no baseline, schedules no Index rebuild and does **not** 555: mark the document clean. Existing `currentSaveHandle` policy is preserved 556: unchanged. 557: 558: ### 8.3 Source precedent to follow exactly 559: 560: The Task lifecycle already implements this shape and is the model: 561: 562: - pure owner `applySaveLifecycle()` in `js/tasks/task-lifecycle.js:905+`; 563: - orchestration `reconcileTasksBeforeSave()` in `js/main.js:10520+`; 564: - single Save entry `saveSmart()` calls reconciliation **once**, before writing 565: (`js/main.js:10902-10930`); 566: - Report documents excluded from reconciliation **by identity**, returning 567: `skippedReason: 'report-document'` (`js/main.js:10525-10536`); 568: - guarded by an explicit baseline and owner-availability check, each returning a 569: skip reason rather than writing; 570: - buffer update guarded by `__programmaticTextChange` so programmatic edits are 571: not mistaken for user typing. 572: 573: Project reconciliation follows the same contract with a **separate owner and a 574: separate skip-reason vocabulary**. It must not reuse `MME_TASK_LIFECYCLE` and 575: must not add a second `createWritable()` call site. 576: 577: --- 578: 579: ## 9.
