343: MarkmapEditor is a Markdown-first workspace for writing, organizing ideas, exploring documents as interactive mindmaps, and creating useful outputs from the same source. 344: 345: This document is editable. Try changing a heading, adding a list item, or writing a new section. The Markmap and HTML Preview update from your Markdown. 346: 347: ## 🎯 What can I do here? 348: 349: Use MarkmapEditor to: 350: 351: - write and edit Markdown; 352: - explore document structure as an interactive mindmap; 353: - preview the rendered document as HTML; 354: - keep journals, concepts, Tasks, links, and Projects in a local workspace; 355: - generate structured Reports; 356: - create editable Draw.io Report outputs; 357: - prepare presentation source in Slides mode. 358: 359: Your Markdown remains the source of truth. Markmap, HTML Preview, Reports, and visual outputs are derived from it. 360: 361: ## 🚀 Start here 362: 363: 1. Edit this document in the Editor pane. 364: 2. Add or rename a heading. 365: 3. Watch the Markmap update. 366: 4. Open HTML Preview to see the rendered document. 367: 5. Use **Open** to choose an existing Markdown file. 368: 6. Use **Save** to save changes to the current writable file. 369: 7. Switch to **Journal** or **Slides** when you want a different workflow. 370: 371: You can always select **?** in the toolbar for Help about the active mode. 372: 373: ## 🗺️ Understand the three views 374: 375: ### Editor 376: 377: The Editor contains the canonical Markdown source. Make document changes here. 378: 379: ### Markmap 380: 381: The Markmap turns headings and nested content into a visual structure. Select a node to navigate back to the related Markdown. 382: 383: ### HTML Preview 384: 385: HTML Preview shows the document as rendered content, including headings, lists, tables, links, images, and code blocks. 386: 387: The three views represent the same document. The Markdown in the Editor remains authoritative. 388: 389: ## ✍️ Try Markdown 390: 391: Edit the examples below and observe how the other views respond. 392: 393: ### Headings 394: 395: Headings define the document structure and become branches in the Markmap. 396: 397: ```markdown 398: # Document title 399: 400: ## Main section 401: 402: ### Subsection 403: 404: #### Detail 405: ``` 406: 407: ### Emphasis 408: 409: ```markdown 410: **Bold text** 411: 412: *Italic text* 413: 414: ***Bold and italic text*** 415: 416: ~~Strikethrough~~ text 417: 418: `Inline code` 419: ``` 420: 421: Rendered examples: 422: 423: - **Bold text** 424: - *Italic text* 425: - ***Bold and italic text*** 426: - ~~Strikethrough~~ 427: - `Inline code` 428: 429: ### Bullet lists 430: 431: ```markdown 432: - First item 433: - Second item 434: - Nested item 435: - Another nested item 436: - Third item 437: ``` 438: 439: - First item 440: - Second item 441: - Nested item 442: - Another nested item 443: - Third item 444: 445: ### Numbered lists 446: 447: ```markdown 448: 1. Confirm the scope 449: 2. Review the proposal 450: 3. Schedule the next meeting 451: ``` 452: 453: 1. Confirm the scope 454: 2. Review the proposal 455: 3. Schedule the next meeting 456: 457: ### Tasks 458: 459: A Task begins as a normal Markdown checkbox: 460: 461: ```markdown 462: - [ ] Open Task 463: - [x] Completed Task 464: ``` 465: 466: Try these Tasks: 467: 468: - [ ] Add a new section to this document 469: - [ ] Open HTML Preview 470: - [ ] Explore the Markmap controls 471: - [x] Open MarkmapEditor 472: 473: In Journal mode, Tasks can also appear in Task Review and Task Board. 474: 475: ### Blockquotes 476: 477: ```markdown 478: > Markdown should remain simple enough to read as plain text. 479: > 480: > Visual tools should help without taking ownership away from the source. 481: ``` 482: 483: > Markdown should remain simple enough to read as plain text. 484: > 485: > Visual tools should help without taking ownership away from the source. 486: 487: ### Links 488: 489: A standard Markdown link: 490: 491: ```markdown 492: [Markmap website](https://markmap.js.org/) 493: ``` 494: 495: A workspace Wiki Link: 496: 497: ```markdown 498: [[Customer Name]] 499: [[Project Name|Open Project]] 500: ``` 501: 502: Wiki Links are most useful in Journal mode, where they connect journals and concepts in the active workspace. 503: 504: ### Tables 505: 506: ```markdown 507: | Item | Status | Owner | 508: |---|---|---| 509: | Proposal | In progress | Commercial | 510: | Scope | Review | Technical | 511: | Meeting | Planned | Team | 512: ``` 513: 514: | Item | Status | Owner | 515: |---|---|---| 516: | Proposal | In progress | Commercial | 517: | Scope | Review | Technical | 518: | Meeting | Planned | Team | 519: 520: ### Code blocks 521: 522: Use three backticks and optionally include the language name: 523: 524: ````markdown 525: ```javascript 526: function greet(name) { 527: console.log(`Hello, ${name}`); 528: } 529: ``` 530: ```` 531: 532: ```javascript 533: function greet(name) { 534: console.log(`Hello, ${name}`); 535: } 536: ``` 537: 538: HTML Preview can apply syntax highlighting to supported code blocks. 539: 540: ### Images 541: 542: Use a standard Markdown image reference: 543: 544: ```markdown 545: ![Description](./images/example.png) 546: ``` 547: 548: In a Journal workspace, local images are normally stored in the workspace assets folder. Use **Add Image** to create the appropriate reference. 549: 550: ### Math 551: 552: Inline math: 553: 554: ```markdown 555: $x = {-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac} \over 2a}$ 556: ``` 557: 558: Block math: 559: 560: ```markdown 561: $$ 562: E = mc^2 563: $$ 564: ``` 565: 566: Math is currently intended primarily for the Markmap view. HTML Preview may display the source syntax rather than rendered math. 567: 568: ## 📁 Open and save files 569: 570: ### Open 571: 572: Use the Open menu to: 573: 574: - create a new document; 575: - browse for a Markdown file; 576: - reopen a recent writable file; 577: - clear a recovery draft when necessary. 578: 579: ### Save 580: 581: Select **Save** to overwrite the current writable Markdown file. 582: 583: If the active document does not have a writable file handle, MarkmapEditor uses **Save As**. Canceling Save As leaves the document unchanged. 584: 585: ### Recovery drafts 586: 587: MarkmapEditor may store a local recovery draft when there are unsaved changes. A recovery draft helps prevent accidental loss, but it does not replace saving the physical Markdown file. 588: 589: ## 📓 Journal mode 590: 591: Journal mode adds a local workspace around Markdown. 592: 593: Use Journal mode to: 594: 595: - capture daily notes; 596: - maintain persistent concept pages; 597: - connect pages with Wiki Links; 598: - review Tasks; 599: - browse Tags and related pages; 600: - manage Projects; 601: - generate Reports. 602: 603: Start with: 604: 605: 1. Switch to **Journal**. 606: 2. Select **Open Workspace**. 607: 3. Choose a local workspace folder. 608: 4. Select **Today** to open or create today's journal. 609: 5. Use **New Concept** for a persistent knowledge page. 610: 611: Contextual **?** buttons provide detailed guidance for Reports, Projects, Tasks, and Related pages. 612: 613: ## 📊 Slides mode 614: 615: Slides mode helps prepare presentation-oriented Markdown for an external Pandoc workflow. 616: 617: Use Slides mode to: 618: 619: - structure slides in Markdown; 620: - add speaker notes; 621: - create columns and presentation layouts; 622: - export Slides Markdown; 623: - convert the exported source with Pandoc and a PowerPoint reference template. 624: 625: Slides mode keeps presentation content editable as Markdown. 626: 627: ## 🎨 Adjust the workspace 628: 629: Use the toolbar and pane controls to: 630: 631: - show or hide the Editor; 632: - show or hide the Markmap; 633: - open HTML Preview; 634: - resize panes; 635: - use fullscreen or focused views; 636: - change Markmap appearance; 637: - switch between light and dark themes; 638: - export supported outputs. 639: 640: Most controls stay close to the pane or feature they affect. 641: 642: ## 🧭 Where should I go next? 643: 644: If you want to write a normal Markdown file: 645: 646: > Continue editing this document or select **Open**. 647: 648: If you want journals, concepts, Tasks, links, Projects, and Reports: 649: 650: > Switch to **Journal** and open a workspace. 651: 652: If you want presentation source: 653: 654: > Switch to **Slides**. 655: 656: If you want to understand a feature: 657: 658: > Select **?** in the toolbar or the contextual **?** beside that feature. 659: 660: If you want to see what changed: 661: 662: > Select **✨ Release Notes**. 663: 664: ## ✅ Your turn 665: 666: Try one of these: 667: 668: - rename this document;
